01Chapter 1 · Machine Learning for Computer Vision

Machine Learning for Computer Vision

Computer vision ka matlab hai computer ko ye sikhana ki woh tasveeron ko dekh kar samajh sake — bilkul waise hi jaise hum apni aankhon se dekh kar samajhte hain. Jab tum baag me baithe hue ek chidiya ko keeda khate hue dekhte ho, to tumhari aankhein sirf tasveer nahi banati, tumhara dimaag us tasveer ka matlab bhi nikalta hai. Computer vision isi kaam ko machine se karwana chahta hai.

Human vision se inspiration

Insaan ki vision me do system kaam karte hain — aankhein jo scene ko capture karti hain, aur dimaag jo us scene ko samajhta hai. Computer vision bhi isi tarah do hisson me banta hai: image formation, matlab camera aur sensor se tasveer banana, aur machine perception, matlab us tasveer se information nikalna. Is book me focus dusre hisse par hai — machine learning se tasveeron se information nikalna.

Jab hum ek phool ki tasveer dekhte hain, to hum turant pehchan lete hain ki ye guldaudi hai ya gulab. Machine learning model bhi yahi kaam karta hai — use bahut saari labelled tasveerein dikhai jati hain, aur woh seekh jata hai ki nayi tasveer me kaunsa phool hai. Ye kaam image classification kehlata hai, aur ye is book ka pehla aur sabse basic kaam hai.

Images kyun special hain?

Tasveerein aam data se alag hoti hain. Ek tasveer me lakhon pixels hote hain, aur paas wale pixels aapas me bahut zyada connected hote hain — ek phool ki pankhudi ke pixels ek saath mil kar ek shape banate hain, aur shapes mil kar phool ka hissa banate hain. Isi liye tasveeron ke liye aam machine learning tareeke kaafi nahi hote, aur khaas tareeke chahiye hote hain jinhe hum aage ke chapters me dekhenge.

Expert system se machine learning tak

2010 se pehle computer vision zyada tar expert system wale tareeke se hota tha — matlab pehle ek expert se poochha jata tha ki woh phool ko kaise pehchanta hai, phir us logic ko haath se filters aur rules me likha jata tha. Ye tareeka bahut mehnat wala tha aur har naye kaam ke liye naye rules banane padte the. Machine learning me hum rules nahi likhte, hum model ko bahut saara data dikhate hain aur woh khud patterns seekh leta hai.

2012 me ek bahut bada badlav aaya jab ek convolutional network ne ek bade image classification competition me sabko peeche chhod diya. Us model ki galti sirf 15.3% thi, jabki dusre number par aane wale ki galti 26% se zyada thi. Aam taur par aise competition me sudhaar 0.1% ke aas-paas hota hai, to ye sudhaar lagbhag sau guna zyada tha. Uske baad se deep learning hi computer vision ka standard tareeka ban gaya.

Yaad rakho: Computer vision ka goal insaan ki vision ki nakal karna hai — sensor se tasveer lena, aur machine learning se us tasveer ka matlab nikalna. Rules likhne ke bajay data se seekhna hi modern computer vision ki pehchan hai.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Machine Learning for Computer Vision
← PreviousHome→ Next01.1 · Machine Learning kya hai?
01.1Chapter 1 · Machine Learning for Computer Vision

Machine Learning kya hai?

Machine learning artificial intelligence ka ek hissa hai jisme computer ko bahut saara data dikha kar sikhaya jata hai, bajay iske ki har kaam ke liye haath se rules likhe jayein. Computer vision me ye tareeka is liye kaam karta hai kyunki tasveeron ke patterns ko rules me likhna lagbhag namumkin hai, lekin examples se seekhna bahut asaan hai.

AI, ML aur expert system me farak

Artificial intelligence ka matlab hai computer se insaani kaabiliyat wale kaam karwana. Iske do bade tareeke hain — expert system aur machine learning. Expert system me hum insaan ke logic ko program me likhte hain, jaise agar phool ki pankhudiyan safed hon aur beech peela ho to ye guldaudi hai. Machine learning me hum computer ko hazaron labelled examples dikhate hain aur woh khud seekh leta hai ki kaunsi cheez kis category me aati hai.

Supervised learning

Supervised learning me har training example ke saath sahi jawab bhi diya jata hai, jise label kehte hain. Jaise guldaudi ki tasveer ke saath label "guldaudi" aur gulab ki tasveer ke saath label "gulab". Model in examples se seekhta hai aur phir nayi tasveer par apni prediction deta hai. Image classification, object detection aur segmentation — is book ke zyada tar kaam supervised learning hi hain.

Unsupervised aur self-supervised learning

Unsupervised learning me labels nahi hote — model ko sirf data diya jata hai aur woh khud usme patterns ya groups dhoondhta hai, jaise similar tasveeron ko ek saath rakhna. Self-supervised learning me label data se hi banaya jata hai, jaise tasveer ka ek hissa chhupa kar model se woh hissa predict karwana. Is book me focus supervised learning par hai, lekin aage ke chapters me self-supervised tareeke bhi aayenge.

Images ke liye ML kyun?

Tasveeron me patterns bahut complex hote hain — ek hi phool alag lighting, alag angle aur alag zoom me bilkul alag dikh sakta hai. Haath se rules likh kar har possibility cover karna namumkin hai. Machine learning model hazaron examples dekh kar woh variations khud seekh leta hai, aur isi liye woh rules wale system se bahut behtar kaam karta hai.

Ek achha ML problem kaisa hota hai?

  • Data se define ho sake: Problem ko examples aur labels ke roop me likha ja sake — jaise tasveer do, label lo.
  • Kaafi data ho: Model ko seekhne ke liye sau, hazaar ya lakh examples chahiye hote hain, jitna zyada utna behtar.
  • Clear success metric ho: Pata ho ki model achha hai ya nahi — jaise accuracy, ya precision aur recall.
  • Rules se mushkil ho: Agar kaam simple rules se ho jata hai, to ML ki zaroorat hi nahi hai.
Yaad rakho: Machine learning ka matlab hai data se seekhna, rules likhna nahi. Jahan labels mil sakte hain aur kaafi data hai, wahan supervised learning sabse seedha aur mazboot tareeka hai.

01.2Chapter 1 · Machine Learning for Computer Vision

Deep Learning Use Cases

Deep learning machine learning ka woh hissa hai jisme bahut saari layers wale neural network use hote hain. 2012 ke baad se deep learning ne computer vision ko poori tarah badal diya hai, aur aaj ye sirf tasveeron tak limited nahi hai — video, audio aur text par bhi yahi tareeka kaam karta hai.

Deep learning kaise kaam karta hai?

Deep learning me model ko bahut saari labelled tasveerein dikhai jati hain — sau, hazaar ya lakhon me. Model pehle simple cheezein seekhta hai jaise kinare aur rang, phir unse shapes banata hai, aur phir shapes se poori cheez pehchan leta hai. Iske liye koi haath se banaya hua filter nahi chahiye — model khud seekhta hai ki kis feature par dhyaan dena hai.

Optical character recognition (OCR)

OCR ka matlab hai scanned tasveer se text nikalna. Rules wale tareeke me har letter ke har font aur har size ko match karna padta tha, jo bahut mushkil tha — kitabein flat nahi rakhi ja sakti, is liye letters tedhe-medhe bhi hote the. Deep learning me OCR ek image classification problem ban jata hai: scanned page dikhao, aur pehle se digitized text ko label banao. Model khud seekh leta hai ki alag fonts me letters kaise dikhte hain.

Industry me use cases

  • Healthcare: X-ray aur MRI se bimari pehchanna, aankh ki bimari dhoondhna, aur mammogram se cancer ke shuruwaati signs pakadna.
  • Retail: QR code padhna, khali shelf pehchanna, aur sabzi ya phal ki quality check karna.
  • Agriculture: Satellite tasveeron se fasal ka andaza lagana, patton ki bimari pehchanna, aur kharab irrigation pump dhoondhna.
  • Manufacturing: Factory floor par quality control aur visual inspection — kharab part ko turant alag karna.
  • Automotive safety: Aage wali gaadi se safe distance rakhna, road sign se speed limit padhna, aur self-parking ya self-driving me madad karna.
  • Government aur security: Satellite images ki monitoring, smart city, aur customs inspection.
  • Insurance: Accident ke baad gaadi ke damage ka automatic assessment.
  • Surveillance: Wildlife camera monitor karna aur intruder detection.

Kab deep learning use karein?

Deep learning tab sabse zyada fayda deta hai jab problem ko data se define kiya ja sake aur kaafi labelled data available ho. Agar data bahut kam hai, to aage ke chapters me bataye gaye tareeke — jaise transfer learning — kaam aate hain, jisme pehle se trained model ka knowledge naye kaam me use hota hai.

Yaad rakho: Deep learning ka asli fayda ye hai ki tumhe har kaam ke liye bespoke filter nahi banana padta. Ek hi approach — labelled data se seekhna — OCR se lekar medical diagnosis tak har jagah kaam karta hai.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Machine Learning for Computer Vision

02Chapter 2 · ML Models for Vision

ML Models for Vision

Is chapter me hum apna pehla machine learning model banayenge — ek aisa model jo tasveer dekh kar bataye ki usme kaunsa phool hai. Ye kaam machine perception kehlata hai, matlab machine ko woh samajhna jo insaan aankh se samajhta hai. Yahan hum Keras API se kaam karenge, jo TensorFlow ka high-level tareeka hai model banane ka.

Machine perception kya hai?

Machine perception ka matlab hai machine ko environment ko samajhna sikhana. Jab kaam aankh se juda ho, to use computer vision kehte hain. Is chapter ka problem image classification hai — tasveer do, model bataye ki usme guldaudi hai, gulab hai, surajmukhi hai, ya koi aur phool. Ye simple lagta hai, lekin isme woh saare basic concepts aate hain jo poori book me kaam aayenge.

5-Flowers dataset

Poori book me ek hi example problem use hoti hai — lagbhag chaar hazaar phoolon ki tasveerein, jinme paanch types hain: guldaudi, dandelion, gulab, surajmukhi aur tulip. Har tasveer ka label pehle se diya hua hai. Ye dataset public domain me hai aur aasani se mil jata hai, is liye seekhne ke liye bahut achha hai. Lekin ye yaad rakho ki ye dataset seekhne ke liye achha hai, apna dataset banane ka template nahi — asli project me lakhon images aur behtar storage format chahiye hota hai.

Is chapter me kya seekhenge?

  • Image data ko kaise padha jata hai — JPEG ko numbers me badalna aur resize karna.
  • Tensor kya hota hai aur data ko visualize kyun karna zaroori hai.
  • Keras me linear model kaise banate hain aur use kaise train karte hain.
  • Neural network kya hota hai aur hidden layer se kya badalta hai.
  • Overfitting, learning rate, regularization, dropout aur batch normalization jaise basic training concepts.

Linear aur dense network ki limit

Is chapter ke models pixels ko independent inputs ki tarah treat karte hain — unhe ye nahi pata hota ki paas wale pixels mil kar shape banate hain. Isi liye in models ki accuracy zyada nahi hoti, lagbhag 0.40 se 0.48 ke beech. Lekin in models se jo tools aur concepts seekhenge — data pipeline, training loop, loss aur metrics — wohi tools aage ke chapters ke powerful models me bhi kaam aayenge. Agle chapter me hum tasveeron ki khaas structure ka fayda uthayenge.

Yaad rakho: Pehla model perfect nahi hota — linear model ki accuracy sirf 0.40 ke aas-paas hoti hai, jabki random guess 0.20 hota hai. Is chapter ka goal accuracy nahi, balki poora training pipeline seekhna hai.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — ML Models for Vision
← Previous01.2 · Deep Learning Use Cases→ Next02.1 · Dataset for Machine Perception
02.1Chapter 2 · ML Models for Vision

Dataset for Machine Perception

Koi bhi machine learning project data se shuru hota hai. Is chapter me hum 5-Flowers dataset ko example bana kar seekhenge ki image data ko kaise padha jata hai, kaise visualize kiya jata hai, aur training aur evaluation ke liye dataset ko kaise alag kiya jata hai.

5-Flowers dataset kaisa hai?

Is dataset me lagbhag chaar hazaar JPEG tasveerein hain, paanch categories me — guldaudi, dandelion, gulab, surajmukhi aur tulip. Ye tasveerein real-world conditions me li gayi hain: kuch close-up hain, kuch poora khet dikhati hain, kuch me rang alag hai. Insaan ke liye inhe label karna bahut asaan hai, lekin simple rules se inhe alag karna mushkil hai — jaise agar tum kaho ki tulip lamba phool hota hai, to sirf kuch tasveerein hi us rule me fit hongi.

Image collection ko standardize karna

Real project me tum aksar problem ko asaan bana sakte ho — jaise factory me lighting aur camera angle fix kar dena, ya object ko sirf ek hi orientation me rakhna. Ye cheating nahi hai, ye smart kaam hai. Lekin ek baat ka dhyaan rakho: training data waisa hi hona chahiye jaisa real me model ko milega. Agar model sirf professional photographer ki tasveeron par train hua hai, to woh aam aadmi ki tasveeron par kharab perform karega.

Image data padhne ke chaar steps

JPEG ya PNG tasveer ko model ke liye taiyar karne me chaar steps hote hain. Pehle file ko memory me bytes ki tarah padha jata hai. Dusre, un bytes ko decode kar ke pixel data banaya jata hai — JPEG me pixels ko lookup table se decode karna padta hai, is liye teen colour channels (red, green, blue) liye jate hain. Teesre, pixel values jo 0 se 255 ke beech hoti hain, unhe float me badal kar 0 se 1 ke beech scale kiya jata hai, kyunki optimizer chhote numbers par behtar kaam karta hai. Chauthe, tasveer ko fix size me resize kiya jata hai, kyunki model ko pata hona chahiye ki input kis size ka hoga.

Tensor kya hota hai?

Tensor ek aisa array hai jiske kitne bhi dimensions ho sakte hain — 1D array ko vector kehte hain, 2D ko matrix, aur usse zyada dimensions wale ko tensor. Ek tasveer aam taur par 3D tensor hoti hai: height, width aur channels. TensorFlow me tensor ka fayda ye hai ki us par calculations GPU par chal sakte hain, jabki aam Python array sirf CPU par chalte hain. Isi liye image pipeline me TensorFlow operations use karna zyada fast hota hai.

Data visualize karna kyun zaroori hai?

Training se pehle hamesha kuch tasveerein dekh lo — aksar data galat tareeke se padha jata hai aur tasveerein ulti ya mirrored ho jati hain. Visualize karne se ye galti turant pakdi jati hai, aur ye bhi samajh aata hai ki problem kitni mushkil hai. Is dataset me filename me hi phool ka naam hota hai, is liye wildcard matching se ek category ki saari tasveerein aasani se mil jati hain.

Dataset file padhna

Ek-ek tasveer padhne ke bajay, training aur evaluation ke liye pehle se bani hui CSV files use hoti hain — har line me ek filename aur uska label hota hai. Training set aur evaluation set pehle se alag kiye hue hain, taaki model ki jaanch unseen data par ho sake. Data ko ek-ek karke padhne ke liye tf.data API use hoti hai, jo bade dataset ko bhi memory me poora load kiye bina, thoda-thoda kar ke padh sakti hai. Har element me do cheezein hoti hain — tasveer aur uska label.

Yaad rakho: Model banane se pehle data ko dekhna aur samajhna sabse zaroori step hai. Galat padha hua data ya training jaisa na dikhne wala evaluation data poore project ko barbaad kar sakta hai.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — ML Models for Vision

02.2Chapter 2 · ML Models for Vision

A Linear Model Using Keras

Linear model machine learning ka sabse simple model hai — ye har pixel ko ek weight deta hai, saare weighted pixels ko jodta hai, aur us total se decide karta hai ki tasveer me kaunsa phool hai. Ye model zyada accurate nahi hota, lekin isse Keras, loss, optimizer aur training ke saare basic concepts ekdum saaf ho jate hain.

Linear model kaise kaam karta hai?

Model paanch outputs banata hai, har phool category ke liye ek. Har output saare pixels ka weighted average hota hai — matlab har pixel ka ek weight hota hai, aur output un sabka jod hota hai, usme ek bias bhi add hota hai. Bias is liye chahiye taaki agar saare pixels kaale hon, tab bhi output zero na ho. Aakhir me jis category ka output sabse bada hota hai, wahi model ki prediction hoti hai. Is model me lagbhag saat lakh se zyada weights train karne hote hain.

Keras me model banana

Keras TensorFlow ka high-level API hai. Isme model layers ka ek sequence hota hai — pehle Flatten layer 3D tasveer ko 1D list me badal deti hai, phir Dense layer har output ko har input se jodti hai, matlab koi weight share nahi hota. Model banane ke baad use compile karna padta hai — optimizer, loss function aur metrics batane padte hain. Yahan optimizer Adam use hota hai, loss SparseCategoricalCrossentropy hota hai, aur metric accuracy hoti hai.

Logits, probability, sigmoid aur softmax

Model ka raw output logits kehlata hai — ye koi bhi number ho sakta hai, minus infinity se plus infinity tak. Inhe probability me badalne ke liye activation function lagta hai. Binary problem me sigmoid use hota hai, jo ek number ko 0 se 1 ke beech le aata hai. Multiclass problem me softmax use hota hai, jo saare outputs ko probabilities me badal deta hai jinka total 1 hota hai. Softmax chhoti values ko daba deta hai aur sabse badi value ko boost karta hai. Agar last layer me hi softmax activation laga do, to model seedha probabilities dega.

Gradient descent aur training loss

Training ka matlab hai weights ko aise adjust karna ki loss kam se kam ho jaye. Classification me loss ke liye cross-entropy use hoti hai — agar model sahi label ko probability 1 deta hai to loss zero hoti hai, aur agar sahi label ko probability zero deta hai to loss infinite ho jati hai. Gradient descent me har step par dekha jata hai ki loss kis direction me sabse tezi se kam ho rahi hai, aur weights ko us direction me thoda sa move kiya jata hai. Ye thoda sa step learning rate se decide hota hai. Ek saath poora dataset nahi, chhote batches me training hoti hai — batch ka gradient zyada stable hota hai aur GPU par fast chalta hai.

Labels ke do tareeke

Label ko do tareekon se represent kiya ja sakta hai — sparse aur one-hot. Sparse me label sirf ek number hota hai, jaise tulip ke liye 4, jo jagah bachata hai. One-hot me label ek vector hota hai, jaise guldaudi ke liye [1, 0, 0, 0, 0]. Sparse zyada efficient hai, lekin agar ek tasveer me do phool hon to one-hot hi kaam aata hai — jaise [1, 0, 0, 0, 1] ka matlab hai tasveer me guldaudi aur tulip dono hain.

Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall

Accuracy ka matlab hai kitni predictions sahi hain, lekin jab ek class bahut rare ho to accuracy dhokha de sakti hai — jaise agar 1000 me se sirf 10 fake card hon, to sabko genuine bol kar bhi 99% accuracy mil jayegi. Is liye precision aur recall bhi dekhe jate hain. Precision batata hai ki jitne ko positive bola, unme se kitne asal me positive the. Recall batata hai ki jitne asal positive the, unme se kitne pakde gaye. F1 score in dono ka harmonic mean hota hai.

Training aur overfitting

Model ko train karne ke liye model.fit use hota hai, jisme training dataset aur validation dataset dono diye jate hain, aur epochs bataye jate hain — ek epoch ka matlab hai poora dataset ek baar dekhna. Is model ki evaluation accuracy lagbhag 0.40 aati hai, jo random guess 0.20 se behtar hai. Lekin training aage badhne par validation loss kam hone ke bajay badhne lagti hai — ye overfitting hai, matlab model training data ko yaad karne laga hai, general rule seekhna band kar diya hai.

Yaad rakho: Linear model me har pixel ka alag weight hota hai aur pixels ke beech ka relation ignore hota hai — isi liye ye tasveeron par zyada achha nahi kar pata. Lekin loss, optimizer, softmax aur metrics jaise concepts yahi se seekhe jate hain.

  # Resize the image to the desired size.

  print(label, avg)

class Centroid:
  def __init__(self, label):
    self.label = label
    self.sum_so_far = tf.constant(0., dtype=tf.float32)
    self.count_so_far = 0
  
  def update(self, value):
    self.sum_so_far = self.sum_so_far + value
    self.count_so_far = self.count_so_far + 1
    if self.count_so_far%100 == 0:
      print(self.label, self.count_so_far)

  def centroid(self):
    return self.sum_so_far / self.count_so_far

  def __str__(self):
    return '{} {}'.format(self.label, self.centroid().numpy())


class CentroidRule:
  def __init__(self):
    self.centroids = {
        f: Centroid(f) for f in CLASS_NAMES}

  def fit(self, dataset):
    for img, label in dataset:
      label = label.numpy().decode("utf-8")
      avg = tf.reduce_mean(img, axis=[0, 1]) # average pixel in the image
      self.centroids[label].update(avg)
  
  def predict(self, img):
    avg = tf.reduce_mean(img, axis=[0, 1]) # average pixel in the image
    best_label = ""
    best_diff = 999
    for key, val in self.centroids.items():
      diff = tf.reduce_sum(tf.abs(avg - val.centroid()))
      if diff < best_diff:
        best_diff = best_diff
        best_label = key
    return best_label
  
  def evaluate(self, dataset):
    num_correct, total_images = 0, 0
    for img, label in dataset:
      correct = label.numpy().decode('utf-8')
      predicted = self.predict(img)
      if correct == predicted:
        num_correct = num_correct + 1
      total_images = total_images + 1
    accuracy = num_correct / total_images
    return(accuracy)

rule = CentroidRule()

← Previous02.1 · Dataset for Machine Perception→ Next02.3 · A Neural Network Using Keras
02.3Chapter 2 · ML Models for Vision

A Neural Network Using Keras

Linear model ki sabse badi kami ye hai ki woh sirf seedha weighted sum kar sakta hai — complex patterns nahi seekh sakta. Neural network me input aur output ke beech ek ya zyada hidden layers add ki jati hain, aur har hidden layer ke baad ek nonlinear activation lagti hai. Bas ye ek badlav model ko bahut zyada powerful bana deta hai.

Hidden layer kyun chahiye?

Agar tum sirf Dense layers ko ek ke baad ek laga do bina kisi activation ke, to poora model phir bhi linear hi rahega — weights ko aapas me multiply kar ke ek hi layer bana sakte ho. Asli taakat nonlinear activation se aati hai. Jab hidden layer ke output par ReLU jaisi activation lagti hai, to model complex, tedhe-medhe relations seekh sakta hai. ReLU ka matlab hai — negative value ko zero kar do, positive ko waisa hi rehne do. Ye simple hai, fast hai, aur isi liye hidden layers me sabse zyada use hota hai.

Activation functions

Sigmoid brain ke neuron jaisa behave karta hai, lekin uska gradient extremes par bahut chhota ho jata hai, is liye training slow ho jati hai. ReLU me gradient active hisse me constant rehta hai, is liye training fast hoti hai — lekin iski ek kami hai, dead ReLU problem: agar neuron ka output zero ho gaya, to uska weight kabhi update nahi hota. Iska solution ELU ya Leaky ReLU hai, jisme negative side par ek chhoti value rehti hai.

Learning rate

Learning rate woh step size hai jisse weights har iteration me update hote hain. Agar learning rate bahut zyada ho, to optimizer minima ke upar se jump kar jayega aur kabhi settle nahi hoga. Agar bahut kam ho, to training bahut slow hogi aur model local minima me atak sakta hai. Adam optimizer ka default learning rate 0.001 hota hai, aur use 0.0001 karne par curves zyada smooth ho jati hain. Ye ek hyperparameter hai — iski sahi value experiment se milti hai.

Regularization aur overfitting

Jab model me parameters zyada aur data kam ho, to model training data ko ratne lagta hai — ise overfitting kehte hain. Regularization me loss me weights par penalty add kar di jati hai, taaki optimizer bade weights ko pasand na kare. L1 regularization bahut se weights ko zero kar deti hai, is liye compact model banta hai. L2 regularization saare weights ko chhota rakhti hai aur overfitting ko zyada se zyada rokne me madad karti hai.

Early stopping aur hyperparameter tuning

Training ke dauraan validation accuracy ek point ke baad girne lagti hai, jabki training accuracy badhti rehti hai — yahi woh point hai jahan training rok deni chahiye. Early stopping callback yahi kaam karta hai: agar validation accuracy kuch epochs tak na badhe, to training ruk jati hai. Lekin ye tabhi lagao jab curves smooth hon. Hyperparameters — jaise learning rate, hidden nodes ki sankhya aur regularization ki matra — ko tune karne ke liye Keras Tuner use hota hai, jo alag-alag combinations try kar ke sabse achha wala dhoondhta hai.

Deep neural network, dropout aur batch normalization

Ek se zyada hidden layers wale network ko deep neural network kehte hain. Is chapter me do hidden layers wala model banaya gaya, lekin chhote dataset par uski accuracy pehle se behtar nahi hui — kyunki parameters bahut zyada ho gaye. Dropout me training ke har step par randomly kuch neurons ko band kar diya jata hai, taaki network kisi ek neuron par depend na kare. Batch normalization me har layer ke outputs ko normalize kiya jata hai, taaki agle layer ko hamesha sahi range ke numbers milein. In dono tricks se accuracy 0.40 se badh kar 0.48 ho gayi — lekin phir bhi ye dense network tasveeron ke liye sahi tareeka nahi hai, kyunki ye pixels ke beech ki spatial structure ko ignore karta hai.

Yaad rakho: Hidden layer + nonlinear activation hi neural network ki jaan hai. Learning rate, regularization, early stopping, dropout aur batch normalization — ye paanch tools har model ki training me kaam aate hain, chahe model kitna bhi bada kyun na ho.

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
IMG_HEIGHT = 224

IMG_CHANNELS = 3

def read_and_decode(filename, reshape_dims):
  # Read the file
  img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
  # Convert the compressed string to a 3D uint8 tensor.
  img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
  # Use `convert_image_dtype` to convert to floats in the [0,1] range.
  img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
  # Resize the image to the desired size.
  return tf.image.resize(img, reshape_dims)

CLASS_NAMES = [item.numpy().decode("utf-8") for item in 
               tf.strings.regex_replace(
                 tf.io.gfile.glob("gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/*"),
                 "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/", "")]
CLASS_NAMES = [item for item in CLASS_NAMES if item.find(".") == -1]
print("These are the available classes:", CLASS_NAMES)

# the label is the index into CLASS_NAMES array
def decode_csv(csv_row):
  record_defaults = ["path", "flower"]
  filename, label_string = tf.io.decode_csv(csv_row, record_defaults)
  img = read_and_decode(filename, [IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH])
  label = tf.argmax(tf.math.equal(CLASS_NAMES, label_string))
  return img, label

BATCH_SIZE = 32

train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).batch(BATCH_SIZE)

eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).batch(BATCH_SIZE)

# NN with one hidden layer
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
          tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)),
          tf.keras.layers.Dense(128, activation=tf.keras.activations.relu),
          tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), activation='softmax')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam',
              loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=False),
              metrics=['accuracy'])

# parameterize to the values in the previous cell
def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.001, # default in Adam constructor
                       l1 = 0,
                       l2 = 0,
                       num_hidden = 128):
  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)

  train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(batch_size)

  eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(32) # this doesn't matter

  # NN with one hidden layers
  model = tf.keras.Sequential([
              tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_hidden,
                                    kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                                    activation=tf.keras.activations.relu),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                                    kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                                    activation='softmax')
  ])
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=False),
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
    
  history = model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset, epochs=10)
  training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
  return model

import kerastuner as kt

# parameterize to the values in the previous cell
def build_model(hp):
  lrate = hp.Float('lrate', 1e-4, 1e-1, sampling='log')
  l1 = 0
  l2 = hp.Choice('l2', values=[0.0, 1e-1, 1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4])
  num_hidden = hp.Int('num_hidden', 32, 256, 32)

  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)

  # NN with one hidden layers
  model = tf.keras.Sequential([
              tf.keras.layers.Flatten(input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_hidden,
                                    kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                                    activation=tf.keras.activations.relu),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                                    kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                                    activation='softmax')
  ])
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=False),
                  metrics=['accuracy'])
  return model

batch_size = 32
train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).batch(batch_size)

eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).batch(32) # this doesn't matter

tuner = kt.BayesianOptimization(
    build_model,
    objective=kt.Objective('val_accuracy', 'max'), 
    max_trials=10,
    num_initial_points=2, 
    overwrite=False) # True to start afresh.

tuner.search(
    train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset,
    epochs=5,
    callbacks=[tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(patience=1)]
)

topN = 1
for x in range(topN):
  print(tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(topN)[x].values)
  print(tuner.get_best_models(topN)[x].summary())

def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.0001,
                       l1 = 0,
                       l2 = 0.001,
                       num_hidden = [64, 16]):
  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)

  train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(batch_size)

  eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(32) # this doesn't matter

  # NN with multiple hidden layers
  layers = [tf.keras.layers.Flatten(
      input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
      name='input_pixels')]
  layers = layers + [
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(nodes,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            activation=tf.keras.activations.relu,
                            name='hidden_dense_{}'.format(hno))
          for hno, nodes in enumerate(num_hidden)
  ]
  layers = layers + [
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
  ]

  model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                    from_logits=False),
                metrics=['accuracy'])
  print(model.summary())
  history = model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset, epochs=10)
  training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
  return model

model = train_and_evaluate(lrate=0.0001, l2=0.001, num_hidden = [64, 16])

def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.0001,
                       l1 = 0,
                       l2 = 0.001,
                       dropout_prob = 0.4,
                       num_hidden = [64, 16]):
  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)

  train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(batch_size)

  eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(32) # this doesn't matter

  # NN with multiple hidden layers
  layers = [tf.keras.layers.Flatten(
      input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
      name='input_pixels')]
  for hno, nodes in enumerate(num_hidden):
    layers.extend([
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(nodes,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            name='hidden_dense_{}'.format(hno)),
      tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(scale=False, # ReLU
                                         center=False, # have bias in Dense
                                         name='batchnorm_dense_{}'.format(hno)),
      #move activation to come after batchnorm
      tf.keras.layers.Activation('relu', name='relu_dense_{}'.format(hno)),
      tf.keras.layers.Dropout(rate=dropout_prob,
                             name='dropout_dense_{}'.format(hno)),                         
    ])

  layers.append(
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
  )

  model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                    from_logits=False),
                metrics=['accuracy'])
  print(model.summary())
  history = model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset, epochs=10)
  training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
  return model

model = train_and_evaluate(dropout_prob=0.4)

03Chapter 3 · Image Vision

Image Vision

Chapter 2 ke models pixels ko independent inputs ki tarah treat karte the — unhe ye nahi pata tha ki paas wale pixels mil kar lines aur shapes banate hain. Is chapter me hum woh tareeke dekhenge jo tasveeron ki isi khaas structure ka fayda uthate hain — convolutional networks, pretrained models aur transfer learning.

Images ki structure kyun important hai?

Ek tasveer me paas wale pixels bahut zyada correlated hote hain — woh mil kar kinare banate hain, kinare mil kar shapes banate hain, aur shapes mil kar phool ki pankhudi ya dandi banate hain. Fully connected layer ko ye hierarchy nahi pata hoti, is liye woh har pixel ko alag treat karta hai aur bahut saare weights waste karta hai. Convolutional layer isi hierarchy ko use karta hai, aur isi liye tasveeron par bahut behtar kaam karta hai.

Embedding kya hoti hai?

Jab tasveer network se guzarti hai, to aakhri se pehle wali layer me poori tasveer ki information kuch numbers me compress ho jati hai — ise embedding kehte hain. Ye numbers tasveer ka ek compact representation hote hain. Agar embedding achhi hai, to us par ek chhota sa classifier laga kar nayi categories bhi seekhi ja sakti hain. Yehi idea transfer learning ki neev hai.

Pretrained model

Pretrained model woh model hota hai jo pehle se hi ek bahut bade dataset par train kiya gaya ho — jaise lakhon tasveeron wala dataset jisme sau se zyada categories hon. Aise model ki embedding bahut powerful hoti hai, kyunki usne duniya bhar ki tasveeron se general features seekhe hote hain. Hum us model ka aakhri layer hata kar apna classifier laga sakte hain. Jaise ek popular halka model, jise lakhon tasveeron par train kiya gaya tha, uski embedding ko phoolon ki classification me use kiya ja sakta hai.

Transfer learning

Transfer learning me pretrained model ke weights ko freeze kar diya jata hai — matlab training ke dauraan woh badalte nahi — aur sirf naye classifier layers train hote hain. Iska fayda ye hai ki lakhon parameters train karne ke bajay sirf 20 hazaar parameters train karne padte hain, jo chhote dataset par bhi ho jata hai. Isi tareeke se 5-Flowers dataset par accuracy 0.48 se badh kar 0.90 ho gayi. Rule of thumb ye hai: agar har label ke liye paanch hazaar se kam images hain, to transfer learning hi sabse achha tareeka hai.

Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning me pretrained layers ko bhi thoda-thoda train karne diya jata hai, taaki woh naye dataset ke hisaab se adjust ho jayein. Lekin yahan ek khatra hai — agar learning rate zyada ho, to pretrained weights bigad jate hain aur saara purana knowledge khatam ho jata hai. Is liye fine-tuning me learning rate schedule use hota hai — shuru me learning rate dheere-dheere badhaya jata hai (warm-up), phir dheere-dheere kam kiya jata hai. Differential learning rate me pehle wali layers ko bahut kam learning rate milta hai aur aakhri layers ko zyada. In dono tricks se accuracy 0.90 se badh kar 0.92 ho gayi.

104 Flowers dataset

Is chapter ke aage ke hisse me ek bada dataset use hota hai — 23 hazaar se zyada tasveerein, 104 categories me. Ye dataset imbalanced bhi hai — kuch categories me hazaron images hain, kuch me sau se kam. Is liye yahan accuracy ke bajay precision, recall aur F1 score use hote hain. Bade dataset par hi alag-alag architectures ka sahi comparison ho pata hai.

Yaad rakho: Chhote dataset par scratch se train karna time aur data dono ki barbadi hai. Pehle transfer learning try karo, phir fine-tuning — aur sirf tab scratch se train karo jab har label ke liye paanch hazaar se zyada images hon.

# Helper functions
def training_plot(metrics, history):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
  for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
    ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
    ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
    ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
    ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
    ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])

# Call model.predict() on a few images in the evaluation dataset
def plot_predictions(model, filename):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(25,15))
  dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(filename).
      map(decode_csv))
  for idx, (img, label) in enumerate(dataset.take(15)):
    ax[idx//5, idx%5].imshow((img.numpy()));
    batch_image = tf.reshape(img, [1, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS])
    batch_pred = model.predict(batch_image)
    pred = batch_pred[0]
    label = CLASS_NAMES[label.numpy()]
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(pred).numpy()
    pred_label = CLASS_NAMES[pred_label_index]
    prob = pred[pred_label_index]
    ax[idx//5, idx%5].set_title('{}: {} ({:.4f})'.format(label, pred_label, prob))
    ax[idx//5, idx%5].axis('off')

def show_trained_weights(model):
  # CLASS_NAMES is ['daisy', 'dandelion', 'roses', 'sunflowers', 'tulips']
  LAYER = 1 # Layer 0 flattens the image, layer=1 is the first dense layer
  WEIGHT_TYPE = 0 # 0 for weight, 1 for bias

  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 5, figsize=(15,15))
  for flower in range(len(CLASS_NAMES)):
    weights = model.layers[LAYER].get_weights()[WEIGHT_TYPE][:, flower]
    min_wt = tf.math.reduce_min(weights).numpy()
    max_wt = tf.math.reduce_max(weights).numpy()
    flower_name = CLASS_NAMES[flower]
    print("Scaling weights for {} in {} to {}".format(
        flower_name, min_wt, max_wt))
    weights = (weights - min_wt)/(max_wt - min_wt)
    ax[flower].imshow(weights.reshape(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, 3));
    ax[flower].set_title(flower_name);
    ax[flower].axis('off')

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
IMG_HEIGHT = 224
IMG_WIDTH = 224
IMG_CHANNELS = 3

def read_and_decode(filename, reshape_dims):
  # Read the file
  img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
  # Convert the compressed string to a 3D uint8 tensor.
  img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
  # Use `convert_image_dtype` to convert to floats in the [0,1] range.
  img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
  # Resize the image to the desired size.
  return tf.image.resize(img, reshape_dims)

CLASS_NAMES = ['daisy', 'dandelion', 'roses', 'sunflowers', 'tulips']
print("These are the available classes:", CLASS_NAMES)

# the label is the index into CLASS_NAMES array
def decode_csv(csv_row):
  record_defaults = ["path", "flower"]
  filename, label_string = tf.io.decode_csv(csv_row, record_defaults)
  img = read_and_decode(filename, [IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH])
  label = tf.argmax(tf.math.equal(CLASS_NAMES, label_string))
  return img, label

import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os
# Load compressed models from tensorflow_hub
os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'

# parameterize to the values in the previous cell
def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.001,
                       l1 = 0.,
                       l2 = 0.,
                       num_hidden = 16):
  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)

  train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(batch_size)

  eval_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
      "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
      map(decode_csv)).batch(32) # this doesn't matter

  layers = [
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4",
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_hidden,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            activation='relu',
                            name='dense_hidden'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
  ]

  model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                    from_logits=False),
                metrics=['accuracy'])
  print(model.summary())
  history = model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset, epochs=5)
  training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
  return model

           'hippeastrum ',     'bee balm',                  'pink quill',       'foxglove',      'bougainvillea',     'camellia',             'mallow',                   'mexican petunia',  'bromelia',         'blanket flower',        # 90 - 99
           'trumpet creeper',  'blackberry lily',           'common tulip',     'wild rose']                                                                                                                                               # 100 - 102

def lrfn(epoch):
    if epoch < LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS:
        lr = (LR_MAX - LR_START) / LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS * epoch + LR_START
    elif epoch < LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS + LR_SUSTAIN_EPOCHS:
        lr = LR_MAX
    else:
        lr = (LR_MAX - LR_MIN) * LR_EXP_DECAY**(epoch - LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS - LR_SUSTAIN_EPOCHS) + LR_MIN
    return lr
    
lr_callback = tf.keras.callbacks.LearningRateScheduler(lrfn, verbose=True)

rng = [i for i in range(EPOCHS)]
y = [lrfn(x) for x in rng]
plt.plot(rng, y)
print("Learning rate schedule: {:.3g} to {:.3g} to {:.3g}".format(y[0], max(y), y[-1]))

# numpy and matplotlib defaults
np.set_printoptions(threshold=15, linewidth=80)

def batch_to_numpy_images_and_labels(data):
    images, labels = data
    numpy_images = images.numpy()
    numpy_labels = labels.numpy()
    if numpy_labels.dtype == object: # binary string in this case, these are image ID strings
        numpy_labels = [None for _ in enumerate(numpy_images)]
    # If no labels, only image IDs, return None for labels (this is the case for test data)
    return numpy_images, numpy_labels

def title_from_label_and_target(label, correct_label):
    if correct_label is None:
        return CLASSES[label], True
    correct = (label == correct_label)
    return "{} [{}{}{}]".format(CLASSES[label], 'OK' if correct else 'NO', u"\u2192" if not correct else '',
                                CLASSES[correct_label] if not correct else ''), correct

def display_one_flower(image, title, subplot, red=False, titlesize=16):
    plt.subplot(*subplot)
    plt.axis('off')
    plt.imshow(image)
    if len(title) > 0:
        plt.title(title, fontsize=int(titlesize) if not red else int(titlesize/1.2), color='red' if red else 'black', fontdict={'verticalalignment':'center'}, pad=int(titlesize/1.5))
    return (subplot[0], subplot[1], subplot[2]+1)
    
def display_batch_of_images(databatch, predictions=None):
    """This will work with:
    display_batch_of_images(images)
    display_batch_of_images(images, predictions)
    display_batch_of_images((images, labels))
    display_batch_of_images((images, labels), predictions)
    """
    # data
    images, labels = batch_to_numpy_images_and_labels(databatch)
    if labels is None:
        labels = [None for _ in enumerate(images)]
        
    # auto-squaring: this will drop data that does not fit into square or square-ish rectangle
    rows = int(math.sqrt(len(images)))
    cols = len(images)//rows
        
    # size and spacing
    FIGSIZE = 13.0
    SPACING = 0.1
    subplot=(rows,cols,1)
    if rows < cols:
        plt.figure(figsize=(FIGSIZE,FIGSIZE/cols*rows))
    else:
        plt.figure(figsize=(FIGSIZE/rows*cols,FIGSIZE))
    
    # display
    for i, (image, label) in enumerate(zip(images[:rows*cols], labels[:rows*cols])):
        title = '' if label is None else CLASSES[label]
        correct = True
        if predictions is not None:
            title, correct = title_from_label_and_target(predictions[i], label)
        dynamic_titlesize = FIGSIZE*SPACING/max(rows,cols)*40+3 # magic formula tested to work from 1x1 to 10x10 images
        subplot = display_one_flower(image, title, subplot, not correct, titlesize=dynamic_titlesize)
    
    #layout
    plt.tight_layout()
    if label is None and predictions is None:
        plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=0, hspace=0)
    else:
        plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=SPACING, hspace=SPACING)
    plt.show()

def display_confusion_matrix(cmat, score, precision, recall):
    plt.figure(figsize=(15,15))
    ax = plt.gca()
    ax.matshow(cmat, cmap='Reds')
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(CLASSES)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(CLASSES, fontdict={'fontsize': 7})
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="left", rotation_mode="anchor")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(CLASSES)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(CLASSES, fontdict={'fontsize': 7})
    plt.setp(ax.get_yticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor")
    titlestring = ""
    if score is not None:
        titlestring += 'f1 = {:.3f} '.format(score)
    if precision is not None:
        titlestring += '\nprecision = {:.3f} '.format(precision)
    if recall is not None:
        titlestring += '\nrecall = {:.3f} '.format(recall)
    if len(titlestring) > 0:
        ax.text(101, 1, titlestring, fontdict={'fontsize': 18, 'horizontalalignment':'right', 'verticalalignment':'top', 'color':'#804040'})
    plt.show()
    
def display_training_curves(training, validation, title, subplot):
    if subplot%10==1: # set up the subplots on the first call
        plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10), facecolor='#F0F0F0')
        plt.tight_layout()
    ax = plt.subplot(subplot)
    ax.set_facecolor('#F8F8F8')
    ax.plot(training)
    ax.plot(validation)
    ax.set_title('model '+ title)
    ax.set_ylabel(title)
    #ax.set_ylim(0.28,1.05)
    ax.set_xlabel('epoch')
    ax.legend(['train', 'valid.'])

def decode_image(image_data):
    image = tf.image.decode_jpeg(image_data, channels=3)
    #image = tf.cast(image, tf.float32) / 255.0  # convert image to floats in [0, 1] range
    image = tf.reshape(image, [*IMAGE_SIZE, 3]) # explicit size needed for TPU
    return image

def read_labeled_tfrecord(example):
    LABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
        "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string), # tf.string means bytestring
        "class": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64),  # shape [] means single element
    }
    example = tf.io.parse_single_example(example, LABELED_TFREC_FORMAT)
    image = decode_image(example['image'])
    label = tf.cast(example['class'], tf.int32)
    return image, label # returns a dataset of (image, label) pairs

def read_unlabeled_tfrecord(example):
    UNLABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
        "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string), # tf.string means bytestring
        "id": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string),  # shape [] means single element
        # class is missing, this competitions's challenge is to predict flower classes for the test dataset
    }
    example = tf.io.parse_single_example(example, UNLABELED_TFREC_FORMAT)
    image = decode_image(example['image'])
    idnum = example['id']
    return image, idnum # returns a dataset of image(s)

def load_dataset(filenames, labeled=True, ordered=False):
    # Read from TFRecords. For optimal performance, reading from multiple files at once and
    # disregarding data order. Order does not matter since we will be shuffling the data anyway.

    ignore_order = tf.data.Options()
    if not ordered:
        ignore_order.experimental_deterministic = False # disable order, increase speed

    dataset = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(filenames, num_parallel_reads=AUTO) # automatically interleaves reads from multiple files
    dataset = dataset.with_options(ignore_order) # uses data as soon as it streams in, rather than in its original order
    dataset = dataset.map(read_labeled_tfrecord if labeled else read_unlabeled_tfrecord, num_parallel_calls=AUTO)
    # returns a dataset of (image, label) pairs if labeled=True or (image, id) pairs if labeled=False
    return dataset

def data_augment(image, label):
    # data augmentation. Thanks to the dataset.prefetch(AUTO) statement in the next function (below),
    # this happens essentially for free on TPU. Data pipeline code is executed on the "CPU" part
    # of the TPU while the TPU itself is computing gradients.
    image = tf.image.random_flip_left_right(image)
    #image = tf.image.random_saturation(image, 0, 2)
    return image, label   

def get_training_dataset():
    dataset = load_dataset(TRAINING_FILENAMES, labeled=True)
    dataset = dataset.map(data_augment, num_parallel_calls=AUTO)
    dataset = dataset.repeat() # the training dataset must repeat for several epochs
    dataset = dataset.shuffle(2048)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def get_validation_dataset(ordered=False):
    dataset = load_dataset(VALIDATION_FILENAMES, labeled=True, ordered=ordered)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.cache()
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def get_test_dataset(ordered=False):
    dataset = load_dataset(TEST_FILENAMES, labeled=False, ordered=ordered)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def count_data_items(filenames):
    # the number of data items is written in the name of the .tfrec files, i.e. flowers00-230.tfrec = 230 data items
    n = [int(re.compile(r"-([0-9]*)\.").search(filename).group(1)) for filename in filenames]
    return np.sum(n)

NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES = count_data_items(TRAINING_FILENAMES)
NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES = count_data_items(VALIDATION_FILENAMES)
NUM_TEST_IMAGES = count_data_items(TEST_FILENAMES)
STEPS_PER_EPOCH = NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES // BATCH_SIZE
VALIDATION_STEPS = -(-NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES // BATCH_SIZE) # The "-(-//)" trick rounds up instead of down :-)
print('Dataset: {} training images, {} validation images, {} unlabeled test images'.format(NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES, NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES, NUM_TEST_IMAGES))

# data dump
print("Training data shapes:")
for image, label in get_training_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, label.numpy().shape)
print("Training data label examples:", label.numpy())
print("Validation data shapes:")
for image, label in get_validation_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, label.numpy().shape)
print("Validation data label examples:", label.numpy())
print("Test data shapes:")
for image, idnum in get_test_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, idnum.numpy().shape)
print("Test data IDs:", idnum.numpy().astype('U')) # U=unicode string

# Peek at training data
training_dataset = get_training_dataset()
training_dataset = training_dataset.unbatch().batch(20)
train_batch = iter(training_dataset)

# run this cell again for next set of images
display_batch_of_images(next(train_batch))

def create_model(verbose=False):
    with strategy.scope():
        pretrained_model = tf.keras.applications.Xception(weights='imagenet', include_top=False)
        pretrained_model.trainable = True # fine-tuning

        model = tf.keras.Sequential([
            tf.keras.layers.Lambda(lambda data: tf.keras.applications.xception.preprocess_input(tf.cast(data, tf.float32)), input_shape=[*IMAGE_SIZE, 3]),
            pretrained_model,
            tf.keras.layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
            tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASSES), activation='softmax')
        ])

    model.compile(
        optimizer='adam',
        loss = 'sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
        metrics=['sparse_categorical_accuracy'],
        steps_per_execution=8
    )
    if verbose:
        model.summary()
    return model
        
def train_new_model(verbose=False):
    model = create_model(verbose)
    history = model.fit(get_training_dataset(), steps_per_epoch=STEPS_PER_EPOCH, epochs=EPOCHS,
                    validation_data=get_validation_dataset(), validation_steps=VALIDATION_STEPS,
                    callbacks=[lr_callback])
    return model, history

def display_curves(history):
    display_training_curves(history.history['loss'], history.history['val_loss'], 'loss', 211)
    display_training_curves(history.history['sparse_categorical_accuracy'], history.history['val_sparse_categorical_accuracy'], 'accuracy', 212)
    
def test_model(model):
    cmdataset = get_validation_dataset(ordered=True) # since we are splitting the dataset and iterating separately on images and labels, order matters.
    images_ds = cmdataset.map(lambda image, label: image)
    labels_ds = cmdataset.map(lambda image, label: label).unbatch()
    cm_correct_labels = next(iter(labels_ds.batch(NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES))).numpy() # get everything as one batch
    cm_probabilities = model.predict(images_ds, steps=VALIDATION_STEPS)
    cm_predictions = np.argmax(cm_probabilities, axis=-1)
    
    cmat = confusion_matrix(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)))
    score = f1_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    precision = precision_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    recall = recall_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    cmat = (cmat.T / cmat.sum(axis=1)).T # normalized
    display_confusion_matrix(cmat, score, precision, recall)
    print('f1 score: {:.3f}, precision: {:.3f}, recall: {:.3f}'.format(score, precision, recall))
    return score, precision, recall

model, history = train_new_model(verbose=True)

display_curves(history)

f1score1, precision1, recall1 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score2, precision2, recall2 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score3, precision3, recall3 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score4, precision4, recall4 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score5, precision5, recall5 = test_model(model)

def print_summary(f1scores, precisions, recalls):
    for i, _ in enumerate(f1scores):
        print('BEST => ' if f1scores[i] == max(f1scores) else '        ', end='')
        print('f1 score: {:.3f}, precision: {:.3f}, recall: {:.3f}'.format(f1scores[i], precisions[i], recalls[i]))
    print('Stats:')
    print('        mean: {:.3f}, stdev: {:.3f}, min: {:.3f}, max: {:.3f}'.format(statistics.mean(f1scores), statistics.stdev(f1scores), min(f1scores), max(f1scores)))
        
print_summary([f1score1, f1score2, f1score3, f1score4, f1score5],
              [precision1, precision2, precision3, precision4, precision5],
              [recall1, recall2, recall3, recall4, recall5])

def lrfn(epoch):
    if epoch < LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS:
        lr = (LR_MAX - LR_START) / LR_RAMPUP_EPOCHS * epoch + LR_START

    subplot=(rows,cols,1)
    if rows < cols:
        plt.figure(figsize=(FIGSIZE,FIGSIZE/cols*rows))
    else:
        plt.figure(figsize=(FIGSIZE/rows*cols,FIGSIZE))
    
    # display
    for i, (image, label) in enumerate(zip(images[:rows*cols], labels[:rows*cols])):
        title = '' if label is None else CLASSES[label]
        correct = True
        if predictions is not None:
            title, correct = title_from_label_and_target(predictions[i], label)
        dynamic_titlesize = FIGSIZE*SPACING/max(rows,cols)*40+3 # magic formula tested to work from 1x1 to 10x10 images
        subplot = display_one_flower(image, title, subplot, not correct, titlesize=dynamic_titlesize)
    
    #layout
    plt.tight_layout()
    if label is None and predictions is None:
        plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=0, hspace=0)
    else:
        plt.subplots_adjust(wspace=SPACING, hspace=SPACING)
    plt.show()

def display_confusion_matrix(cmat, score, precision, recall):
    plt.figure(figsize=(15,15))
    ax = plt.gca()
    ax.matshow(cmat, cmap='Reds')
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(CLASSES)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(CLASSES, fontdict={'fontsize': 7})
    plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="left", rotation_mode="anchor")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(CLASSES)))
    ax.set_yticklabels(CLASSES, fontdict={'fontsize': 7})
    plt.setp(ax.get_yticklabels(), rotation=45, ha="right", rotation_mode="anchor")
    titlestring = ""
    if score is not None:
        titlestring += 'f1 = {:.3f} '.format(score)
    if precision is not None:
        titlestring += '\nprecision = {:.3f} '.format(precision)
    if recall is not None:
        titlestring += '\nrecall = {:.3f} '.format(recall)
    if len(titlestring) > 0:
        ax.text(101, 1, titlestring, fontdict={'fontsize': 18, 'horizontalalignment':'right', 'verticalalignment':'top', 'color':'#804040'})
    plt.show()
    
def display_training_curves(training, validation, title, subplot):
    if subplot%10==1: # set up the subplots on the first call
        plt.subplots(figsize=(10,10), facecolor='#F0F0F0')
        plt.tight_layout()
    ax = plt.subplot(subplot)
    ax.set_facecolor('#F8F8F8')
    ax.plot(training)
    ax.plot(validation)
    ax.set_title('model '+ title)
    ax.set_ylabel(title)
    #ax.set_ylim(0.28,1.05)
    ax.set_xlabel('epoch')
    ax.legend(['train', 'valid.'])

def decode_image(image_data):
    image = tf.image.decode_jpeg(image_data, channels=3)
    #image = tf.cast(image, tf.float32) / 255.0  # convert image to floats in [0, 1] range
    image = tf.reshape(image, [*IMAGE_SIZE, 3]) # explicit size needed for TPU
    return image

def read_labeled_tfrecord(example):
    LABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
        "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string), # tf.string means bytestring
        "class": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64),  # shape [] means single element
    }
    example = tf.io.parse_single_example(example, LABELED_TFREC_FORMAT)
    image = decode_image(example['image'])
    label = tf.cast(example['class'], tf.int32)
    return image, label # returns a dataset of (image, label) pairs

def read_unlabeled_tfrecord(example):
    UNLABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
        "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string), # tf.string means bytestring
        "id": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string),  # shape [] means single element
        # class is missing, this competitions's challenge is to predict flower classes for the test dataset
    }
    example = tf.io.parse_single_example(example, UNLABELED_TFREC_FORMAT)
    image = decode_image(example['image'])
    idnum = example['id']
    return image, idnum # returns a dataset of image(s)

def load_dataset(filenames, labeled=True, ordered=False):
    # Read from TFRecords. For optimal performance, reading from multiple files at once and
    # disregarding data order. Order does not matter since we will be shuffling the data anyway.

    ignore_order = tf.data.Options()
    if not ordered:
        ignore_order.experimental_deterministic = False # disable order, increase speed

    dataset = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(filenames, num_parallel_reads=AUTO) # automatically interleaves reads from multiple files
    dataset = dataset.with_options(ignore_order) # uses data as soon as it streams in, rather than in its original order
    dataset = dataset.map(read_labeled_tfrecord if labeled else read_unlabeled_tfrecord, num_parallel_calls=AUTO)
    # returns a dataset of (image, label) pairs if labeled=True or (image, id) pairs if labeled=False
    return dataset

def data_augment(image, label):
    # data augmentation. Thanks to the dataset.prefetch(AUTO) statement in the next function (below),
    # this happens essentially for free on TPU. Data pipeline code is executed on the "CPU" part
    # of the TPU while the TPU itself is computing gradients.
    image = tf.image.random_flip_left_right(image)
    #image = tf.image.random_saturation(image, 0, 2)
    return image, label   

def get_training_dataset():
    dataset = load_dataset(TRAINING_FILENAMES, labeled=True)
    dataset = dataset.map(data_augment, num_parallel_calls=AUTO)
    dataset = dataset.repeat() # the training dataset must repeat for several epochs
    dataset = dataset.shuffle(2048)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def get_validation_dataset(ordered=False):
    dataset = load_dataset(VALIDATION_FILENAMES, labeled=True, ordered=ordered)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.cache()
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def get_test_dataset(ordered=False):
    dataset = load_dataset(TEST_FILENAMES, labeled=False, ordered=ordered)
    dataset = dataset.batch(BATCH_SIZE)
    dataset = dataset.prefetch(AUTO) # prefetch next batch while training (autotune prefetch buffer size)
    return dataset

def count_data_items(filenames):
    # the number of data items is written in the name of the .tfrec files, i.e. flowers00-230.tfrec = 230 data items
    n = [int(re.compile(r"-([0-9]*)\.").search(filename).group(1)) for filename in filenames]
    return np.sum(n)

NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES = count_data_items(TRAINING_FILENAMES)
NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES = count_data_items(VALIDATION_FILENAMES)
NUM_TEST_IMAGES = count_data_items(TEST_FILENAMES)
STEPS_PER_EPOCH = NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES // BATCH_SIZE
VALIDATION_STEPS = -(-NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES // BATCH_SIZE) # The "-(-//)" trick rounds up instead of down :-)
print('Dataset: {} training images, {} validation images, {} unlabeled test images'.format(NUM_TRAINING_IMAGES, NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES, NUM_TEST_IMAGES))

# data dump
print("Training data shapes:")
for image, label in get_training_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, label.numpy().shape)
print("Training data label examples:", label.numpy())
print("Validation data shapes:")
for image, label in get_validation_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, label.numpy().shape)
print("Validation data label examples:", label.numpy())
print("Test data shapes:")
for image, idnum in get_test_dataset().take(3):
    print(image.numpy().shape, idnum.numpy().shape)
print("Test data IDs:", idnum.numpy().astype('U')) # U=unicode string

# Peek at training data
training_dataset = get_training_dataset()
training_dataset = training_dataset.unbatch().batch(20)
train_batch = iter(training_dataset)

# run this cell again for next set of images
display_batch_of_images(next(train_batch))

def create_model(verbose=False):
    with strategy.scope():
        pretrained_model = tf.keras.applications.Xception(weights='imagenet', include_top=False)
        #pretrained_model = efficientnet.tfkeras.EfficientNetB7(weights='imagenet', include_top=False, input_shape=[*IMAGE_SIZE, 3])
        pretrained_model.trainable = True # fine-tuning

        model = tf.keras.Sequential([
            tf.keras.layers.Lambda(lambda data: tf.keras.applications.xception.preprocess_input(tf.cast(data, tf.float32)), input_shape=[*IMAGE_SIZE, 3]),
            pretrained_model,
            tf.keras.layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
            tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASSES), activation='softmax', name='flower_prob')
        ])
        
        mult_by_layer={ 
            'flower_prob': 1.0,
            'block1_': 0.1,
            'block2_': 0.15,
            'block3_': 0.2,
            'block4_': 0.25,
            'block5_': 0.3,
            'block6_': 0.35,
            'block7_': 0.4,
            'block8_': 0.45,
            'block9_': 0.5,
            'block10_': 0.6,
            'block11_': 0.7,
            'block12_': 0.8,
            'block13_': 0.9,
            'block14_': 0.95,
            # these layers do not have stable identifiers in tf.keras.applications.Xception
            'conv2d_': 0.5,
            'batch_normalization_': 0.5
        }

        optimizer = AdamW(model=model, lr_multipliers=mult_by_layer)

    model.compile(
        optimizer=optimizer,
        loss = 'sparse_categorical_crossentropy',
        metrics=['sparse_categorical_accuracy'],
        steps_per_execution=8
    )
    if verbose:
        model.summary()
    return model
        
def train_new_model(verbose=False):
    model = create_model(verbose)
    history = model.fit(get_training_dataset(), steps_per_epoch=STEPS_PER_EPOCH, epochs=EPOCHS,
                    validation_data=get_validation_dataset(), validation_steps=VALIDATION_STEPS,
                    callbacks=[lr_callback])
    return model, history

def display_curves(history):
    display_training_curves(history.history['loss'], history.history['val_loss'], 'loss', 211)
    display_training_curves(history.history['sparse_categorical_accuracy'], history.history['val_sparse_categorical_accuracy'], 'accuracy', 212)
    
def test_model(model):
    cmdataset = get_validation_dataset(ordered=True) # since we are splitting the dataset and iterating separately on images and labels, order matters.
    images_ds = cmdataset.map(lambda image, label: image)
    labels_ds = cmdataset.map(lambda image, label: label).unbatch()
    cm_correct_labels = next(iter(labels_ds.batch(NUM_VALIDATION_IMAGES))).numpy() # get everything as one batch
    cm_probabilities = model.predict(images_ds, steps=VALIDATION_STEPS)
    cm_predictions = np.argmax(cm_probabilities, axis=-1)
    
    cmat = confusion_matrix(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)))
    score = f1_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    precision = precision_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    recall = recall_score(cm_correct_labels, cm_predictions, labels=range(len(CLASSES)), average='macro')
    cmat = (cmat.T / cmat.sum(axis=1)).T # normalized
    display_confusion_matrix(cmat, score, precision, recall)
    print('f1 score: {:.3f}, precision: {:.3f}, recall: {:.3f}'.format(score, precision, recall))
    return score, precision, recall

model, history = train_new_model(verbose=True)

display_curves(history)

f1score1, precision1, recall1 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score2, precision2, recall2 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score3, precision3, recall3 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score4, precision4, recall4 = test_model(model)

model, history = train_new_model()

display_curves(history)

f1score5, precision5, recall5 = test_model(model)

def print_summary(f1scores, precisions, recalls):
    for i, _ in enumerate(f1scores):
        print('BEST => ' if f1scores[i] == max(f1scores) else '        ', end='')
        print('f1 score: {:.3f}, precision: {:.3f}, recall: {:.3f}'.format(f1scores[i], precisions[i], recalls[i]))
    print('Stats:')
    print('        mean: {:.3f}, stdev: {:.3f}, min: {:.3f}, max: {:.3f}'.format(statistics.mean(f1scores), statistics.stdev(f1scores), min(f1scores),max(f1scores)))
        
print_summary([f1score1, f1score2, f1score3, f1score4, f1score5],
              [precision1, precision2, precision3, precision4, precision5],
              [recall1, recall2, recall3, recall4, recall5])
