07Chapter 7 · Training Pipeline

Training Pipeline

Preprocessing ke baad aata hai model training — model training data padhta hai aur apne weights adjust karta hai. Training ka kaafi time data ingest karne me lagta hai, isliye is chapter ka focus hai ingestion ko efficient banana, CPU aur GPU ke beech time slicing ka fayda uthana, aur poore process ko resilient aur reproducible banana.

Data ko efficiently store karna

Pehla principle hai data ko efficiently store karna — input images ko jitna ho sake preprocess karke aise format me store karo jo padhne me tez ho. TFRecords iske liye best hain, kyunki ek batch ki saari images ek hi network connection se padhi ja sakti hain, har file ko 10 se 100 MB ke aas-paas shard kiya ja sakta hai, aur bytes ko bina parse kiye seedha in-memory structure me map kiya ja sakta hai. Preprocessing ko ETL pipeline aur model code ke beech baantna padta hai — ETL me jo preprocessing hoti hai woh sirf ek baar hoti hai, jabki model code me jo hoti hai woh har epoch me repeat hoti hai. Isliye decode aur scaling TFRecord banate waqt kar lo, lekin jo operations model-specific hain ya har epoch me alag hone chahiye, woh training code me rakho. Ek extreme option hai image embeddings ko hi TFRecord me store karna — isse training bahut tez ho jaati hai, kyunki embedding compute karne me sau se zyada layers lagte hain, lekin isse transfer learning ke alawa kuch nahi kar sakte, aur dataset dobara use nahi ho sakta. Isliye TFRecord me kya preprocessing hui hai, use metadata ke roop me document karna achhi practice hai.

Data ko parallel me padhna

Doosra principle hai reading ko parallelize karna — storage devices ki speed aksar bottleneck hoti hai, lekin alag files alag disks ya network connections se padhi ja sakti hain. TFRecordDataset banate waqt num_parallel_reads se interleaved reading karwao, aur map operations par num_parallel_calls se parallelize karo. Measurement me dikhta hai ki parallel map aur interleave se wall-clock time lagbhag 35 percent kam ho jaata hai, chahe CPU time thoda badh jaaye. Ye fayda simple linear model train karne par bhi dikhta hai — lagbhag 25 percent speedup. Performance measure karte waqt dhyaan rakhna ki optimizer aapka calculation optimize karke hata na de — isliye random threshold jaise tareeke se calculation ko meaningful banao, aur dataset ko loop karke dekhna training se halka tareeka hai ingestion code ko test karne ka.

GPU utilization maximize karna

Teesra principle hai GPU utilization maximize karna, kyunki GPU matrix math me CPU se kai guna tez hota hai, aur agar GPU ghante ke hisaab se rent par hai, to uska idle rehna seedha cost badhata hai. Teen cheezein matter karti hain — CPU aur GPU ke beech data transfer me time lagta hai, GPU ko ek baar me zyada data dene se fayda hota hai, aur GPU ki memory limited hoti hai. Isliye CPU ko prefetch karne ka kaam do — agla batch GPU ke train karte waqt hi taiyaar rahe — aur chhote dataset ko cache bhi kar lo. Vectorization me images ko ek-ek karke nahi, batch me bhejo — batch size badhane se epoch tez hota hai, lekin diminishing returns aate hain aur GPU memory ki limit bhi hoti hai. Preprocessing ko Keras layers me rakhna isliye behtar hai kyunki woh poore batch par ek saath chalti hai, jabki tf.data ke map me woh ek-ek image par chalti hai.

Graph me rehna: iteration se matrix math tak

Aakhri principle hai graph me rehna — TensorFlow data ko CPU se GPU par bhejta hai aur saara code graph ke andar chalata hai, isliye data ko graph se bahar nikaalna mehenga padta hai. Pixel-by-pixel iteration, individual pixel read aur write jaise operations graph me nahi ho sakte — unke liye data ko numpy me nikaal kar wapas tensor banana padta hai, jo bahut slow hota hai. Slicing se iteration se bacha ja sakta hai, conditionals ke liye tf.where use karo, aur weighted sum jaise calculations ko matrix multiplication me badal do — isse 10x se bhi zyada speedup milta hai. Batch par kaam karne se aur bhi fayda hota hai — custom Keras layer me poore batch par matrix math lagao. Pure Python code ko kabhi-kabhi tf.py_function se call karna padta hai, lekin woh koi optimization ya acceleration nahi karta, isliye use sirf tab karo jab koi aur tareeka na ho.

Yaad rakho: GPU ko kabhi idle mat rehne do — data pehle se taiyaar rakho, batch me bhejo, aur saara calculation graph ke andar rakho.

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os
# Load compressed models from tensorflow_hub
os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'    

from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE

IMG_HEIGHT = 448 # note *twice* what we used to have
IMG_WIDTH = 448
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

def training_plot(metrics, history):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
  for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
    ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
    ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
    ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
    ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
    ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])
    
class _Preprocessor:    
    def __init__(self):
        # nothing to initialize
        pass
    
    def read_from_tfr(self, proto):
        feature_description = {
            'image': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.float32),
            'shape': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.int64),
            'label': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string, default_value=''),
            'label_int': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64, default_value=0),
        }
        rec = tf.io.parse_single_example(
            proto, feature_description
        )
        shape = tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['shape'])
        img = tf.reshape(tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['image']), shape)
        label_int = rec['label_int']
        return img, label_int
    
    def read_from_jpegfile(self, filename):
        # same code as in 05_create_dataset/jpeg_to_tfrecord.py
        img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        return img
      
    def preprocess(self, img):
        return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

def create_preproc_dataset_plain(pattern):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    trainds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(
        [filename for filename in tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern)],
        compression_type='GZIP'
    ).map(preproc.read_from_tfr).map(
        lambda img, label: (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    )                             
    return trainds

# note: addition of AUTOTUNE to the map() calls
def create_preproc_dataset_parallelmap(pattern):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    def _preproc_img_label(img, label):
        return (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    trainds = (
        tf.data.TFRecordDataset(
            [filename for filename in tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern)],
            compression_type='GZIP'
        )
        .map(preproc.read_from_tfr, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
        .map(_preproc_img_label, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
    )
    return trainds

# note: splits the files into two halves and interleaves datasets
def create_preproc_dataset_interleave(pattern, num_parallel=None):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    files = [filename for filename in tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern)]
    if len(files) > 1:
        print("Interleaving the reading of {} files.".format(len(files)))
        def _create_half_ds(x):
            if x == 0:
                half = files[:(len(files)//2)]
            else:
                half = files[(len(files)//2):]
            return tf.data.TFRecordDataset(half,
                                          compression_type='GZIP')
        trainds = tf.data.Dataset.range(2).interleave(
            _create_half_ds, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
    else:
        trainds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(files,
                                         compression_type='GZIP')
    def _preproc_img_label(img, label):
        return (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    
    trainds = (trainds
               .map(preproc.read_from_tfr, num_parallel_calls=num_parallel)
               .map(_preproc_img_label, num_parallel_calls=num_parallel)
              )
    return trainds

def create_preproc_image(filename):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    img = preproc.read_from_jpegfile(filename)
    return preproc.preprocess(img)

class RandomColorDistortion(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, contrast_range=[0.5, 1.5], 
                 brightness_delta=[-0.2, 0.2], **kwargs):
        super(RandomColorDistortion, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.contrast_range = contrast_range
        self.brightness_delta = brightness_delta
    
    def call(self, images, training=None):
        if not training:
            return images
        
        contrast = np.random.uniform(
            self.contrast_range[0], self.contrast_range[1])
        brightness = np.random.uniform(
            self.brightness_delta[0], self.brightness_delta[1])
        
        images = tf.image.adjust_contrast(images, contrast)
        images = tf.image.adjust_brightness(images, brightness)
        images = tf.clip_by_value(images, 0, 1)
        return images

def loop_through_dataset(ds, nepochs):
    lowest_mean = tf.constant(1.)
    for epoch in range(nepochs):
        thresh = np.random.uniform(0.3, 0.7) # random threshold
        count = 0
        sumsofar = tf.constant(0.)
        for (img, label) in ds:
            # mean of channel values > thresh
            mean = tf.reduce_mean(tf.where(img > thresh, img, 0))
            sumsofar = sumsofar + mean
            count = count + 1
            if count%100 == 0:
                print('.', end='')
        mean = sumsofar/count
        print(mean)
        if mean < lowest_mean:
            lowest_mean = mean
    return lowest_mean

PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-0000[01]-*', 2 # 2 files, 2 epochs
#PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-*', 20 # 16 files, 20 epochs

%%time
ds = create_preproc_dataset_plain(
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
)
loop_through_dataset(ds, NUM_EPOCHS)

%%time
# parallel map
ds = create_preproc_dataset_parallelmap(
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
)
loop_through_dataset(ds, NUM_EPOCHS)

%%time
# with interleave

    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX,
    num_parallel=None
)

%%time
# with interleave and parallel mpas

    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX,
    num_parallel=AUTOTUNE
)
loop_through_dataset(ds, NUM_EPOCHS)

def train_simple_model(ds, nepochs):
    model = tf.keras.Sequential([
        tf.keras.layers.Flatten(
            input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)),
        #tf.keras.layers.Dense(32, activation='relu'),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), activation='softmax')
    ])
    model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(),
                loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                    from_logits=False),
                metrics=['accuracy'])
    model.fit(ds, epochs=nepochs)

%%time

).batch(1)

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf

def read_jpeg(filename):
    img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
    img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=3)
    img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
    img = tf.reshape(img, [338, 600, 3])
    return img

ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').map(read_jpeg)
f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15,10))
for idx, img in enumerate(ds):
    ax[idx].imshow( img.numpy() );

def to_grayscale(img):
    red = img[:, :, 0]
    green = img[:, :, 1]
    blue = img[:, :, 2]
    c_linear = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue
    gray = tf.where(c_linear > 0.0031308,
                    1.055 * tf.pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055,
                    12.92*c_linear)
    print(gray.shape)
    return gray

ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').map(read_jpeg).map(to_grayscale)
f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15,10))
for idx, img in enumerate(ds):
    im = ax[idx].imshow( img.numpy() , interpolation='none');
    if idx == 1:
        f.colorbar(im, fraction=0.028, pad=0.04)

# This function is not accelerated. At all.
def to_grayscale(img):
    rows, cols, _ = img.shape
    result = np.zeros([rows, cols], dtype=np.float32)
    for row in range(rows):
        for col in range(cols):
            red = img[row][col][0]
            green = img[row][col][1]
            blue = img[row][col][2]
            c_linear = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue
            if c_linear > 0.0031308:
                result[row][col] = 1.055 * pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055
            else:
                result[row][col] = 12.92*c_linear
    return result

%%time
ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').repeat(10).map(read_jpeg)

overall = tf.constant([0.], dtype=tf.float32)
count = 0
for img in ds:
    # Notice that we have to call .numpy() to move the data outside TF Graph
    gray = to_grayscale(img.numpy())
    # This moves the data back into the graph
    m = tf.reduce_mean(gray, axis=[0, 1])
    overall += m
    count += 1
print(overall/count)

def to_grayscale_numpy(img):
    # the numpy happens here
    img = img.numpy()
    rows, cols, _ = img.shape
    result = np.zeros([rows, cols], dtype=np.float32)
    for row in range(rows):
        for col in range(cols):
            red = img[row][col][0]
            green = img[row][col][1]
            blue = img[row][col][2]
            c_linear = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue
            if c_linear > 0.0031308:
                result[row][col] = 1.055 * pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055
            else:
                result[row][col] = 12.92*c_linear
    # the convert back happens here
    return tf.convert_to_tensor(result)

def to_grayscale(img):
    return tf.py_function(to_grayscale_numpy, [img], tf.float32)

%%time
ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').repeat(10).map(read_jpeg).map(to_grayscale)

overall = tf.constant([0.], dtype=tf.float32)
count = 0
for gray in ds:
    m = tf.reduce_mean(gray, axis=[0, 1])
    overall += m
    count += 1
print(overall/count)

# All in GPU
def to_grayscale(img):
    # TensorFlow slicing functionality
    red = img[:, :, 0]
    green = img[:, :, 1]
    blue = img[:, :, 2]
    # All these are actually tf.mul(), tf.add(), etc.
    c_linear = 0.2126 * red + 0.7152 * green + 0.0722 * blue
    # Use tf.cond and tf.where for if-then statements
    gray = tf.where(c_linear > 0.0031308,
                    1.055 * tf.pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055,
                    12.92*c_linear)
    return gray

%%time
ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').repeat(10).map(read_jpeg).map(to_grayscale)

overall = tf.constant([0.])
count = 0
for gray in ds:
    m = tf.reduce_mean(gray, axis=[0, 1])
    overall += m
    count += 1
print(overall/count)

def to_grayscale(img):
    wt = tf.constant([[0.2126], [0.7152], [0.0722]]) # 3x1 matrix
    c_linear = tf.matmul(img, wt) # (ht,wd,3) x (3x1) -> (ht, wd)
    gray = tf.where(c_linear > 0.0031308,
                    1.055 * tf.pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055,
                    12.92*c_linear)
    return gray

%%time
ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').repeat(10).map(read_jpeg).map(to_grayscale)

overall = tf.constant([0.])
count = 0
for gray in ds:
    m = tf.reduce_mean(gray, axis=[0, 1])
    overall += m
    count += 1
print(overall/count)

class Grayscale(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super(Grayscale, self).__init__(kwargs)
    
    def call(self, img):
        wt = tf.constant([[0.2126], [0.7152], [0.0722]]) # 3x1 matrix
        c_linear = tf.matmul(img, wt) # (N, ht,wd,3) x (3x1) -> (N, ht, wd)
        gray = tf.where(c_linear > 0.0031308,
                        1.055 * tf.pow(c_linear, 1/2.4) - 0.055,
                        12.92*c_linear)
        return gray # (N, ht, wd)

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    Grayscale(input_shape=(336, 600, 3)),
    tf.keras.layers.Lambda(lambda gray: tf.reduce_mean(gray, axis=[1, 2])) # note axis change
])

%%time
ds = tf.data.TextLineDataset('input.txt').repeat(10).map(read_jpeg).batch(5)
overall = tf.constant([0.])
count = 0
for batch in ds:
    bm = model(batch)
    overall += tf.reduce_sum(bm)
    count += len(bm)
print(overall/count)

← Previous06.3 · Data Augmentation→ Next07.1 · Saving Model State
07.1Chapter 7 · Training Pipeline

Saving Model State

Model train karke turant predictions karna unrealistic hai — asal me trained model ko save karke rakhna hota hai, taaki baad me usse predictions bhi ki ja sakein aur training bhi resume ki ja sake. Dono kaam ke liye model ko save karna alag hota hai, aur ye farak samajhna bahut zaroori hai.

Export aur checkpointing me farak

Model save karne ke do reasons hain — inference ke liye aur training resume karne ke liye. Inference ke liye model save karna exporting kehlata hai, aur training resume karne ke liye save karna checkpointing kehlata hai. Checkpoints exports se bahut bade hote hain, kyunki unme model ki structure aur weights ke saath-saath bahut saara internal state bhi hota hai. Jaise RandomColorDistortion jaise augmentation layer ko inference ke liye poori tarah hataaya ja sakta hai, lekin training resume karne ke liye uska poora state chahiye hota hai, kyunki training aage badhne par distortion ki amount bhi badal sakti hai. Isi tarah, agar ek mahine baad nayi images aati hain, to purane model ko thode steps ke liye fine-tune karna, scratch se train karne se bahut behtar hota hai — aur iske liye checkpoint chahiye hota hai.

Model export karna

Keras model ko export karne ke liye save method use hota hai, jo SavedModel format me export karta hai — output directory me saved_model.pb naam ki protobuf file, variable weights aur prediction ke liye chahiye assets jaise vocabulary files hote hain. SavedModel ka ek alternative hai ONNX, jo framework-agnostic format hai aur jisme TensorFlow model ko convert kiya ja sakta hai. Export kiye gaye model ko saved_model_cli tool se inspect kiya ja sakta hai — ye batata hai ki prediction signature kya hai, inputs kis shape ke hain aur outputs kya hain. Signature ka matlab hai function ka naam, uske parameters aur return values — TensorFlow me type hints ke saath tensor ki shape bhi specify karni hoti hai, taaki serving system ko pata ho ki kya expect karna hai.

Usable signature banana

Seedha exported model ko invoke karna client ke liye mushkil hota hai — client ko tensor reshape karna, argmax nikaalna aur internal details jaanna padta hai. Isse behtar hai ek usable signature banana — client sirf JPEG filenames bheje, aur model wapas probability, predicted class ka index aur class ka naam de. Aisa function tf.function se banaya jaata hai, jisme input signature filenames ki list hoti hai. Filenames ko iterate karne ki jagah tf.map_fn use karo taaki data graph ke andar hi rahe, phir model ko call karo, phir reduce_max aur argmax se top probability aur uska index nikaalo, aur class naam ke liye tf.gather use karo kyunki Python wali indexing graph me kaam nahi karti. Is signature ko serving_default ke roop me save kar do — ek model me kai signatures bhi ho sakte hain, jaise versioning ya alag clients ke liye. Iske baad client ka code bahut simple ho jaata hai — model load karo, signatures se serving_default lo, filenames bhejo, aur dictionary me se flower type padh lo.

Checkpointing aur early stopping

Checkpointing sirf training ke end me nahi, beech-beech me bhi ki jaati hai, do reasons se. Pehla, training loss to kam hota rehta hai, lekin ek point ke baad validation loss badhne lagta hai kyunki overfitting shuru ho jaata hai — isliye woh checkpoint chahiye hota hai jahan validation accuracy sabse zyada thi. Doosra, production datasets par training ghanton ya dinon tak chalti hai, aur machine crash hone ka risk hota hai — isliye periodic backups se training ko beech se resume kiya ja sakta hai. Keras me checkpointing callbacks se hoti hai — ModelCheckpoint callback validation accuracy monitor karta hai aur sirf best model ko save karta hai. EarlyStopping callback bhi saath me lagaya ja sakta hai — agar validation accuracy do consecutive epochs tak improve na ho, to training ruk jaati hai. Last checkpoint se shuru karne ke liye load_weights call karna hota hai, aur poori fault resilience ke liye BackupAndRestore callback bhi available hai.

Yaad rakho: Export inference ke liye hai, checkpoint training resume karne ke liye — dono ko confuse mat karo, aur hamesha best validation wala checkpoint save karo.

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os
# Load compressed models from tensorflow_hub
os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'    

from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE

IMG_HEIGHT = 448 # note *twice* what we used to have
IMG_WIDTH = 448
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

def training_plot(metrics, history):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
  for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
    ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
    ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
    ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
    ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
    ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])
    
class _Preprocessor:    
    def __init__(self):
        # nothing to initialize
        pass
    
    def read_from_tfr(self, proto):
        feature_description = {
            'image': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.float32),
            'shape': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.int64),
            'label': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string, default_value=''),
            'label_int': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64, default_value=0),
        }
        rec = tf.io.parse_single_example(
            proto, feature_description
        )
        shape = tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['shape'])
        img = tf.reshape(tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['image']), shape)
        label_int = rec['label_int']
        return img, label_int
    
    def read_from_jpegfile(self, filename):
        # same code as in 05_create_dataset/jpeg_to_tfrecord.py
        img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        return img
      
    def preprocess(self, img):
        return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

# most efficient way to read the data
# as determined in 07a_ingest.ipynb
# splits the files into two halves and interleaves datasets
def create_preproc_dataset(pattern):
    """
    Does interleaving, parallel calls, prefetch, batching
    Caching is not a good idea on large datasets.
    """
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    files = [filename for filename in tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern)]
    if len(files) > 1:
        print("Interleaving the reading of {} files.".format(len(files)))
        def _create_half_ds(x):
            if x == 0:
                half = files[:(len(files)//2)]
            else:
                half = files[(len(files)//2):]
            return tf.data.TFRecordDataset(half,
                                          compression_type='GZIP')
        trainds = tf.data.Dataset.range(2).interleave(
            _create_half_ds, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
    else:
        trainds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(files,
                                         compression_type='GZIP')
    def _preproc_img_label(img, label):
        return (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    
    trainds = (trainds
               .map(preproc.read_from_tfr, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .map(_preproc_img_label, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .shuffle(200)
               .prefetch(AUTOTUNE)
              )
    return trainds

def create_preproc_image(filename):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    img = preproc.read_from_jpegfile(filename)
    return preproc.preprocess(img)

class RandomColorDistortion(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, contrast_range=[0.5, 1.5], 
                 brightness_delta=[-0.2, 0.2], **kwargs):
        super(RandomColorDistortion, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.contrast_range = contrast_range
        self.brightness_delta = brightness_delta
    
    def call(self, images, training=None):
        if not training:
            return images
        
        contrast = np.random.uniform(
            self.contrast_range[0], self.contrast_range[1])
        brightness = np.random.uniform(
            self.brightness_delta[0], self.brightness_delta[1])
        
        images = tf.image.adjust_contrast(images, contrast)
        images = tf.image.adjust_brightness(images, brightness)
        images = tf.clip_by_value(images, 0, 1)
        return images

#PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-0000[01]-*', 3 # small
PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-*', 20 # full

import os, shutil
shutil.rmtree('chkpts', ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir('chkpts')

def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.001,
                       l1 = 0.,
                       l2 = 0.,
                       num_hidden = 16):
    regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)
    
    train_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
    ).batch(batch_size)
    eval_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/valid' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
    ).batch(batch_size)

    layers = [
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomCrop(
          height=IMG_HEIGHT//2, width=IMG_WIDTH//2,
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          name='random/center_crop'
      ),
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomFlip(
          mode='horizontal',
          name='random_lr_flip/none'
      ),
      RandomColorDistortion(name='random_contrast_brightness/none'),
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4", 
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_hidden,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            activation=tf.keras.activations.relu,
                            name='dense_hidden'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
    ]

    # checkpoint and early stopping callbacks
    model_checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath='./chkpts',
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        save_best_only=True)
    early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        patience=2)
    
    # model training
    model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')
    model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                      from_logits=False),
                  metrics=['accuracy']
                 )
    print(model.summary())
    history = model.fit(train_dataset, 
                        validation_data=eval_dataset,
                        epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
                        callbacks=[model_checkpoint_cb, early_stopping_cb]
                       )
    training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
    return model

model = train_and_evaluate()

    input_images = tf.map_fn(
        create_preproc_image,
        filenames,

07.2Chapter 7 · Training Pipeline

Distribution Strategy

Data ingestion ko parallelize karne ke baad bhi model code ek hi processor par chal raha hota hai. Model training ko multiple GPUs, multiple machines ya TPUs par distribute karne ke liye distribution strategy chahiye hoti hai — ye batati hai ki model ke weights aur data ko workers ke beech kaise baanta jaaye.

Strategy kaise choose karein

Image ML models deep hote hain aur unka input data dense hota hai, isliye inke liye teen strategies main hain. MirroredStrategy model ki copies har available GPU par banata hai — har weight har replica par mirror hota hai aur har batch ke end me identical updates se sync rehta hai. Ye single machine ke liye use karo, chahe ek GPU ho ya kai — isse doosra GPU lagane par code badalna nahi padta. MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy isi idea ko multiple machines par spread karta hai, aur workers ke beech communication ke liye ek config variable set karna padta hai. TPUStrategy training ko TPU par chalata hai — ye machine learning ke liye specially designed chips hain, jinme custom matrix multiplication unit, high-speed networking aur badi shared memory hoti hai. Teeno hi data parallelism ke forms hain — har batch workers me baant diya jaata hai aur phir all-reduce operation se gradients combine kiye jaate hain. Recommendation ye hai ki pehle ek machine par zyada se zyada GPUs use karo, phir multiple workers par jaao — TPU aam taur par GPUs se zyada cost-effective hote hain, khaas taur par bade batch sizes par.

MirroredStrategy aur batch size

MirroredStrategy banana simple hai — strategy banao aur model ko uske scope ke andar create karo. Saari trainable variables strategy ke scope me hi banani hoti hain, compile method kahin bhi call kar sakte ho, aur ingestion pipeline kahin bhi bana sakte ho kyunki woh hamesha CPU par chalti hai. Do GPUs par epoch ka time lagbhag aadha ho jaata hai — jaise CPU par 100 seconds, single GPU par 55 seconds, aur do GPUs par 29 seconds. Distributed training me batch size badhana zaroori hai, kyunki batch GPUs me baant diya jaata hai — agar ek GPU 32 ka batch sambhal sakta hai, to do GPUs aasani se 64 ka global batch sambhal lenge, har GPU par local batch 32 ka hoga. Debugging aur consistency ke liye kabhi-kabhi bina distribution ke bhi strategy use karni helpful hoti hai.

Multi-worker training: shuffling aur virtual epochs

Multiple machines par synchronous updates wasteful hote hain, kyunki saare workers ko sabse slow worker ka wait karna padta hai. Isliye workers parallel me kaam karte hain aur gradient updates asynchronous tareeke se average kiye jaate hain — late aane wala gradient drop kar diya jaata hai. Aise me batch ko workers me baanta nahi ja sakta, har worker ko poora batch padhna hota hai, aur har worker ke batches me alag examples hone chahiye — isliye shuffling zaroori hai. Files ko bhi shuffle karo aur records ko bhi batching se pehle ek bade buffer me shuffle karo — buffer batch size se kaafi bada hona chahiye, aur agar dataset label ke hisaab se sorted hai, to sirf poora dataset cover karne wala buffer hi kaam karega, warna data ko pehle se hi shuffle kar lo. Virtual epochs ka matlab hai fixed epochs ki jagah fixed number of training examples par train karna — steps per epoch ko total examples ko batch size se divide karke nikaalo, aur model.fit me steps_per_epoch pass karo. Agar examples ki count galat ho, to dataset ko repeat karke infinite bana do, taaki dataset khatm hone se pehle epoch khatm na ho.

Serverless ML aur Python package

Notebooks experimentation ke liye achhe hain, lekin production code ko Python packages me organize karna chahiye — har level par __init__.py file ke saath, reusable modules alag folders me, aur hyperparameters command-line parameters ke roop me. Isse code ko managed training service par submit karna aasan ho jaata hai — package ko cloud storage par daalo, YAML config me machine type, accelerator aur python module specify karo, aur ek command se training job submit kar do. Python package aur container dono options hain — package efficiency aur maintainability deta hai, kyunki service framework-optimized container par install karti hai, jabki container zyada flexible hai, khaas taur par purane runtime ya proprietary software ke liye. Har distribution scenario ke liye alag YAML config hoti hai — single GPU, multiple GPUs, multiple workers ya TPU — aur training code me hardware detect karke sahi strategy banane ka boilerplate bhi likha ja sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Pehle ek machine par GPUs badhao, phir multiple workers par jaao — aur har worker ko alag data mile, iske liye shuffling kabhi mat bhoolo.

import tensorflow as tf
print('TensorFlow version' + tf.version.VERSION)
print('Built with GPU support? ' + ('Yes!' if tf.test.is_built_with_cuda() else 'Noooo!'))
print('There are {} GPUs'.format(len(tf.config.experimental.list_physical_devices("GPU"))))
device_name = tf.test.gpu_device_name()
if device_name != '/device:GPU:0':
  raise SystemError('GPU device not found')
print('Found GPU at: {}'.format(device_name))

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os, shutil
from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE

#PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-0000[01]-*', 3 # small
PATTERN_SUFFIX, NUM_EPOCHS = '-*', 20 # full

IMG_HEIGHT = 448 # note *twice* what we used to have
IMG_WIDTH = 448
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

CHECKPOINT_DIR='./chkpts'
OUTDIR = './export'

def setup_trainer():
    shutil.rmtree(CHECKPOINT_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
    os.mkdir(CHECKPOINT_DIR)
    shutil.rmtree(OUTDIR, ignore_errors=True)
    os.mkdir(OUTDIR)
    # Load compressed models from tensorflow_hub
    os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'    

def create_strategy(mode='gpus_one_machine'):
    """
    mode has be to be one of the following:
    * gpus_one_machine
    * gpus_multiple_machines
    * tpu_colab
    * tpu_caip
    * the actual name of the cloud_tpu
    """
    if mode == 'gpus_one_machine':
        print('Using {} GPUs'.format(len(tf.config.experimental.list_physical_devices("GPU"))))
        return tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy()
    if mode == 'gpus_multiple_machines':
        print("Using TFCONFIG=", os.environ["TF_CONFIG"])
        return tf.distribute.MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy()
    
    # treat as tpu
    if mode == 'tpu_colab':
        tpu_name = 'grpc://' + os.environ['COLAB_TPU_ADDR']
    elif mode == 'tpu_caip':
        tpu_name = None
    else:
        tpu_name = mode
    print("Using TPU: ", tpu_name)
    resolver = tf.distribute.cluster_resolver.TPUClusterResolver(tpu=tpu_name)
    tf.config.experimental_connect_to_cluster(resolver)
    # TPUs wipe out memory, so this has to be at very start of program
    tf.tpu.experimental.initialize_tpu_system(resolver)
    print("All devices: ", tf.config.list_logical_devices('TPU'))
    return tf.distribute.TPUStrategy(resolver)

setup_trainer()
strategy = create_strategy()

def training_plot(metrics, history):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
  for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
    ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
    ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
    ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
    ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
    ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])
    
class _Preprocessor:    
    def __init__(self):
        # nothing to initialize
        pass
    
    def read_from_tfr(self, proto):
        feature_description = {
            'image': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.float32),
            'shape': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.int64),
            'label': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string, default_value=''),
            'label_int': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64, default_value=0),
        }
        rec = tf.io.parse_single_example(
            proto, feature_description
        )
        shape = tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['shape'])
        img = tf.reshape(tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['image']), shape)
        label_int = rec['label_int']
        return img, label_int
    
    def read_from_jpegfile(self, filename):
        # same code as in 05_create_dataset/jpeg_to_tfrecord.py
        img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        return img
      
    def preprocess(self, img):
        return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

# most efficient way to read the data
# as determined in 07a_ingest.ipynb
# splits the files into two halves and interleaves datasets
def create_preproc_dataset(pattern):
    """
    Does interleaving, parallel calls, prefetch, batching
    Caching is not a good idea on large datasets.
    """
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    files = [filename for filename 
             in tf.random.shuffle(tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern))]
    if len(files) > 1:
        print("Interleaving the reading of {} files.".format(len(files)))
        def _create_half_ds(x):
            if x == 0:
                half = files[:(len(files)//2)]
            else:
                half = files[(len(files)//2):]
            return tf.data.TFRecordDataset(half,
                                          compression_type='GZIP')
        trainds = tf.data.Dataset.range(2).interleave(
            _create_half_ds, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
    else:
        trainds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(files,
                                         compression_type='GZIP')
    def _preproc_img_label(img, label):
        return (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    
    trainds = (trainds
               .map(preproc.read_from_tfr, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .map(_preproc_img_label, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .shuffle(200)
               .prefetch(AUTOTUNE)
              )
    return trainds

def create_preproc_image(filename):
    preproc = _Preprocessor()
    img = preproc.read_from_jpegfile(filename)
    return preproc.preprocess(img)

class RandomColorDistortion(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, contrast_range=[0.5, 1.5], 
                 brightness_delta=[-0.2, 0.2], **kwargs):
        super(RandomColorDistortion, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.contrast_range = contrast_range
        self.brightness_delta = brightness_delta
    
    def call(self, images, training=None):
        if not training:
            return images
        
        contrast = np.random.uniform(
            self.contrast_range[0], self.contrast_range[1])
        brightness = np.random.uniform(
            self.brightness_delta[0], self.brightness_delta[1])
        
        images = tf.image.adjust_contrast(images, contrast)
        images = tf.image.adjust_brightness(images, brightness)
        images = tf.clip_by_value(images, 0, 1)
        return images

def create_model(l1, l2, num_hidden):
    regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)
        
    layers = [
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomCrop(
          height=IMG_HEIGHT//2, width=IMG_WIDTH//2,
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          name='random/center_crop'
      ),
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomFlip(
          mode='horizontal',
          name='random_lr_flip/none'
      ),
      RandomColorDistortion(name='random_contrast_brightness/none'),
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4", 
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_hidden,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            activation=tf.keras.activations.relu,
                            name='dense_hidden'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
    ]

    # checkpoint and early stopping callbacks
    model_checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath='./chkpts',
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        save_best_only=True)
    early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        patience=2)
    
    # create model
    return tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')

def train_and_evaluate(strategy,
                       batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.001,
                       l1 = 0.,
                       l2 = 0.,
                       num_hidden = 16):
    
    train_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/train' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
    ).batch(batch_size)
    eval_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr/valid' + PATTERN_SUFFIX
    ).batch(batch_size)

    # checkpoint and early stopping callbacks
    model_checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath='./chkpts',
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        save_best_only=True)
    early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        patience=2)
    
    # model training
    with strategy.scope():
        model = create_model(l1, l2, num_hidden)
    model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                      from_logits=False),
                  metrics=['accuracy']
                 )
    print(model.summary())
    history = model.fit(train_dataset, 
                        validation_data=eval_dataset,
                        epochs=NUM_EPOCHS,
                        callbacks=[model_checkpoint_cb, early_stopping_cb]
                       )
    training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history)
    return model

model = train_and_evaluate(strategy)

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def predict_flower_type(filenames):
    input_images = tf.map_fn(
        create_preproc_image,
        filenames,
        fn_output_signature=tf.float32
    )
    batch_pred = model(input_images) # same as model.predict()
    top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
    pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
    return {
        'probability': top_prob,
        'flower_type_int': pred_label_index,
        'flower_type_str': pred_label
    }

model.save(os.path.join(OUTDIR, 'flowers_model'),
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_flower_type
          })

serving_fn = tf.keras.models.load_model(
    os.path.join(OUTDIR, 'flowers_model')
).signatures['serving_default']
filenames = [
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9818247_e2eac18894.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9853885425_4a82356f1d_m.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/daisy/9158041313_7a6a102f7a_n.jpg',

    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8733586143_3139db6e9e_n.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8713397358_0505cc0176_n.jpg'
]
pred = serving_fn(tf.convert_to_tensor(filenames))
print(pred)
print('******')
print(pred['flower_type_str'].numpy())

f, ax = plt.subplots(1, 6, figsize=(15,15))
for idx, (filename, prob, pred_label) in enumerate(
        zip(filenames, pred['probability'].numpy(), pred['flower_type_str'].numpy())):
    
    img = tf.io.read_file(filename)

← Previous07.1 · Saving Model State→ Next07.3 · Hyperparameter Tuning
07.3Chapter 7 · Training Pipeline

Hyperparameter Tuning

Model banate waqt humne kai arbitrary choices ki hain — hidden nodes ki sankhya, batch size, learning rate, regularization ki amount, crop ratio — aur inke possible combinations bahut zyada hain. In sab ko haath se try karna possible nahi hai, isliye hyperparameter tuning ka use karte hain, jahan ek budget dekar optimization technique ko best settings dhoondhne ko kehte hain.

Managed tuning service kaise kaam karti hai

Chhote model aur dataset ke liye in-built tuner kaam kar sakta hai, lekin realistic datasets ke liye fully managed service behtar hoti hai. Aisi service ko teen cheezein chahiye hoti hain — tune karne wale parameters, unki search space aur budget specify karna; trainer me diye gaye parameter combination ko incorporate karna; aur us combination se model ki performance report karna. Jaise YAML config me likhte hain ki goal accuracy ko maximize karna hai, budget 50 trials ka hai jo 2 parallel chalenge, aur parameters hain L2 regularization 0 se 0.2 ke beech aur batch size 16, 32 ya 64 me se ek. Algorithm unspecified chhodne par Bayesian optimization use hoti hai.

Parameter values ko trainer me use karna

Service trainer ko specific parameter values command-line arguments ke roop me bhejti hai, isliye un sab ko argparse me list karna hota hai. Phir training program me un values ko use karo — jaise batch size se dataset ko batch karo. Yahan ek important baat hai — model me chhupe hue implicit choices ko bhi dhyaan se dekho. Jaise center crop layer me 2 number baked-in tha, lekin asal me fixed cheez sirf woh size hai jo model ko chahiye — isliye crop ratio ko bhi hyperparameter bana do, aur use karke image ki size calculate karo. Har cheez ko configurable banana achhi practice hai — L1 aur L2 regularization ke saath-saath data augmentation layers ko bhi optional bana do.

Accuracy report karna aur results

Training ke baad accuracy ko tuning service ko report karna hota hai — ek helper library se metric tag aur value bhej do. Job submit karne par 50 trials 2 at a time chalte hain, aur Bayesian optimizer har trial ke khatm hone par decide karta hai ki input space ke kis hisse ko aur explore karna hai. Cost infrastructure par depend karti hai — 50 trials ko 10 at a time chalane se job 10 guna tez khatm hogi lekin cost wahi rahegi, aur pehle trials ko pichhle trials ki information ka fayda nahi milega. Isliye recommendation hai — jitne trials budget allow kare utne karo, aur jitne kam parallel trials patience allow kare utne rakho. Ek example me best accuracy 0.89 mili, jisme L2 zero, batch size 64, hidden nodes 24 aur crop ratio lagbhag 0.707 tha. Agar best values search space ke edge par hon, to tuning continue karo — naye values explore karo aur search space ko narrow karo, jaise grid search se batch size, hidden nodes aur crop ratio ke combinations try karo.

Model deploy karna

Tune kiya hua best model deploy karne ke liye pehle ek endpoint banao, phir model upload karo aur us endpoint par deploy karo. Deploy hone ke baad HTTP POST se JSON request bhej kar predictions li ja sakti hain — request me filenames ki list hoti hai aur response me har image ke liye probability, class index aur class naam milta hai. Lekin isme ek kami hai — user ko pehle image ko cloud par upload karna padta hai aur phir uska path bhejna padta hai. Model ko seedha image contents accept karne layak banana ek aage ka improvement hai, jo serving experience ko kaafi behtar bana deta hai.

Yaad rakho: Har implicit choice ko hyperparameter banao, budget ke hisaab se trials rakho, aur agar best value edge par mile to search space badha kar dobara tune karo.

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os, shutil
from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE
os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'

from flowers.utils.augment import *
from flowers.utils.util import cleanup_dir
from flowers.ingest.tfrecords import create_preproc_image

CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()
MODEL_IMG_SIZE = 224 # What mobilenet expects

def create_model(opts, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS):
    regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(opts['l1'] or 0, opts['l2'] or 0)
    
    layers = [
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomCrop(
          height=MODEL_IMG_SIZE, width=MODEL_IMG_SIZE,
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          name='random/center_crop'
      ),
      tf.keras.layers.experimental.preprocessing.RandomFlip(
          mode='horizontal',
          name='random_lr_flip/none'
      )
    ]
    
    if opts['with_color_distort']:
        layers.append(
            RandomColorDistortion(name='random_contrast_brightness/none')
        )
    
    layers += [
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4", 
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(opts['num_hidden'] or 16,
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                            activation=tf.keras.activations.relu,
                            name='dense_hidden'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(len(CLASS_NAMES), 
                            kernel_regularizer=regularizer,
                            activation='softmax',
                            name='flower_prob')
    ]

    # checkpoint and early stopping callbacks
    model_checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath='./chkpts',
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        save_best_only=True)
    early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        patience=2)
    
    # create model
    return tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flower_classification')

def export_model(model, outdir, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS):
    def create_preproc_image_of_right_size(filename):
        return create_preproc_image(filename, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)

    @tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
    def predict_flower_type(filenames):
        input_images = tf.map_fn(
            create_preproc_image_of_right_size,
            filenames,
            fn_output_signature=tf.float32
        )
        batch_pred = model(input_images) # same as model.predict()
        top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
        pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
        pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
        return {
            'probability': top_prob,
            'flower_type_int': pred_label_index,
            'flower_type_str': pred_label
        }
    
    outpath = os.path.join(outdir, 'flowers_model')
    cleanup_dir(outpath)
    model.save(outpath,
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_flower_type
          })

#!/usr/bin/env python
# Copyright 2020 Google Inc. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,

# specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import os, shutil
import argparse
import hypertune
from distutils.util import strtobool
from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE     

from flowers.utils.util import cleanup_dir, create_strategy
from flowers.ingest.tfrecords import *
from flowers.classifier.model import *
from flowers.utils.plots import *
from flowers.classifier.model import MODEL_IMG_SIZE

def train_and_evaluate(strategy, opts):
    # calculate the image dimensions given that we have to center crop
    # to achieve the model image size
    IMG_HEIGHT = IMG_WIDTH = round(MODEL_IMG_SIZE / opts['crop_ratio'])
    print('Will pad input images to {}x{}, then crop them to {}x{}'.format(
        IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, MODEL_IMG_SIZE, MODEL_IMG_SIZE
    ))
    IMG_CHANNELS = 3

    train_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        os.path.join(opts['input_topdir'], 'train' + opts['pattern']),
        IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS
    ).batch(opts['batch_size'])
    eval_dataset = create_preproc_dataset(
        os.path.join(opts['input_topdir'], 'valid' + opts['pattern']),
        IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS
    ).batch(opts['batch_size'])

    # if number of training examples per epoch is specified
    # repeat the training dataset indefinitely
    num_steps_per_epoch = None
    if (opts['num_training_examples'] > 0):
        train_dataset = train_dataset.repeat()
        num_steps_per_epoch = opts['num_training_examples'] // opts['batch_size']
        print("Will train for {} steps".format(num_steps_per_epoch))
    
    # checkpoint and early stopping callbacks
    model_checkpoint_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.ModelCheckpoint(
        filepath=os.path.join(opts['outdir'], 'chkpts'),
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        save_best_only=True)
    early_stopping_cb = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(
        monitor='val_accuracy', mode='max',
        patience=2)
    
    # model training
    with strategy.scope():
        model = create_model(opts, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)
    model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=opts['lrate']),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
                      from_logits=False),
                  metrics=['accuracy']
                 )
    print(model.summary())
    history = model.fit(train_dataset, 
                        validation_data=eval_dataset,
                        epochs=opts['num_epochs'],
                        steps_per_epoch=num_steps_per_epoch,
                        callbacks=[model_checkpoint_cb, early_stopping_cb]
                       )
    training_plot(['loss', 'accuracy'], history, 
                  os.path.join(opts['outdir'], 'training_plot.png'))
    
    # export the model
    export_model(model, 
                 opts['outdir'],
                 IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)
    
    # report hyperparam metric
    hpt = hypertune.HyperTune()
    accuracy = np.max(history.history['val_accuracy']) # highest encountered
    nepochs = len(history.history['val_accuracy'])
    hpt.report_hyperparameter_tuning_metric(
        hyperparameter_metric_tag='accuracy',
        metric_value=accuracy,
        global_step=nepochs)
    print("Reported hparam metric name=accuracy value={}".format(accuracy))
    
    return model


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()

    ## Training parameters
    parser.add_argument(
        '--job-dir', help='Top-level output directory', required=True)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--input_topdir', help='Top-level directory of the TF Records',
        default='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_tfr'
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        '--pattern', help='Files in {input_topdir}/train to read',
        default='-0000[01]-*')
    parser.add_argument(
        '--num_epochs', help='How many times to iterate over training patterns',
        default=3, type=int)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--num_training_examples', 
        help='Number of examples to term as a virtual epoch. If not specified, will use actual number of examples.',
        default=-1, type=int)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--distribute', default='gpus_one_machine',
        help="""
            Has to be one of:
            * cpu
            * gpus_one_machine
            * gpus_multiple_machines
            * tpu_colab
            * tpu_caip
            * the actual name of the cloud_tpu
        """)
    parser.add_argument('--resume', dest='resume', action='store_true',
                       help="Starts from checkpoints in output directory")
    
    ## model parameters
    parser.add_argument(
        '--batch_size', help='Number of records in a batch', default=32, type=int)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--l1', help='L1 regularization', default=0., type=float)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--l2', help='L2 regularization', default=0., type=float)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--lrate', help='Adam learning rate', default=0.001, type=float)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--num_hidden', help='Number of nodes in last but one layer', default=16, type=int)
    parser.add_argument(
        '--crop_ratio', help='Images are center-cropped to this ratio', default=0.5, type=float)
    parser.add_argument('--with_color_distort',
                        type=lambda x: bool(strtobool(x)), nargs='?', const=True, default=True,
                        help="Specify True or False. Default is True.")

    # parse arguments, and set up outdir based on job-dir
    # job-dir is set by CAIP, but outdir is what our code wants.
    args = parser.parse_args()
    opts = args.__dict__
    opts['outdir'] = opts['job_dir']
    print("Job Parameters={}".format(opts))
    
    # able to resume
    if not opts['resume']:
        cleanup_dir(os.path.join(opts['outdir'], 'chkpts'))
    
    # Train, evaluate, export
    strategy = create_strategy(opts['distribute'])  # has to be first/early call in program
    train_and_evaluate(strategy, opts)

#!/usr/bin/env python
# Copyright 2020 Google Inc. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
# software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES
# OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. See the License for the
# specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.data.experimental import AUTOTUNE

class _Preprocessor:    
    def __init__(self, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS):
        self.IMG_HEIGHT = IMG_HEIGHT
        self.IMG_WIDTH = IMG_WIDTH
        self.IMG_CHANNELS = IMG_CHANNELS
    
    def read_from_tfr(self, proto):
        feature_description = {
            'image': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.float32),
            'shape': tf.io.VarLenFeature(tf.int64),
            'label': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string, default_value=''),
            'label_int': tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64, default_value=0),
        }
        rec = tf.io.parse_single_example(
            proto, feature_description
        )
        shape = tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['shape'])
        img = tf.reshape(tf.sparse.to_dense(rec['image']), shape)
        label_int = rec['label_int']
        return img, label_int
    
    def read_from_jpegfile(self, filename):
        # same code as in 05_create_dataset/jpeg_to_tfrecord.py
        img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=self.IMG_CHANNELS)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        return img
      
    def preprocess(self, img):
        return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, self.IMG_HEIGHT, self.IMG_WIDTH)

# most efficient way to read the data
# as determined in 07a_ingest.ipynb
# splits the files into two halves and interleaves datasets
def create_preproc_dataset(pattern, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS):
    """
    Does interleaving, parallel calls, prefetch, batching
    Caching is not a good idea on large datasets.
    """
    preproc = _Preprocessor(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)
    files = [filename for filename 
             in tf.random.shuffle(tf.io.gfile.glob(pattern))]
    
    if len(files) > 1:
        print("Interleaving the reading of {} files.".format(len(files)))
        def _create_half_ds(x):
            if x == 0:
                half = files[:(len(files)//2)]
            else:
                half = files[(len(files)//2):]
            return tf.data.TFRecordDataset(half,
                                          compression_type='GZIP')
        trainds = tf.data.Dataset.range(2).interleave(
            _create_half_ds, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
    else:
        print("WARNING! Only {} files match {}".format(len(files), pattern))
        trainds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(files,
                                          compression_type='GZIP')
    def _preproc_img_label(img, label):
        return (preproc.preprocess(img), label)
    
    trainds = (trainds
               .map(preproc.read_from_tfr, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .map(_preproc_img_label, num_parallel_calls=AUTOTUNE)
               .shuffle(200)
               .prefetch(AUTOTUNE)
              )
    return trainds

def create_preproc_image(filename, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS):
    preproc = _Preprocessor(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS)
    img = preproc.read_from_jpegfile(filename)
    return preproc.preprocess(img)

# specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf

class RandomColorDistortion(tf.keras.layers.Layer):
    def __init__(self, contrast_range=[0.5, 1.5], 
                 brightness_delta=[-0.2, 0.2], **kwargs):
        super(RandomColorDistortion, self).__init__(**kwargs)
        self.contrast_range = contrast_range
        self.brightness_delta = brightness_delta
    
    def call(self, images, training=None):
        if not training:
            return images
        
        contrast = np.random.uniform(
            self.contrast_range[0], self.contrast_range[1])
        brightness = np.random.uniform(
            self.brightness_delta[0], self.brightness_delta[1])
        
        images = tf.image.adjust_contrast(images, contrast)
        images = tf.image.adjust_brightness(images, brightness)
        images = tf.clip_by_value(images, 0, 1)
        return images

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import os, shutil, tempfile, subprocess

def training_plot(metrics, history, filename):
    f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
    for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
        ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
        ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
        ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
        ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
        ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])
    
    on_cloud = filename.startswith('gs://')
    if on_cloud:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            tmpfilename = os.path.join(tmpdir, "out.png")
            plt.savefig(tmpfilename)
            subprocess.check_call('gcloud storage cp {} {}'.format(
                tmpfilename, filename).split())
    else:
        plt.savefig(filename)

#!/usr/bin/env python
# Copyright 2020 Google Inc. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. You may obtain a copy of the License at
# http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0 Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
# software distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES
# OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied. See the License for the
# specific language governing permissions and limitations under the License.

import os, shutil, subprocess
import tensorflow as tf

def cleanup_dir(OUTPUT_DIR):
    on_cloud = OUTPUT_DIR.startswith("gs://")
    if on_cloud:
        try:
            subprocess.check_call("gcloud storage rm --recursive {}".format(OUTPUT_DIR).split())
        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
            pass
    else:
        shutil.rmtree(OUTPUT_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
        os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR)

def create_strategy(mode):
    """
    mode has be to be one of the following:
    * cpu
    * gpus_one_machine
    * gpus_multiple_machines
    * tpu_colab
    * tpu_caip
    * the actual name of the cloud_tpu
    If you are using TPUs, this method has to be the very first thing you do.
    """
    if mode == "cpu":
        print("Using CPU.")
        return tf.distribute.OneDeviceStrategy("/cpu:0")
    elif mode == "gpus_one_machine":
        print("Using {} GPUs".format(len(tf.config.experimental.list_physical_devices("GPU"))))
        return tf.distribute.MirroredStrategy()
    elif mode == "gpus_multiple_machines":
        print("Using TFCONFIG=", os.environ["TF_CONFIG"])
        return tf.distribute.experimental.MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy()
    
    # treat as tpu
    if mode == "tpu_colab":
        tpu_name = "grpc://" + os.environ["COLAB_TPU_ADDR"]
    elif mode == "tpu_caip":
        tpu_name = None
    else:
        tpu_name = mode
        print("Using TPU: ", tpu_name)
    resolver = tf.distribute.cluster_resolver.TPUClusterResolver(tpu=tpu_name)
    tf.config.experimental_connect_to_cluster(resolver)
    # TPUs wipe out memory, so this has to be at very start of program
    tf.tpu.experimental.initialize_tpu_system(resolver)
    print("All devices: ", tf.config.list_logical_devices("TPU"))
    return tf.distribute.TPUStrategy(resolver)

08Chapter 8 · Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

Model train karke deploy kar dena kaafi nahi hai — uske baad bhi uski quality maintain rakhni hoti hai. Model ko akela chhod dena aise hai jaise chhote bachche ko akela chhod dena — uski quality aur performance ko lagatar monitor karna hota hai, khaas taur par jab naye data par retrain karte hain aur data distribution badal sakta hai.

Monitoring kyun zaroori hai

Training ke dauraan aur deployment ke baad, dono waqt monitoring chahiye hoti hai. Training jobs kabhi-kabhi dinon ya hafton tak chalti hain — agar shuru me hi kuch galat ho gaya aur pata training khatm hone par chala, to bahut time aur cost waste ho jaati hai. Isliye training ke dauraan hi loss curves aur metrics par nazar rakhni chahiye, taaki pata chale ki model improve ho raha hai ya ruk gaya hai. Deployment ke baad bhi accuracy jaise quality metrics aur queries per second aur latency jaise performance metrics monitor karne hote hain, kyunki naye data me distribution changes, errors ya aur issues aa sakte hain.

TensorBoard: loss curves aur metrics

TensorBoard ek interactive dashboard hai jo training ke dauraan save kiye gaye summaries ko display karta hai. Isse experiments ka historical record milta hai, alag versions ko compare kiya ja sakta hai, aur training jobs ko analyze kiya ja sakta hai. Loss curves dekh kar pata chalta hai ki training abhi bhi progress kar rahi hai ya ruk gayi hai. Accuracy, precision ya AUC jaise metrics ko bhi display karke filter, smoothing aur outlier removal kiya ja sakta hai, aur zoom in aur out karke detail me dekha ja sakta hai. TensorBoard ko sirf training ke end me dekhna kaafi nahi hai — use training ke dauraan hi check karte rehna chahiye.

Weight histograms se diagnosis

TensorBoard me histograms se weights, gradients aur doosri scalar quantities ko monitor kiya ja sakta hai. Har layer me hazaaron ya lakhon weights hote hain, aur unka distribution training ke shuru aur end me bahut alag hota hai. Shuru me distribution initialization strategy par depend karta hai, lekin jaise-jaise model converge karta hai, central limit theorem ke hisaab se weight distribution Gaussian jaisi dikhni chahiye. Agar weights zero ki taraf skewed hain, to ye dead layers ka sign hai — input values galat scale par hain, isliye input ko 0 se 1 ki jagah -1 se 1 me scale karo ya batch normalization add karo. Agar weights bahut bade ho rahe hain, to ye overfitting ka sign hai — regularization add karo ya dataset bada karo. Gradient issues ke liye gradient clipping, constraints ya penalties use kar sakte ho, aur initialization method badal kar bhi dekh sakte ho.

Device placement, data visualization aur training events

TensorBoard me model graph ko bhi visualize kiya ja sakta hai — structure view batata hai ki kaunse nodes ki structure same hai, aur device view batata hai ki kaunsa node kis device par hai, har device ke liye alag color ke saath. Isse verify hota hai ki model code sahi tareeke se accelerate ho raha hai ya nahi. Images tab se training images ko live dekha ja sakta hai, aur confusion matrix se pata chalta hai ki classifier kis class me sabse zyada galti kar raha hai. TensorBoard callback ko model.fit me add karke log directory, histogram frequency, graph writing aur profiling jaise options set kiye jaate hain — validation data specify karna zaroori hai warna histograms nahi dikhenge. Callback add karne ke baad TensorBoard ko log directory dekar run karo, aur summaries me loss aur metrics ke alawa images aur weight histograms bhi emit kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho: Model ko deploy karke bhool mat jao — TensorBoard se training ke dauraan hi loss, weights aur graph par nazar rakho, taaki problem end me nahi, shuru me hi pakdi jaaye.

08.1Chapter 8 · Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

Model Quality Metrics

Validation loss dekhna model ki performance samajhne ke liye kaafi nahi hai — asli picture ke liye evaluation metrics chahiye hoti hain, jo unseen data par model ki predictions se calculate hoti hain aur use case se judi hoti hain. Alag problems ke liye alag metrics hote hain — classification, regression aur object detection, teeno ke apne metrics hain.

Classification: confusion matrix, accuracy, precision aur recall

Classification me model har class ke liye probability predict karta hai, aur threshold se use 0 ya 1 me convert karte hain — binary classification me default threshold 0.5 hota hai. Confusion matrix chaar cheezein gin-ti hai — true positives, true negatives, false positives aur false negatives. Accuracy sahi predictions ka percentage hai, lekin ye tabhi useful hai jab classes balanced hon. Jaise 1000 patients me sirf 2 ko eye disease hai, to har image ko healthy predict karne wala model bhi 99.8 percent accuracy de dega, lekin woh bilkul bekaar hai. Isliye precision aur recall dekhte hain — precision batata hai ki model ne jitne positive predict kiye, unme se kitne sahi the, aur recall batata hai ki asli positive cases me se kitne model ne dhoondh liye. Dono ka balance F1 score se milta hai, jo precision aur recall ka harmonic mean hai. Agar false positive aur false negative ki cost alag hai, to F-beta score use karte hain, jisme ek parameter se dono ki importance adjust ki ja sakti hai.

ROC aur precision-recall curves, AUC

Threshold choose karna mushkil hai, isliye kai thresholds par metrics calculate karke curves banayi jaati hain. ROC curve me y-axis par true positive rate aur x-axis par false positive rate hota hai, aur precision-recall curve me y-axis par precision aur x-axis par recall hota hai. In curves ke neeche ka area AUC kehlata hai — perfect classifier ka AUC 1 hota hai, random classifier ka 0.5, aur 0.5 se kam ka matlab model random se bhi kharab hai. Classes balanced hon to AUC-ROC use karo, aur imbalanced hon to AUC-PR behtar hai. Threshold ko sirf statistical metric se nahi, business ya use case ki cost se choose karna chahiye — jaise ek patient ko miss karne ki cost versus unnecessary screening ki cost.

Multiclass aur multilabel classification

Multiclass single-label me confusion matrix n x n ki hoti hai, jahan n classes ki sankhya hai, aur true negatives nahi hote kyunki woh doosri classes ke true positives ban jaate hain. Har class ko alag se dekh kar uske liye precision, recall aur F1 nikaale jaate hain, aur phir unka unweighted average macro metric deta hai, jabki saare true positives ko jod kar micro metric milta hai — micro precision, recall aur F1 teeno same hote hain. Class ke sample count se weight karke weighted metrics bhi nikaale ja sakte hain, jo imbalanced classes me useful hote hain. Multilabel me ek image ke kai labels ho sakte hain — yahan exact match ratio sabse strict metric hai, jo sirf woh examples ginta hai jahan saare labels bilkul sahi hon. Hamming score partial credit deta hai — sahi predict kiye labels ka ratio, jabki Hamming loss galat predictions ko measure karta hai aur chhota hona behtar hota hai. Multilabel precision, recall aur F1 bhi predicted aur actual label sets ke intersection se calculate hote hain.

Regression aur object detection metrics

Regression me goal metrics ko minimize karna hota hai. Mean squared error predicted aur actual values ke beech squared error ka mean hai — ye outliers se bahut affect hota hai. Root mean squared error usi ka square root hai, aur mean absolute error absolute difference ka mean hai, jo outliers se kam affect hota hai. Huber loss dono ka best combination hai — chhote errors par squared term aur bade errors par linear term use karta hai, taaki outliers se robustness mile. Object detection me sabse common metric hai intersection over union, ya IoU — predicted aur actual bounding box ke overlap ka area, unke union ke area se divide kiya jaata hai. IoU 1 ho to perfect overlap, 0 ho to koi overlap nahi. IoU par threshold lagakar true positive, false positive aur false negative decide karte hain — threshold aam taur par 50, 75 ya 95 percent hota hai. True negatives object detection me apply nahi hote, kyunki na lagaye gaye boxes ki sankhya bahut badi hoti hai. Precision-recall curve se average precision nikaali jaati hai, aur saari classes ka mean lekar mean average precision, ya mAP, milti hai. Recall-IoU curve se average recall aur mean average recall milti hai. Segmentation ke liye bhi wahi metrics use hote hain, IoU boxes ki jagah masks par calculate hota hai.

Yaad rakho: Accuracy sirf balanced data par bharosemand hai — imbalanced data par precision, recall, F1 aur AUC dekho, aur object detection me IoU aur mAP ko samjho.

08.2Chapter 8 · Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

Sliced Evaluations & Fairness

Validation dataset par calculate kiye gaye aggregate metrics model ki quality ki poori kahani nahi batate — model kuch slices par bahut kharab ho sakta hai, aur ye kami overall number me kho jaati hai. Isliye sliced evaluations zaroori hain, jahan data ko chhote groups me baant kar har group par alag se metrics calculate karte hain.

Sliced evaluations kya hain

Sliced evaluation me data ko classes ya kisi aur characteristic ke basis par slices me baanta jaata hai, aur har slice par wahi evaluation metrics calculate kiye jaate hain jo overall data par kiye the. Phir har slice ka metric overall metric se compare kiya jaata hai — jaise do alag segments ki ROC curve ko overall ROC curve ke saath plot karke dekho. Kuch use cases me kuch segments khaas taur par important hote hain, un par nazar rakhna aur bhi zaroori hai. Ye sirf passive monitoring nahi hai — jab pata chal jaaye ki kis slice par model kharab hai, to data ya model me adjustment karke us slice ko behtar banaya ja sakta hai, jaise us class ke liye data augment karna ya model me complexity badhana.

Fairness monitoring kyun zaroori hai

Image ML models kuch population segments par kharab perform karte hue dekhe gaye hain. Ek study me dikhaya gaya ki commercially available facial analysis programs me darker skin wali mahilaon ki gender pehchanane me error rate, lighter skin wale purushon ke comparison me bahut zyada tha. Aise hi photo preview feature par bhi ek community ke faces ko preference dene ki shikayat aayi, aur ek photo app ne ek couple ki selfie ko galat tareeke se label kar diya tha. Itni capable engineering teams se bhi aisi galtiyan hui hain, isliye agar aapke computer vision problem me human subjects hain, to race aur gender jaise segments par sliced evaluations karke check karna chahiye ki koi problem to nahi hai.

Fairness sirf data problem nahi hai

Kuch segments par kharab performance ko sirf ye ensure karke fix nahi kiya ja sakta ki saari races aur genders training aur evaluation data me present hon — isse gehre problems bhi ho sakte hain. Photographic filters aur processing techniques historically lighter skin tones ko behtar represent karne ke liye optimize kiye gaye the, isliye darker skin par lighting effects ki problem aati hai — iske liye preprocessing aur data augmentation me correction karna padta hai. ML training pehle common cases par focus karta hai aur rare examples par baad me, isliye early stopping, pruning aur quantization jaise techniques minorities ke against bias ko amplify kar sakti hain. Matlab fairness ko address karna sirf data ka kaam nahi hai — poore machine learning pipeline ki examination chahiye hoti hai. Sliced evaluations is diagnosis ke liye invaluable tool hain, aur jin bhi segments ke saath unfair treatment ka risk ho, un sab par ye evaluations karni chahiye.

Yaad rakho: Overall accuracy achhi dikh sakti hai jabki ek group par model bahut kharab ho — isliye har important segment par alag se metric check karo, aur fairness ko poore pipeline ka sawaal samjho.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

08.3Chapter 8 · Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation

Continuous Evaluation

Model ko deploy karke evaluation band kar dena galat hai — models ko lagatar evaluate karte rehna chahiye, taaki jo cheezein galat ho rahi hain, woh jaldi pakdi jaayein. Prediction drift, data distribution me slow shift, ya koi sudden event — ye sab model ke behavior ko badal sakte hain, aur continuous evaluation hi inhe pakadti hai.

Continuous evaluation ke saat steps

Continuous evaluation me saat steps hote hain. Pehla, deployed model ko bheje gaye data ka random sample save karo — jaise saari images ka 1 percent. Doosra, model se predictions to usual tareeke se karwao aur client ko bhejo, lekin sampled images ke liye model ki prediction bhi save kar lo. Teesra, samples ko labeling ke liye bhejo — wahi labeling approach use karo jo training data ke liye use ki thi, jaise labeling service, ya kuch din baad eventual outcome ke basis par label karo. Chauthe, sampled data par evaluation metrics calculate karo, jisme sliced evaluation metrics bhi hon. Paanchve, metrics ka moving average plot karo — jaise pichhle saat dinon ka average loss. Chhathe, averaged metrics me changes dhoondho ya thresholds check karo — jaise kisi monitored segment ki accuracy 95 percent se neeche jaaye, ya is hafte ki accuracy pichhle hafte se 1 percent se zyada kam ho, to alert bhejo. Saatve, sampled aur subsequently labeled data ko training dataset me add karke model ko periodically retrain ya fine-tune karo.

Kab retrain karein aur kaise

Kab retrain karna hai, ye decision lena hota hai. Aam choices hain — jab evaluation metric kisi threshold se neeche jaaye, har X din me retrain karo, ya jab X naye labeled examples mil jaayein. Scratch se train karna hai ya fine-tune karna hai, ye bhi decide karna hota hai. Aam taur par fine-tune karte hain agar naye samples original training data ka chhota sa fraction hon, aur scratch se train karte hain jab sampled data original dataset ke lagbhag 10 percent ke kareeb pahunch jaaye. Ye decision metric ke trend par depend karta hai, guesswork par nahi.

Continuous evaluation kyun matter karti hai

Continuous evaluation ke bina model dheere-dheere kharab hota jaata hai aur pata tab chalta hai jab users shikayat karte hain ya business ko nuksaan ho chuka hota hai. Regular sampling aur labeling se aapko fresh ground truth milta rehta hai, sliced metrics se fairness issues jaldi pakde jaate hain, aur moving averages se slow drift bhi dikhai deta hai jo ek din ke number me nahi dikhega. Alert thresholds pehle se set karke aap reactive ki jagah proactive ho jaate ho — model kharab hone se pehle hi retraining shuru kar dete ho. Isi liye model quality ek baar ka kaam nahi hai, ye ek continuous process hai jo deployment ke baad bhi chalta rehta hai.

Yaad rakho: Deploy ke baad evaluation band mat karo — 1 percent sample karo, label karo, sliced metrics dekho, aur metric girte hi retrain karo.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 8 — Model Quality and Continuous Evaluation
