09Chapter 9 · Model Predictions

Model Predictions

Model train karna sirf aadhi kahani hai — asli kaam tab shuru hota hai jab trained model se prediction lena ho. Chapter 9 me hum dekhenge ki trained model ko kaise export karte hain, usko client program me kaise load karte hain, aur prediction ko fast aur use karne me aasan kaise banate hain.

Model ko export karna

Prediction lene se pehle model ko export karna padta hai. Keras model ko save karne par woh TensorFlow SavedModel format me save hota hai, jisme model ke weights ke saath-saath ek serving signature bhi hoti hai. Serving signature matlab woh function jo input lekar prediction deta hai. By default yeh signature model ki input layer se match karti hai, lekin hum apni khud ki function bhi serving signature ke roop me specify kar sakte hain. Yeh bahut important hai kyunki serving function me hum preprocessing bhi daal sakte hain — jaise image ko resize karna — taaki client ko kisi bhi size ki image bhejne ki freedom mile aur server khud usko model ke hisaab se adjust kar le.

In-memory model se prediction

Sabse seedha tareeka yeh hai ki client program khud SavedModel ko apni memory me load kar le aur serving function ko call kar de. Client filenames ka tensor banata hai, serving function ko deta hai, aur result ke roop me ek dictionary milti hai jisme sabse likely class, uska index aur probability hoti hai. Tensor se normal Python value nikalne ke liye .numpy() use hota hai. Yeh tareeka chhote experiments aur notebooks ke liye theek hai, lekin production me isme do badi problems hain — abstraction aur efficiency.

Abstraction ko behtar banana

ML model banane wale log aur usko app me integrate karne wale developers aksar alag-alag tools aur skills use karte hain. App developer ko TensorFlow ya tensor ki samajh nahi honi chahiye. Lekin in-memory tareeke me client machine par TensorFlow install hona chahiye, client sirf kuch khaas languages me likha ja sakta hai, aur developer ko tensor shapes aur eager execution jaise concepts samajhne padte hain. Iska solution hai model ko HTTP protocol ke through expose karna, aur input-output ko JSON jaise generic format me bhejna. Phir koi bhi language ya platform se prediction li ja sakti hai, bina TensorFlow ke baare me kuch jaane.

Efficiency aur chaar prediction scenarios

In-memory tareeke me client ko badi memory aur accelerator jaise GPU ya TPU chahiye hote hain, kyunki image models kaafi bade hote hain. Performance ki problem chaar situations me dikhti hai. Online prediction me hazaron users ek saath real-time prediction chahte hain, jaise e-commerce site par product photo upload karte hi result mile. Batch prediction me bade dataset par inference karna hota hai — agar ek image me 300 ms lagte hain to 10,000 images me lagbhag ek ghanta lag jayega. Stream prediction me images lagatar aati rehti hain aur system ko stream ke saath pace banaye rakhna hota hai, traffic spike par peeche nahi rehna chahiye. Edge prediction me low-connectivity device par turant result chahiye hota hai, jaise factory ki conveyor belt par defect pehchanana ya phone camera se decision lena — yahan image ko cloud bhejkar wapas laane ka time nahi hota.

Online prediction ka idea

Online prediction ke liye microservices architecture chahiye hoti hai — model inference powerful servers par hoti hai jin par accelerator lage hote hain, aur clients HTTP request bhejkar HTTP response lete hain. Accelerator aur autoscaling se performance problem solve hoti hai, aur HTTP plus JSON se abstraction problem solve hoti hai. Aage ke sections me hum dekhenge ki yeh TensorFlow Serving se kaise hota hai, batch aur stream prediction ke liye distributed pipeline kaise banate hain, aur edge devices par model kaise chalate hain.

Yaad rakho: Training sirf shuruaat hai — prediction ke liye model ko export karo, serving signature me preprocessing daalo, aur client ko HTTP aur JSON jaisa simple interface do taaki TensorFlow ki knowledge ke bina bhi koi prediction le sake.

import apache_beam as beam
from apache_beam.utils.shared import Shared
import tensorflow as tf

class ModelPredict:
    def __init__(self, shared_handle, model_location):
        self._shared_handle = shared_handle
        self._model_location = model_location 

    def __call__(self, filenames):
        def initialize_model():
            print('Loading Keras model from ' + self._model_location)
            return (tf.keras.models.load_model(self._model_location)
                    .signatures['serving_default'])
        
        serving_fn = self._shared_handle.acquire(initialize_model)
        if isinstance(filenames, str):
            # only one element, put it into a batch of 1
            result = serving_fn(tf.convert_to_tensor([filenames]))
        else:
            # a list
            result = serving_fn(tf.convert_to_tensor(filenames))
        return {
            'filenames': filenames,
            'probability': result['probability'].numpy(),
            'pred_label': result['flower_type_str'].numpy()
        }

with beam.Pipeline() as p:
    
    shared_handle = Shared()
    
    (p 
     | 'input' >> beam.Create([
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9818247_e2eac18894.jpg',
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9853885425_4a82356f1d_m.jpg',
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/daisy/9299302012_958c70564c_n.jpg',
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8733586143_3139db6e9e_n.jpg',
        'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8713397358_0505cc0176_n.jpg'
     ]) 
     | 'pred' >> beam.Map(ModelPredict(shared_handle, MODEL_LOCATION))
     | 'write' >> beam.io.textio.WriteToText('/tmp/out.txt', num_shards=1)
    )

import tensorflow as tf
import os, shutil

MODEL_LOCATION='export/flowers_model3'  # will be created

# load from checkpoint and export a model that has desired signature
CHECK_POINT_DIR='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained/chkpts'
model = tf.keras.models.load_model(CHECK_POINT_DIR)

IMG_HEIGHT = 345
IMG_WIDTH = 345
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

def preprocess(filename):
    img_bytes = tf.io.read_file(filename)
    img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
    img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
    return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS], dtype=tf.float32)])
def xai_model(input_images):
    batch_pred = model(input_images) # same as model.predict()
    top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
    pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
    return {
        'probability': top_prob,
        'flower_type_int': pred_label_index,
        'flower_type_str': pred_label
    }

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def xai_preprocess(filenames):
    input_images = tf.map_fn(
        preprocess,
        filenames,
        fn_output_signature=tf.float32
    )
    return {
        # match the signature of xai_model
        'input_images': input_images
    }

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def predict_filename(filenames):
    preproc_output = xai_preprocess(filenames)
    # return xai_model(preproc_output['input_images'])
    return xai_model(**preproc_output)

shutil.rmtree('export', ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir('export')
model.save(MODEL_LOCATION,
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_filename,
              'xai_preprocess': xai_preprocess, # should be exactly what's supplied to model
              'xai_model': xai_model # call the model
          })

#!/bin/bash

MODEL_NAME=flowers_regional
MODEL_LOCATION="gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained" # will change when we call script
VERSION_NAME=ig
EXPLAIN="--explanation-method integrated-gradients --num-integral-steps 25"
REGION='us-central1'  # CHANGE! You need GPU quota in this region
BUCKET='ai-analytics-solutions-kfpdemo' # CHANGE! for staging


while [[ "$#" -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        -v|--version) VERSION_NAME="$2"; shift ;;
        -m|--model_location) MODEL_LOCATION="$2"; shift ;;
        *) echo "Unknown parameter passed: $1"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    shift
done

if [[ "$VERSION_NAME" -eq "xrai" ]]; then
   EXPLAIN="--explanation-method xrai --num-integral-steps 25"
fi

echo "Deploying $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME with $EXPLAIN from $MODEL_LOCATION"

if [[ $(gcloud ai-platform models list --region=$REGION --format='value(name)' | grep $MODEL_NAME) ]]; then
    echo "The model named $MODEL_NAME already exists."
else
    # create model
    echo "Creating $MODEL_NAME model now."
    gcloud ai-platform models create --region=$REGION --enable-logging $MODEL_NAME
fi

if [[ $(gcloud ai-platform versions list --region=$REGION --model $MODEL_NAME --format='value(name)' | grep $VERSION_NAME) ]]; then
    echo "Deleting already the existing model $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME ... "
    gcloud ai-platform versions delete --quiet --region=$REGION --model=$MODEL_NAME $VERSION_NAME
    echo "Please run this script again if you don't see a Creating message ... "
    sleep 2
fi

# create model
echo "Creating $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME $EXPLAIN"
gcloud beta ai-platform versions create --model=$MODEL_NAME $VERSION_NAME --async \
       --region=$REGION  --machine-type n1-standard-4 \
       --framework=tensorflow --python-version=3.7 --runtime-version=2.1 \
       --origin=$MODEL_LOCATION --staging-bucket=gs://$BUCKET $EXPLAIN

import json
import base64
input_images = []
with open('request.json') as ifp:
    instances = json.load(ifp)['instances']
    for instance in instances:
        img_bytes = tf.io.read_file(instance['filenames'])
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=3)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        img = tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)
        input_images.append(img.numpy())
        
explain_images = []
with open('response.json') as ifp:
    explanations = json.load(ifp)['explanations']
    for expln in explanations:
        b64bytes = expln['attributions_by_label'][0]['attributions']['input_images']['b64_jpeg']
        img_bytes = base64.b64decode(b64bytes)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=3)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        explain_images.append(img.numpy())

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import tensorflow as tf

f, ax = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(15,10))
for idx in range(len(input_images)):
    ax[0, idx].imshow(input_images[idx])
    ax[1, idx].imshow(explain_images[idx])
    ax[2, idx].imshow(1-explain_images[idx])
    ax[0, idx].axis('off')
    ax[1, idx].axis('off')
    ax[2, idx].axis('off')

← Previous08.3 · Continuous Evaluation→ Next09.1 · TensorFlow Serving
09.1Chapter 9 · Model Predictions

TensorFlow Serving

Online prediction ke liye recommended tareeka hai model ko TensorFlow Serving ke through ek web microservice ke roop me deploy karna. Client sirf ek HTTP POST request bhejta hai aur JSON me prediction pa leta hai — usko tensor, model architecture ya TensorFlow ke baare me kuch nahi jaanna padta.

Deploy kaise karte hain

TensorFlow Serving sirf software hai, uske liye infrastructure bhi chahiye — user requests ko alag-alag servers par route karna, aur traffic peak par autoscale karna. Isliye managed services jaise Vertex AI, SageMaker ya Azure ML use karna behtar hota hai, kyunki wahan GPU aur custom accelerator bhi milte hain aur infrastructure management ka bojh nahi rehta. Deploy karte time hum machine type, accelerator ka type aur minimum-maximum replica count specify kar sakte hain. Model ko deploy karne ke baad koi bhi machine jo HTTPS call kar sakti hai, woh prediction le sakti hai.

JSON request aur response

Prediction ke liye client ek JSON request bhejta hai jisme instances ki list hoti hai. Har instance ek dictionary hoti hai jiske keys model signature ke inputs se match karte hain — jaise flowers model ke liye har instance me filenames naam ka string field hota hai. Signature ko saved_model_cli tool se dekhkar pata chal sakta hai ki input ka naam, type aur shape kya hai. Response me har instance ke liye predicted class, uska index aur probability milti hai. Kyunki yeh sirf ek REST API hai, isko kisi bhi language se call kiya ja sakta hai jo HTTPS POST bhej sakti ho, authentication token ke saath.

Serving function ko modify karna

Aksar production me woh signature chahiye hoti hai jo export ke time sochi nahi gayi thi. Jaise client chahta hai ki response me filename bhi wapas aaye taaki woh prediction ko input se match kar sake. Iske liye trainer ko wapas jaakar retrain karne ki zaroorat nahi hai — exported model ko load karke ek nayi function define ki ja sakti hai jo purani serving function ko andar se call kare aur result me filename jaisi pass-through value jod de. Phir model ko nayi signature ke saath dobara export kar dete hain. Aise hi sequence number ya koi aur client-specific field bhi pass-through kiya ja sakta hai.

Multiple signatures

Agar alag-alag clients ko alag signature chahiye to ek hi model me multiple signatures rakh sakte hain, lekin sirf ek hi serving default hoti hai. Jaise original signature aur pass-through wali signature dono export kar sakte hain. Jo client non-default signature chahiye, woh request me signature_name field bhejkar usko specifically invoke kar sakta hai, baaki clients ko default wali response milti hai.

Image bytes handle karna

Ab tak hum filename bhej rahe the, jo tab kaam karta hai jab image pehle se cloud par uploaded ho. Lekin agar image client ke paas local hai to pehle usko cloud par upload karna ek extra step ban jata hai. Behtar hai ki client seedha JPEG bytes bhej de. Iske liye ek nayi prediction function banani padti hai jo bytes ko decode kare, wahi preprocessing kare jo training me use hui thi, aur phir model ko call kare. JPEG bytes me aise characters ho sakte hain jo JSON parser ko confuse kar dein, isliye file contents ko base64 encode karke bheja jata hai aur request me b64 naam ka special field use hota hai, jise TensorFlow Serving samajhkar decode kar leta hai. Dono functions — filename wali aur bytes wali — ek saath export ki ja sakti hain taaki client ko choice mile.

Yaad rakho: Serving signature woh contract hai jo client aur model ke beech hota hai — usko retrain kiye bina badla ja sakta hai, multiple signatures ek saath rakh sakte hain, aur image bytes ke liye base64 encoding use hoti hai.

import apache_beam as beam
import json
from oauth2client.client import GoogleCredentials
import requests

class ModelPredict:
    def __init__(self, project, region, endpoint_id):
        self._api = "https://{}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{}/locations/{}/endpoints/{}:predict".format(
            region, project, region, endpoint_id)   
        
    def __call__(self, filenames):        
        token = GoogleCredentials.get_application_default().get_access_token().access_token
        if isinstance(filenames, str):
            # Only one element, put it into a batch of 1.
            data = {
                "instances": [
                    {"filenames": filenames}
                ]
            }
        else:
            data = {
                "instances": []
            }
            for f in filenames:
                data["instances"].append({
                    "filenames" : f
                })
        # print(data)
        headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token }
        response = requests.post(self._api, json=data, headers=headers)
        response = json.loads(response.content.decode("utf-8"))
        # print(response)
        if isinstance(filenames, str):
            result = response["predictions"][0]
            result["filename"] = filenames
            yield result
        else:
            for (a,b) in zip(filenames, response["predictions"]):
                result = b
                result["filename"] = a
                yield result


PROJECT = os.environ['PROJECT']
REGION = os.environ['REGION']
ENDPOINT_ID = os.environ['ENDPOINT_ID']

with beam.Pipeline() as p:    
    (p 
     | "input" >> beam.Create([
        "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9818247_e2eac18894.jpg",
        "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9853885425_4a82356f1d_m.jpg",
        "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/daisy/9299302012_958c70564c_n.jpg",
        "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8733586143_3139db6e9e_n.jpg",
        "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8713397358_0505cc0176_n.jpg"
     ]) 
     | "batch" >> beam.BatchElements(min_batch_size=2, max_batch_size=3)
     | "addpred" >> beam.FlatMap(ModelPredict(PROJECT, REGION, ENDPOINT_ID))
     | "write" >> beam.Map(print)
    )

import os
import shutil
import tensorflow as tf

CHECK_POINT_DIR='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained/chkpts'
model = tf.keras.models.load_model(CHECK_POINT_DIR)
print(model.summary())

IMG_HEIGHT = 345
IMG_WIDTH = 345
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

def read_from_jpegfile(filename):
    img_bytes = tf.io.read_file(filename)
    return img_bytes
    
def preprocess(img_bytes):
    img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
    img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
    return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

filenames = [
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9818247_e2eac18894.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dandelion/9853885425_4a82356f1d_m.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/daisy/9299302012_958c70564c_n.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8733586143_3139db6e9e_n.jpg',
    'gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/tulips/8713397358_0505cc0176_n.jpg'
]
for filename in filenames:
    img_bytes = read_from_jpegfile(filename)
    img = preprocess(img_bytes)
    img = tf.expand_dims(img, axis=0)
    pred = model.predict(img)
    print(pred)

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def predict_bytes(img_bytes):
    input_images = tf.map_fn(
        preprocess,
        img_bytes,
        fn_output_signature=tf.float32
    )
    batch_pred = model(input_images) # same as model.predict()
    top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
    pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
    return {
        'probability': top_prob,
        'flower_type_int': pred_label_index,
        'flower_type_str': pred_label
    }

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def predict_filename(filenames):
    img_bytes = tf.map_fn(
        tf.io.read_file,
        filenames
    )
    result = predict_bytes(img_bytes)
    result['filename'] = filenames
    return result

shutil.rmtree('export', ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir('export')
model.save('export/flowers_model3',
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_filename,
              'from_bytes': predict_bytes
          })

09.2Chapter 9 · Model Predictions

Batch and Stream Prediction

Ek-ek image par prediction karna bade dataset ke liye bahut slow hota hai. Batch aur stream prediction ke liye kaam ko parallel karna padta hai — aur iske liye Apache Beam jaisa distributed processing framework sabse behtar tareeka hai.

Batch prediction kyun parallel honi chahiye

Batch prediction ek embarrassingly parallel problem hai — ek image ki prediction ka doosri image se koi lena-dena nahi hota, isliye dono ek saath chal sakti hain. Lekin ek hi machine par bahut saare GPU threads chalane se memory problem aati hai kyunki har thread ko model ki apni copy chahiye hoti hai. Isliye data processing ko bahut saari machines par distribute karna behtar hota hai. Streaming prediction me bhi yahi zaroorat hoti hai, bas wahan traffic spiky hota hai — isliye infrastructure ko autoscale bhi karna chahiye, peak par machines badhaye aur low traffic par kam karein.

Apache Beam pipeline

Apache Beam me hum ek transform likhte hain jo inference karta hai. Pipeline me filenames ko pehle batch kiya jata hai, kyunki TensorFlow ke graph operations batch me zyada fast hote hain, aur phir model prediction call hoti hai. Ek important detail yeh hai ki model ko har element ke liye dobara load nahi karna chahiye — ideally har worker par model ek baar load ho aur reuse ho. Iske liye Beam ka shared handle use hota hai, jo har worker par ek baar model load karta hai aur worker deactivate-reactivate hone par dobara load kar leta hai. Wahi Beam code batch aur streaming dono ke liye bina badlav ke kaam karta hai, aur isko Cloud Dataflow par scale par chalaya ja sakta hai.

Batch prediction ke liye managed service

Agar model pehle se online prediction ke liye web service ke roop me deploy hai to batch prediction ke liye managed service bhi use kar sakte hain, jaise Vertex AI par batch prediction job chalana. Yeh aasan hota hai kyunki batched requests handle karne ka code khud nahi likhna padta. Performance ke hisaab se kaunsa tareeka behtar hai, yeh is par depend karta hai ki online infrastructure par kaunse accelerator available hain versus big data infrastructure par kaunse hain — online infrastructure par custom ML chips mil sakte hain, isliye woh aksar behtar hota hai.

Beam se online prediction invoke karna

Beam pipeline aur REST API dono ke fayde ek saath bhi liye ja sakte hain — Beam pipeline in-memory model ko call karne ke bajay deployed REST endpoint ko call kare. Isse streaming prediction bhi support ho jati hai, jo managed batch service nahi karti. Iske do performance fayde hain — deployed model ko model ki computation ke hisaab se scale kiya ja sakta hai aur Beam pipeline ko data rate ke hisaab se, alag-alag scale karne se cost bachti hai. Aur deployed model GPU ka behtar use karta hai kyunki poora model code TensorFlow graph par hota hai, jabki Dataflow pipeline me data reading aur grouping jaise kaam GPU se fayda nahi uthate. Iske against ek cost hai — Beam se deployed model tak ek extra network call hoti hai. Aam taur par model jitna bada hota hai aur batch jitna bada hota hai, online model ko Beam se call karna utna hi faydemand hota hai. Measure karke decide karo ki tumhare case me kaunsa tareeka behtar hai.

Yaad rakho: Batch prediction ko parallel karo, model ko har worker par ek baar load karo aur batch karo — aur Beam pipeline ko REST endpoint se jodkar streaming support aur independent scaling ka fayda lo.

09.3Chapter 9 · Model Predictions

Edge ML & Federated Learning

Har prediction cloud par nahi ho sakti. Jab device ke paas internet nahi hai, ya result turant chahiye, ya data device se bahar nahi ja sakta, tab model ko device par hi chalana padta hai — yahi edge ML hai.

Edge devices ki constraints

Edge devices jaise smartphones, factory ke instruments aur outdoor sensors par kuch khaas limitations hoti hain. Internet connection ho bhi to spotty aur low bandwidth wali ho sakti hai, isliye cloud ka round trip afford nahi hota. Privacy ki wajah se image data device se bahar nahi jaana chahiye. Device par memory, storage aur computing power cloud machine ke mukable bahut kam hoti hai. Aur device sasta, chhota, kam power khane wala aur zyada garam na hone wala hona chahiye. Isliye edge par efficient on-device ML accelerator aur halka-phulka model dono chahiye hote hain — modern phones me GPU pehle se hota hai, aur instruments me alag se accelerator lagaya ja sakta hai.

TensorFlow Lite

TensorFlow Lite ek framework hai jo TensorFlow model ki inference edge devices par chalata hai. Yeh TensorFlow ka alag version nahi hai — isse train nahi kar sakte. Pehle model ko normal TensorFlow se train karte hain, phir converter tool se SavedModel ko efficient .tflite file me convert karte hain. Efficient prediction ke liye do cheezein zaroori hain — pehle, MobileNet jaisa edge-optimized model use karo, jo bade models ke mukable lagbhag 40x fast ho sakta hai. Doosra, model weights ko quantize karo, matlab float32 ki jagah int8 numbers use karo. Isse memory ek-chauthai ho jati hai aur integer arithmetic float se bahut fast hoti hai, accuracy me sirf lagbhag 0.2 se 0.5% ka nuksan hota hai. Quantization ke liye converter ko representative dataset diya jata hai taaki woh bina accuracy khoye weights ko sahi tareeke se quantize kar sake.

TensorFlow Lite chalana

Edge device par prediction ke liye TensorFlow Lite interpreter chalana padta hai — Android aur iOS ke liye alag interpreters available hain. Non-phone devices ke liye Coral Edge TPU use hota hai, jo USB dongle, baseboard ya chip ke roop me milta hai aur CPU ke mukable 30–50x speedup de sakta hai. Phone par pehle se available common kaam jaise text recognition ya face detection ke liye ML Kit jaisa ready-made framework check kar lena chahiye, khud ka solution banane se pehle. Microcontrollers jaise Arduino par TensorFlow Lite nahi, TinyML use hota hai, kyunki wahan operating system bhi nahi hota aur sirf kuch tens of kilobytes memory hoti hai.

Image buffer ko process karna

Edge device par image seedha camera buffer se milti hai, isliye ek time par sirf ek image process hoti hai. Iske liye serving signature ko aise badla jata hai ki woh image tensor ko input lekar prediction de, phir us signature wale model ko TensorFlow Lite me convert kiya jata hai. Yeh dhyaan rakhna zaroori hai ki preprocessing wahi ho jo training me use hui thi.

Federated learning

TensorFlow Lite me model cloud par train hokar device par aata hai aur phir dobara train nahi hota — lekin data drift aur model drift edge par bhi hota hai. Privacy-sensitive cases me images ko device se bahar bhejna allowed nahi hota, to model ko update kaise karein? Iska jawab hai federated learning — har device apna data apne paas rakhkar sirf gradient update share karta hai, original image nahi. Bahut saare devices ke gradient updates ko average karke shared model ko update kiya jata hai, aur har device us shared model ko apne interactions se thoda fine-tune bhi kar sakta hai. Isse privacy bani rehti hai aur personalization bhi hoti hai. Privacy ko aur strong karne ke liye iske saath differential privacy bhi jodi ja sakti hai.

Yaad rakho: Edge ML me model ko chhota aur fast banao — MobileNet jaisa architecture, int8 quantization, aur on-device interpreter. Aur jab data device se bahar nahi ja sakta to federated learning se sirf gradients share karo, images nahi.

import tensorflow as tf
import os, shutil

MODEL_LOCATION='export/flowers_model3'  # will be created
# load from checkpoint and export a model that has desired signature
CHECK_POINT_DIR='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained/chkpts'
model = tf.keras.models.load_model(CHECK_POINT_DIR)

IMG_HEIGHT = 345
IMG_WIDTH = 345
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()
    
# a single image of any size
@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None, None, 3], dtype=tf.float32)])
def predict_flower_type(img):
    img = tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)
    batch_pred = model(tf.expand_dims(img, axis=0))
    top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
    pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
    return {
        'probability': tf.squeeze(top_prob, axis=0),
        'flower_type': tf.squeeze(pred_label, axis=0)
    }

shutil.rmtree('export', ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir('export')


model.save(MODEL_LOCATION,
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_flower_type
          })

import tensorflow as tf
converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_saved_model(MODEL_LOCATION)
tflite_model = converter.convert()

with open('export/model.tflite', 'wb') as ofp:
    ofp.write(tflite_model)

10Chapter 10 · Trends in Production ML

Trends in Production ML

Model banana data scientist ka kaam hai, lekin production me usko chalana ek team ka kaam hai — ML engineer pipeline banata hai, end user model par bharosa karna chahta hai, aur domain expert bina code likhe model banana chahta hai. Chapter 10 in teeno trends ko cover karta hai.

Machine learning pipeline kya hoti hai

End-to-end ML pipeline me dataset banana, model train karna aur model deploy karna — yeh teeno steps ek flow me judte hain. Jaise flowers wale example me pehle JPEG images ko TensorFlow Records me convert karte hain, phir model train karte hain, phir serving ke liye deploy karte hain. Pipeline banane ke liye pehle cluster setup karna hota hai, phir codebase ko containerize karna hota hai, phir har step ke liye component likhna hota hai, components ko jodna hota hai, aur aakhir me run ko automate karna hota hai.

Pipeline ki zaroorat kyun hai

Model ek baar train karke khatam nahi hota. Naya data aata rehta hai — kuch sau nayi files milengi to wahi steps dobara karne padenge. Data drift bhi hota hai — naya data training data se alag ho sakta hai, jaise zyada resolution wali images ya naye season ki photos, jisse model ki performance girne lagti hai. Aur naye ideas bhi aate rehte hain — koi behtar augmentation filter ya architecture ka naya version. Isliye ek aisa framework chahiye jo ML pipeline ko schedule aur operationalize kare aur constant experimentation allow kare. Kubeflow Pipelines aisa hi framework hai — yeh Kubernetes par chalta hai aur pipeline ko apni domain-specific language me represent karta hai. Google Cloud par iska managed version Vertex Pipelines ke naam se milta hai. Agar pipeline standard steps follow kare — data validation, transformation, training, evaluation, deployment aur monitoring — to TensorFlow Extended jaisi higher-level abstraction bhi use ki ja sakti hai.

Kubeflow Pipelines cluster aur containerization

Kubeflow pipeline chalane ke liye pehle ek cluster setup karna hota hai, jise managed console se create kiya ja sakta hai. Pipeline Jupyter notebook me develop karke cluster par deploy ki ja sakti hai. Pipeline containers chalati hai, isliye codebase ko containerize karna zaroori hai — notebook wali container image lekar usme extra dependencies install karte hain aur poora repository copy karte hain, aur Dockerfile se image banakar container registry me push karte hain.

Component likhna aur jodna

Har pipeline step ek component hota hai, jo ek YAML file se define hota hai — usme inputs, container image aur command likhe hote hain. Jaise dataset banane wala component ek shell script call karta hai jo Python program ko chalata hai. Shell script isliye use hoti hai kyunki setup, agle steps ko message pass karna aur cleanup jaise kaam Python code me daalna sahi nahi hota. Components ko jodne ke liye ek step ka output doosre step ka input banaya jata hai — jaise create_dataset step ka output directory train_model step ko milta hai. Aise jodne se Kubeflow pehla step complete hone ka wait karta hai, phir doosra step shuru karta hai. Deploy step ke liye custom code ki zaroorat nahi — Kubeflow ka ready-made deploy operator use hota hai.

Run ko automate karna

Pipeline submit karne ka Python API hai, isliye usko Cloud Function ya container me daalkar schedule par ya nayi files aane par trigger kiya ja sakta hai. CI triggers par bhi retraining chalai ja sakti hai jab naya code commit ho. Kubeflow results ko cache bhi karta hai — agar component wahi inputs ke saath dobara chale to purana result mil jata hai — lekin cache ki ek limit hai: woh storage directory ke contents check nahi karta, isliye input-output directory ke naam me timestamp daalna aur cache ki staleness set karna zaroori hota hai. CI, CD, permissions aur infrastructure authorization milkar MLOps banta hai.

Yaad rakho: Model ek baar ka kaam nahi hai — naya data, data drift aur naye experiments ke liye pipeline chahiye. Kubeflow me har step ek containerized component hota hai, aur ek step ka output doosre ka input bankar poora flow automate ho jata hai.

import kfp
import kfp.dsl as dsl
import json
import os

create_dataset_op = kfp.components.load_component_from_file(
    #'components/noop_create_dataset.yaml'
    'components/create_dataset.yaml'
)
train_model_op = kfp.components.load_component_from_file(
    #'components/train_model_kfp.yaml'
    'components/train_model_caip.yaml'
)
deploy_op = kfp.components.load_component_from_url(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubeflow/pipelines/master/components/gcp/ml_engine/deploy/component.yaml')

@dsl.pipeline(
    name='Flowers Transfer Learning Pipeline',
    description='End-to-end pipeline'
)
def flowerstxf_pipeline(
    project_id = PROJECT,
    bucket = BUCKET,
    region = REGION
):
    # Step 1: Create dataset
    create_dataset = create_dataset_op(
        runner='DataflowRunner',
        project_id=project_id,
        region=region,
        input_csv='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/all_data.csv',
        output_dir='gs://{}/data/flower_tfrecords'.format(bucket),
        labels_dict='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/dict.txt'
    )
    create_dataset.execution_options.caching_strategy.max_cache_staleness = "P7D"
    
    # Step 2: Train model
    train_model = train_model_op(
        input_topdir=create_dataset.outputs['tfrecords_topdir'],
        region=region,
        job_dir='gs://{}/trained_model'.format(bucket)
    )
    train_model.execution_options.caching_strategy.max_cache_staleness = "P0D"
    
    # Step 3: Deploy trained model
    deploy_model = deploy_op(
        model_uri=train_model.outputs['trained_model'],
        project_id=project_id, 
        model_id='flowers', 
        version_id='txf', 
        runtime_version='2.3', 
        python_version='3.7',
        version={}, 
        replace_existing_version='True', 
        set_default='True', 
        wait_interval='30')

pipeline_func = flowerstxf_pipeline
pipeline_filename = pipeline_func.__name__ + '.zip'
import kfp.compiler as compiler
compiler.Compiler().compile(pipeline_func, pipeline_filename)

import kfp
client = kfp.Client(host=KFPHOST)
experiment = client.create_experiment('from_notebook')
run_name = pipeline_func.__name__ + ' run'
run_result = client.run_pipeline(experiment.id, run_name, pipeline_filename, 
                                 {
                                     'project_id': PROJECT,
                                     'bucket': BUCKET,
                                     'region': REGION
                                 })

10.1Chapter 10 · Trends in Production ML

Explainability

Model ne prediction to de di, lekin kyun di? Agar doctor ko X-ray par fracture dikh raha hai to woh jaanna chahega ki model ne exactly kin pixels ko dekhkar yeh faisla liya. Isi sawaal ka jawab hai explainability — aur medicine jaise domains me yeh responsible AI ki pehli shart mani jati hai.

Explainability kyun zaroori hai

Teen bade fayde hain. Pehla hai trust — bina explanation ke black-box model par user bharosa nahi karega, khaas taur par jab faisla health ya finance se juda ho. Doosra hai troubleshooting — agar model kutte ko lomdi bata raha hai aur sabse important pixels barf ke hain, to samajh aata hai ki model ne background ko galat tareeke se seekh liya hai, aur usko theek karne ke liye alag seasons ki photos ya augmentation chahiye. Teesra hai bias pakadna — agar model sensitive features ko zyada importance de raha hai, to training data ke bias ka pata chal sakta hai, jaise kuch areas me zyada tickets milne ki wajah se model sadak ke gaddhon ko violation se jod le.

Global aur instance-level explanation

Do types ki explanations hoti hain. Global explanation poore model ki property hoti hai — kaunsi feature overall prediction ke variance ko kitna explain karti hai, jaise ek feature 36% aur doosri 23%. Lekin images me koi explicit human-readable feature nahi hoti, isliye global methods computer vision me zyada useful nahi hote. Instance-level explanation har ek prediction ko alag se explain karti hai — is image me kin pixels ne is faisle me sabse zyada yogdan diya. Yahi image models me sabse zyada kaam aati hai.

Chaar techniques

LIME image ko similar pixels ke patches me todta hai, kuch patches ko hatakar perturbed images banata hai, aur model se un par prediction lekar dekhta hai ki kaunse patches sabse zyada positive weight rakhte hain — wahi explanation hoti hai. KernelSHAP LIME jaisa hai lekin perturbed instances ko game theory se aayi distribution ke hisaab se weight karta hai — zyada patches wali instance ko kam weight milta hai kyunki koi bhi patch important ho sakta tha. Yeh LIME se mehenga hota hai lekin thoda behtar result deta hai. Integrated Gradients baseline image se lekar actual image tak har pixel ko step-by-step badal kar gradient compute karta hai — jinki integrated gradient sabse zyada hoti hai, woh pixels sabse important hote hain. Baseline chunna critical hota hai — X-ray me kaale areas ka matlab hota hai, isliye wahan random pixels wala baseline behtar hota hai. xRAI LIME wali patch approach aur Integrated Gradients wali pixel attribution ko combine karta hai — pehle regions banata hai, phir un regions ko hatakar model ko dobara chalata hai aur importance ke hisaab se rank karta hai.

IG ya xRAI — kab kaunsa

Integrated Gradients pixel-wise attribution deta hai, isliye low-contrast images jaise X-ray ya lab ki scientific images par behtar kaam karta hai. xRAI region-based attribution deta hai, isliye natural images jaise janwar ki photo par behtar hota hai. Flowers wale example me Integrated Gradients ne tulip ki pehchan ke liye green stalks ko important bataya, lekin xRAI ne sahi dikhaya ki asal me tulip ke bulb drive kar rahe the — yeh Integrated Gradients ki limitation ka achha example hai.

Explainability ko deploy karna

Explainability ko prediction service me jodne ke liye model me do extra signatures add karni padti hain — ek preprocessing signature jo filename se image tensor banaye, aur ek model signature jo perturbed image tensor lekar prediction de. Saath me ek metadata file bhi chahiye hoti hai jisme baseline image aur kaunsi output explain karni hai, yeh likha hota hai. Phir model ko Integrated Gradients ya xRAI method ke saath deploy karte hain, aur normal prediction ke saath-saath explanation bhi mangi ja sakti hai. Explanation me approximation error bhi milta hai — agar woh zyada ho to integral steps badha dene chahiye. Ek aur naya tareeka training ke dauraan hi proponents aur opponents pehchanana hai — kaunsi training examples loss kam karti hain aur kaunsi badhati hain, jisse mislabeled examples aur outliers pakde ja sakte hain.

Yaad rakho: Explainability trust, debugging aur bias pakadne ke liye hai. Natural images par region-based xRAI behtar hota hai, low-contrast scientific images par pixel-wise Integrated Gradients — aur baseline ka choice explanation ki quality badal sakta hai.

import tensorflow as tf
import os, shutil

MODEL_LOCATION='export/flowers_model3'  # will be created

# load from checkpoint and export a model that has desired signature
CHECK_POINT_DIR='gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained/chkpts'
model = tf.keras.models.load_model(CHECK_POINT_DIR)

IMG_HEIGHT = 345
IMG_WIDTH = 345
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
CLASS_NAMES = 'daisy dandelion roses sunflowers tulips'.split()

def preprocess(filename):
    img_bytes = tf.io.read_file(filename)
    img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
    img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
    return tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS], dtype=tf.float32)])
def xai_model(input_images):
    batch_pred = model(input_images) # same as model.predict()
    top_prob = tf.math.reduce_max(batch_pred, axis=[1])
    pred_label_index = tf.math.argmax(batch_pred, axis=1)
    pred_label = tf.gather(tf.convert_to_tensor(CLASS_NAMES), pred_label_index)
    return {
        'probability': top_prob,
        'flower_type_int': pred_label_index,
        'flower_type_str': pred_label
    }

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def xai_preprocess(filenames):
    input_images = tf.map_fn(
        preprocess,
        filenames,
        fn_output_signature=tf.float32
    )
    return {
        # match the signature of xai_model
        'input_images': input_images
    }

@tf.function(input_signature=[tf.TensorSpec([None,], dtype=tf.string)])
def predict_filename(filenames):
    preproc_output = xai_preprocess(filenames)
    # return xai_model(preproc_output['input_images'])
    return xai_model(**preproc_output)

shutil.rmtree('export', ignore_errors=True)
os.mkdir('export')
model.save(MODEL_LOCATION,
          signatures={
              'serving_default': predict_filename,
              'xai_preprocess': xai_preprocess, # should be exactly what's supplied to model
              'xai_model': xai_model # call the model
          })

#!/bin/bash

MODEL_NAME=flowers_regional
MODEL_LOCATION="gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_trained" # will change when we call script
VERSION_NAME=ig
EXPLAIN="--explanation-method integrated-gradients --num-integral-steps 25"
REGION='us-central1'  # CHANGE! You need GPU quota in this region
BUCKET='ai-analytics-solutions-kfpdemo' # CHANGE! for staging


while [[ "$#" -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        -v|--version) VERSION_NAME="$2"; shift ;;
        -m|--model_location) MODEL_LOCATION="$2"; shift ;;
        *) echo "Unknown parameter passed: $1"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    shift
done

if [[ "$VERSION_NAME" -eq "xrai" ]]; then
   EXPLAIN="--explanation-method xrai --num-integral-steps 25"
fi

echo "Deploying $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME with $EXPLAIN from $MODEL_LOCATION"

if [[ $(gcloud ai-platform models list --region=$REGION --format='value(name)' | grep $MODEL_NAME) ]]; then
    echo "The model named $MODEL_NAME already exists."
else
    # create model
    echo "Creating $MODEL_NAME model now."
    gcloud ai-platform models create --region=$REGION --enable-logging $MODEL_NAME
fi

if [[ $(gcloud ai-platform versions list --region=$REGION --model $MODEL_NAME --format='value(name)' | grep $VERSION_NAME) ]]; then
    echo "Deleting already the existing model $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME ... "
    gcloud ai-platform versions delete --quiet --region=$REGION --model=$MODEL_NAME $VERSION_NAME
    echo "Please run this script again if you don't see a Creating message ... "
    sleep 2
fi

# create model
echo "Creating $MODEL_NAME:$VERSION_NAME $EXPLAIN"
gcloud beta ai-platform versions create --model=$MODEL_NAME $VERSION_NAME --async \
       --region=$REGION  --machine-type n1-standard-4 \
       --framework=tensorflow --python-version=3.7 --runtime-version=2.1 \
       --origin=$MODEL_LOCATION --staging-bucket=gs://$BUCKET $EXPLAIN

import json
import base64
input_images = []
with open('request.json') as ifp:
    instances = json.load(ifp)['instances']
    for instance in instances:
        img_bytes = tf.io.read_file(instance['filenames'])
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=3)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        img = tf.image.resize_with_pad(img, IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)
        input_images.append(img.numpy())
        
explain_images = []
with open('response.json') as ifp:
    explanations = json.load(ifp)['explanations']
    for expln in explanations:
        b64bytes = expln['attributions_by_label'][0]['attributions']['input_images']['b64_jpeg']
        img_bytes = base64.b64decode(b64bytes)
        img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img_bytes, channels=3)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
        explain_images.append(img.numpy())
        print("approx error = {}".format(expln['attributions_by_label'][0]['approx_error']))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import tensorflow as tf

f, ax = plt.subplots(3, 5, figsize=(15,10))
for idx in range(len(input_images)):
    ax[0, idx].imshow(input_images[idx])
    ax[1, idx].imshow(explain_images[idx])
    ax[2, idx].imshow(1-explain_images[idx])
    ax[0, idx].axis('off')
    ax[1, idx].axis('off')
    ax[2, idx].axis('off')

10.2Chapter 10 · Trends in Production ML

No-Code Computer Vision

Har computer vision project me code likhna zaroori nahi hota. No-code aur low-code tools bina ek line code likhe image classification, object detection aur segmentation jaise kaam kar lete hain — aur aksar yahi project ka sabse smart pehla step hota hai.

No-code kyun use karein

Teen bade reasons hain. Pehla hai problem viability check — no-code tool ek sanity check deta hai ki kitni accuracy expect ki ja sakti hai. Agar counterfeit ID pehchanne me 98% precision mil rahi hai aur 2% customers galat tareeke se reject ho rahe hain, to shayad project hi futile hai aur time waste nahi karna chahiye. Doosra hai data quality aur quantity check — agar confusion matrix dikha raha hai ki paani me khade saare phool lily classify ho rahe hain, to samajh aata hai ki aur behtar data collect karna hai, model train karna nahi. Teesra hai benchmarking — no-code tool se jo accuracy milti hai, woh ek baseline ban jati hai jisse apne khud ke banaye models ko compare kar sakte hain. Isliye bahut si organizations domain experts ko no-code tools deti hain taaki woh problem viability aur data collection me madad kar sakein, data science team ke paas jaane se pehle.

Data load karna

Pehla step hai data load karna — tool ko CSV file ya storage bucket ki taraf point karte hain. Data load hone ke baad dikhta hai ki kitni images hain, har class me kitni hain, aur kya saari images labeled hain. UI me labels ko correct bhi kiya ja sakta hai, aur agar dataset bina labels ke ho to wahan se labeling service ko bhi outsource kiya ja sakta hai.

Training

Labels theek lagne par Train New Model button dabate hain — phir model type, dataset split aur training budget select karte hain. Achhe no-code systems andar hi andar data preprocessing, augmentation, state-of-the-art models aur hyperparameter tuning karte hain. Flowers dataset wale example me 8 ghante ka budget lagbhag 25 dollar ka tha, lekin early stopping ki wajah se training 30 minute se bhi kam me khatam ho gayi aur cost lagbhag 3 dollar aayi — aur accuracy 96.4% mili, jo Chapter 3 me bahut tuning ke baad mile sophisticated models ke barabar thi. Lekin dhyaan rakho — saare no-code systems ek jaise nahi hote. Kuch sirf ek model train karte hain, kuch sirf hyperparameter tuning karte hain, kuch model family me search karte hain. Documentation padhkar samajh lo ki tumhe kya mil raha hai.

Evaluation aur deployment

Evaluation me confusion matrix aur galat predictions ko dekhte hain — jaise sabse zyada galtiyan roses ko tulips samajhne me hui. Phir un mistakes ko dekhkar decide karte hain ki kaisi aur images collect karni hain ya kaunsi unrepresentative images hatani hain. Satisfied hone par model ko ek endpoint par deploy kar dete hain, jisse web service ban jati hai aur clients sample requests bhejkar prediction le sakte hain. Basic computer vision problems ke liye no-code systems ki ease of use, low cost aur high accuracy bahut compelling hai — isliye inko apne har computer vision project ke pehle step ke roop me use karna chahiye.

Yaad rakho: No-code tool ko shortcut nahi, sanity check samjho — viability, data quality aur benchmark teeno ek saath milte hain, aur aksar 3 dollar me woh accuracy mil jati hai jiske liye hafton ki tuning lagti hai.
SOURCESource: Practical Machine Learning for Computer Vision, O'Reilly, Chapter 10 — Trends in Production ML

11Chapter 11 · Advanced Vision Problems

Advanced Vision Problems

Ab tak humne poori image ko classify karna seekha hai. Lekin computer vision sirf classification nahi hai — kabhi object ki lambai naapni hoti hai, kabhi bheed me log ginne hote hain. Chapter 11 me hum measurement aur counting jaise advanced problems dekhenge, jo basic building blocks se hi solve hote hain.

Object measurement — problem kya hai

Kabhi-kabhi image ke andar object ka measurement chahiye hota hai, jaise sofa 180 cm lamba hai. Sirf pixels ginne se kaam nahi chalega, kyunki wahi object camera ki doori, rotation aur aspect ratio ke hisaab se alag number of pixels me dikh sakta hai. Isliye measurement ke liye chaar steps chahiye — reference object, segmentation, rotation correction aur ratio se measurement. Example ke roop me online shoe store ko le lo — customer apne footprint ki photo bhejta hai aur store ko foot ki length, width aur arch type se sahi shoe size nikalna hai.

Reference object

Footprint ki photo akele kaafi nahi hai, kyunki camera kitna paas hai, isse foot ka size image me badal jata hai. Iska simple solution hai ek reference object use karna jiska real size pata ho — jaise credit card, jiske standard dimensions hote hain aur jo lagbhag har customer ke paas hota hai. Customer ko footprint ke paas credit card rakhkar photo leni hoti hai. Ab measurement ka kaam foot ko card se compare karne ka ban jata hai. Training dataset me alag-alag paper types, lighting, rotation aur flips hone chahiye taaki model real-world variations handle kar sake, aur shuruaat me augmentation jaise rotation, blur, brightness aur contrast change karke dataset ko bada aur flexible banaya jata hai.

Segmentation aur rotation correction

Pehle Mask R-CNN jaise segmentation model se footprint aur credit card ke alag-alag masks nikalte hain — mask branch ke do channels hote hain, ek har object ke liye. Phir dono masks ko rotation ke hisaab se normalize karna padta hai, kyunki customer ne card ko thoda tedha rakha ho sakta hai. Iske liye har mask par principal component analysis (PCA) karte hain — sabse bade eigenvector ki direction object ki length hoti hai, aur original axis aur pehle eigenvector ke beech ka angle batata hai ki kitni rotation correction karni hai.

Ratio aur measurements

Rotation-corrected masks ko do dimensions me project karke length aur width nikaalte hain — y-coordinate ke smallest aur largest value ke beech ki pixel distance length hoti hai, aur x-dimension me width. Dono measurements abhi pixels me hain, centimeters me nahi. Ab credit card ke real measurements pata hone ki wajah se pixel aur real dimension ke beech ka ratio nikalte hain, aur wahi ratio footprint ki pixel dimensions par lagakar uske asli measurements nikal lete hain. Arch type nikalna thoda aur complex hai — high-pressure areas me pixels ginne padte hain — lekin principle wahi hai.

Counting — seedha tareeka kyun fail hota hai

Counting ke applications bahut hain — bheed ka size, drone imagery se fasal ki yield. Berries ki photo me kitni berries hain, yeh ginna sochne se zyada mushkil hai. Object detection se bounding boxes ginne par overlapping berries miss ya combine ho sakti hain. Segmentation se cluster ke size ke hisaab se ginna scale-invariant nahi hai — berries chhoti ya badi hui to fail ho jayega. Poori image se number ko regression karna bhi scale problem se pareshan hota hai aur labeled images milna mushkil hota hai, aur location ki information bhi kho jati hai.

Density estimation

Chhote aur overlapping objects ke liye behtar tareeka hai density estimation. Image ko chhote non-overlapping patches me todte hain aur har patch ko label karte hain — us patch me kitne object centers hain. Model ko yahi density estimate karna sikhate hain. Berry ko usi patch me ginte hain jisme uska center point hai, taaki total count sahi rahe. Input patch label patch se bada hota hai, kyunki aas-paas ka context bhi chahiye hota hai, aur image ke border par padding use hoti hai. Yeh tareeka bheed ginne, biological images me cells ginne aur aise hi kaamo me detection se behtar kaam karta hai.

Patches nikalna aur simulated images

Patches nikalne ke liye TensorFlow ka extract_patches function use hota hai — input image se bade patches SAME padding ke saath aur label image se chhote patches VALID padding ke saath. Label patch ke pixel values ko sum karke density milti hai. Ek kamaal ki baat yeh hai ki training ke liye asli labeled photos ki zaroorat bhi nahi hai — simulated images se kaam chal sakta hai. Jaise tamatar ginne ke liye sirf brown-green background par laal circles wali simulated images se train kiya gaya model asli tamatar ke plants par bhi achha perform karta hai. Isse bada dataset jaldi ban jata hai. Lekin simulation ko real jaisa banana zaroori hai — sirf ek hi size ki berries simulate karne par asli photo par estimate galat ho sakta hai.

Regression aur prediction

Patch aur density milne ke baad ek simple ConvNet regression model train karte hain — output ek hi numeric value hoti hai, output node linear hota hai taaki density koi bhi value le sake, aur loss mean squared error hoti hai. Prediction ke time par input image ko training jaisi hi patches me todte hain, har patch par model se density predict karte hain aur sabko sum kar dete hain — yahi total count hota hai. Independent simulated images par predictions actual numbers ke 10% ke andar aati hain, jo is approach ki taakat dikhata hai.

Yaad rakho: Measurement me scale ka problem reference object se solve hota hai, aur counting me overlapping objects ka problem density estimation se — dono me seedha pixel ginna ya box ginna kaam nahi karta.

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import scipy.ndimage as ndimage
from skimage import draw

FULL_IMG_WIDTH = 512
FULL_IMG_HEIGHT = 512
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
PATCH_WIDTH = 32
PATCH_HEIGHT = 32
INPUT_WIDTH = PATCH_WIDTH*2
INPUT_HEIGHT = PATCH_HEIGHT*2

def generate_image(with_intermediates=False):
  # the image has a random greenish background that is smoothed
  backgr = np.zeros([FULL_IMG_HEIGHT, FULL_IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS])
  backgr[ np.random.rand(FULL_IMG_HEIGHT, FULL_IMG_WIDTH) < 0.3, 1 ] = 1
  backgr = ndimage.gaussian_filter(backgr, sigma=(5, 5, 0), order=0)

  # between 25 and 75 berries randomly placed
  num_berries = np.random.randint(25, 75)
  berry_cx = np.random.randint(0, FULL_IMG_WIDTH, size=num_berries)
  berry_cy = np.random.randint(0, FULL_IMG_HEIGHT, size=num_berries)
  label = np.zeros([FULL_IMG_WIDTH, FULL_IMG_HEIGHT])
  label[berry_cx, berry_cy] = 1

  # draw the berries which are 10 px in radius
  berries = np.zeros([FULL_IMG_HEIGHT, FULL_IMG_WIDTH])
  for idx in range(len(berry_cx)):
    rr, cc = draw.circle(berry_cx[idx], berry_cy[idx],
                         radius=10, 
                         shape=berries.shape)
    berries[rr, cc] = 1

  # add berries to the background
  img = np.copy(backgr)
  img[berries > 0] = [1, 0, 0] # red

  if with_intermediates:
    print("{} berries simulated".format(num_berries))
    return backgr, berries, img, label
  else:
    return img, label

images = generate_image(True)
f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(images), figsize=(15, 5))
for idx, img in enumerate(images):
  ax[idx].imshow(img)
  ax[idx].axis('off')

## given an image, get the patches
def get_patches(img, label, verbose=False):
  img = tf.expand_dims(img, axis=0)
  label = tf.expand_dims(tf.expand_dims(label, axis=0), axis=-1)
  if verbose:
    print(img.shape, label.shape)
  num_patches = (FULL_IMG_HEIGHT // PATCH_HEIGHT)**2
  patches = tf.image.extract_patches(img, 
                                     sizes=[1, INPUT_HEIGHT, INPUT_WIDTH, 1],
                                     strides=[1, PATCH_HEIGHT, PATCH_WIDTH, 1],
                                     rates=[1, 1, 1, 1],
                                     padding='SAME',
                                     name='get_patches')
  patches = tf.reshape(patches, [num_patches, -1])
  labels = tf.image.extract_patches(label,
                                    sizes=[1, PATCH_HEIGHT, PATCH_WIDTH, 1],
                                    strides=[1, PATCH_HEIGHT, PATCH_WIDTH, 1],
                                    rates=[1, 1, 1, 1],
                                    padding='VALID',
                                    name='get_labels')
  labels = tf.reshape(labels, [num_patches, -1])
  # the "density" is the number of points in the label patch
  patch_labels = tf.math.reduce_sum(labels, axis=[1], name='calc_density')
  if verbose:
    print(patches.shape, labels.shape, patch_labels.shape)
  return patches, patch_labels

# Getting input data
def create_dataset(num_full_images):
  def generate_patches():
    for i in range(num_full_images):
      img, label = generate_image()
      patches, patch_labels = get_patches(img, label)
      # print(len(patches) * num_full_images)
      for patch, patch_label in zip(patches, patch_labels):
        yield patch, patch_label

  return tf.data.Dataset.from_generator(
    generate_patches,
    (tf.float32, tf.float32), # patch, patch_label
    (tf.TensorShape([INPUT_HEIGHT*INPUT_WIDTH*IMG_CHANNELS]),
    tf.TensorShape([]))  
  )

trainds = create_dataset(1) # will create 256 patches per image
for img, label in trainds.take(3):
  avg = tf.math.reduce_mean(img) # avg pixel in image
  print(img.shape, label.numpy(), avg.numpy())

# Train
NUM_TRAIN = 200 # 10000 more realistic
NUM_EVAL = 10 # 1000 more realistic
NUM_EPOCHS = 5

def training_plot(metrics, history):
  f, ax = plt.subplots(1, len(metrics), figsize=(5*len(metrics), 5))
  for idx, metric in enumerate(metrics):
    ax[idx].plot(history.history[metric], ls='dashed')
    ax[idx].set_xlabel("Epochs")
    ax[idx].set_ylabel(metric)
    ax[idx].plot(history.history['val_' + metric]);
    ax[idx].legend([metric, 'val_' + metric])

def train_and_evaluate(batch_size = 32,
                       lrate = 0.001, # default in Adam constructor
                       l1 = 0,
                       l2 = 0,
                       num_filters = 32):
  regularizer = tf.keras.regularizers.l1_l2(l1, l2)
  train_dataset = create_dataset(NUM_TRAIN).batch(batch_size)
  eval_dataset = create_dataset(NUM_EVAL).batch(64)

  # a simple convnet. you can make it more complex, of course
  # the patch is flattened, so we start by reshaping to an image
  model = tf.keras.Sequential([
              tf.keras.layers.Reshape([INPUT_HEIGHT, INPUT_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS],
                                      input_shape=[INPUT_WIDTH * INPUT_HEIGHT * IMG_CHANNELS]),
              tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(num_filters, (3,3), activation='relu'),
              tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
              tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(num_filters*2, (3,3), activation='relu'),
              tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
              tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(num_filters*2, (3,3), activation='relu'),
              tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_filters*2,
                                    kernel_regularizer=regularizer, 
                                    activation=tf.keras.activations.relu),
              tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='linear')
  ])
  model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=lrate),
                  loss=tf.keras.losses.mean_squared_error,
                  metrics=['mse', 'mae'])
  print(model.summary())
  history = model.fit(train_dataset, validation_data=eval_dataset, epochs=NUM_EPOCHS)
  training_plot(['loss', 'mse', 'mae'], history)
  return model

model = train_and_evaluate()

## prediction.
def count_berries(model, img):
  num_patches = (FULL_IMG_HEIGHT // PATCH_HEIGHT)**2
  img = tf.expand_dims(img, axis=0)
  patches = tf.image.extract_patches(img,
                sizes=[1, INPUT_HEIGHT, INPUT_WIDTH, 1],
                strides=[1, PATCH_HEIGHT, PATCH_WIDTH, 1],
                rates=[1, 1, 1, 1],
                padding='SAME',
                name='get_patches')
  patches = tf.reshape(patches, [num_patches, -1])
  densities = model.predict(patches)
  return tf.reduce_sum(densities)

# use an example image
f, ax = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(20, 20))
for idx in range(16):
  backgr, berries, img, label = generate_image(True)
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].imshow(img)
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].set_title("actual={:.1f} pred={:.1f}".format(
    tf.reduce_sum(label).numpy(),
    count_berries(model, img).numpy()
  ))
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].axis('off')

# OPTIONAL, CAN BE OMITTED
img, label = images = generate_image()
patches, labels = get_patches(img, label, verbose=True)

# display a few patches
f, ax = plt.subplots(4, 4, figsize=(20, 20))
for idx in range(16):
  r = np.random.randint(0, patches.shape[0])
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].imshow(tf.reshape(patches[r], [INPUT_HEIGHT, INPUT_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS]).numpy())
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].set_title("density={:.1f}".format(labels[r].numpy()))
  ax[idx//4, idx%4].axis('off')

!file berries.jpg

contents = tf.io.read_file('./berries.jpg')
img = tf.image.decode_image(contents)
img = tf.image.resize(img, [FULL_IMG_WIDTH, FULL_IMG_HEIGHT])
n = count_berries(model, img)
print(n.numpy())

11.1Chapter 11 · Advanced Vision Problems

Pose Estimation

Photo me insaan baitha hai, khada hai, naach raha hai ya leta hai — yeh jaanna ho, ya sports aur medical setting me posture par advice deni ho, to body ke key parts ki position pehchanani padti hai. Yahi pose estimation hai.

Pose estimation kya hai

Pose estimation me image me elbows, knees, shoulders, face jaise key body parts — jinhe joints kehte hain — ki position identify karni hoti hai. In joints ki relative position se pata chalta hai ki subject kya kar raha hai. Pose estimation model ko scratch se train karna aam taur par zaroori nahi hota — pehle se trained model ka output lekar usse decide karte hain ki image ke subjects kya kar rahe hain.

PersonLab aur PoseNet ka idea

State-of-the-art approach me teen steps hote hain. Pehle, object detection model se skeleton ke saare points of interest ka heatmap banate hain — yeh detection model ke classification head ka score hota hai, thresholding se pehle ka. Doosra, har detected joint se aas-paas ke joints ki sabse likely location nikalte hain — jaise wrist detect hua to usse elbow ki offset location bhi milti hai. Teesra, voting mechanism se joints ke basis par human pose detect karte hain. Pehle do steps ek saath hi hote hain, kyunki object detection model ek saath joint, uski location aur paas ke joints ka offset predict karta hai.

Offset aur voting kyun zaroori hai

Sirf object detection chalana kaafi nahi hota — model kuch joints miss kar sakta hai ya galat joints detect kar sakta hai. Offset predictions isiliye important hain — agar elbow detect nahi hua to wrist aur shoulder se mile offset se elbow ki candidate locations mil jati hain. Ab ek joint ke liye teen candidate locations ho sakti hain — heatmap se ek aur do offsets se do. In sab par weighted voting mechanism, jise Hough transform kehte hain, final location decide karta hai. Yeh voting hi pose estimation ko robust banata hai.

PoseNet model

PoseNet ki implementations TensorFlow me Android aur web browser ke liye available hain. Web wali implementation MobileNet ya ResNet ko underlying architecture ke roop me use karti hai — ResNet bada aur slow hota hai lekin zyada accurate, MobileNet halka aur fast hota hai. Model 17 body parts identify karne ke liye train kiya gaya hai — naak, aankhein, kaan jaise facial features aur shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle jaise limb joints, left aur right dono taraf. Output me har keypoint ka score aur image me uski x-y position milti hai, jisse image par skeleton annotate kiya ja sakta hai.

Accuracy aur speed ka trade-off

PoseNet ki accuracy underlying classification model aur output stride par depend karti hai. Output stride jitna bada hoga, patches utne bade honge aur location ki precision utni kam hogi — chhota stride zyada accurate hota hai lekin slow. Input resolution bhi matter karta hai — badi resolution zyada accurate hoti hai, phir se speed ki keemat par. MobileNet me depth multiplier badhane se accuracy badhti hai lekin model slow hota hai, aur ResNet me quantization bytes badhane se accuracy aur model size dono badhte hain. Selfie images process karte time image ko horizontally flip karna chahiye taaki mirrored experience match kare.

Multiple poses pehchanana

Ek image me multiple logon ki pose estimate karne ke liye kuch extra steps lagte hain. Pehle segmentation model se woh saare pixels identify karte hain jo persons se belong karte hain. Phir joints ke combination se kisi khaas body part, jaise naak, ki sabse likely location nikalte hain. Phir segmentation mask ke pixels aur likely connections ke basis par person pixels ko alag-alag individuals ko assign karte hain. Iske liye maxDetections jaise parameters set karte hain — image me maximum kitne log hain, person detection ka confidence threshold kya ho, aur kitni doori ke andar do detections ek-doosre ko suppress karein.

Yaad rakho: Pose estimation me sirf joints detect karna kaafi nahi — offsets aur voting se missed ya galat joints theek hote hain, aur accuracy aur speed ke beech hamesha trade-off hota hai.

11.2Chapter 11 · Advanced Vision Problems

Image Search

Shopping site par celebrity ke pehne chashme dhoondhne hon ya apne gadget ki technical specifications nikalni hon — image search ka core problem ek hi hai: nayi upload ki gayi image se sabse similar image dataset me dhoondhni hai. Iska jawab hai embeddings.

Embeddings se search ka idea

Do images jo ek-doosre se similar hain, unke embeddings bhi ek-doosre ke paas honge. Toh similar image dhoondhne ke liye similar embedding dhoondhna kaafi hai. Iske liye dataset ki saari images ke embeddings ka ek search index banana padta hai. Yeh index ek bade distributed data warehouse me store kiya ja sakta hai, jaise BigQuery — wahan SQL query se nayi embedding aur har stored embedding ke beech Euclidean distance nikal kar sabse paas wale matches dikhaye ja sakte hain. Weather images wale example me sabse similar images pichle ya agle ghante ki nikli — jo bilkul sense banata hai.

Fast search — ScaNN

Data warehouse poora dataset scan karke search karta hai aur woh kaafi efficient hai, lekin uski latency zyada hoti hai — millisecond response time nahi milta. Real-time serving ke liye search space ko smart tareeke se prune karna padta hai. Scalable Nearest Neighbors, jise ScaNN kehte hain, yahi karta hai — woh fast search ke liye ek tree banata hai. Pehle MobileNet se embeddings banate hain, phir ScaNN searcher ko distance function ke saath initialize karte hain, jaise cosine distance ya dot product, aur phir query embedding ke nearest neighbors nikalte hain.

Generic embeddings ki limit

MobileNet embeddings ek bade image classification model ki intermediate layer se aati hain, jo transfer learning ke liye bani hoti hain. Flowers par search karne par results utne impressive nahi hote — paas wali images dikhne me utni similar nahi lagti. Isliye search ke liye customized embeddings chahiye hoti hain — jaise face similarity ke liye woh model behtar hoga jo faces identify aur verify karne ke liye train hua ho, generic embedding nahi. Yahan ek ethical note bhi zaroori hai — facial search aur verification ke aas-paas sensitive issues hain, isliye iska use hamesha responsibly aur rules ke andar hi karna chahiye.

Triplet loss se behtar embeddings

Triplet loss se aise embeddings banaye ja sakte hain jisme same label wali images paas-paas cluster karein aur alag label wali door rahein. Har triplet me teen images hoti hain — anchor image, usi label ki ek aur image jo positive pair banati hai, aur alag label ki image jo negative pair banati hai. Loss ka goal hota hai anchor aur positive ke beech ki distance ko zero ki taraf dhakelna aur anchor aur negative ke beech ki distance ko kam se kam ek margin se zyada rakhna. Negatives teen type ke hote hain — hard negatives jo positive se bhi paas hote hain, easy negatives jo bahut door hote hain, aur semi-hard negatives jo positive se door hain lekin margin ke andar hain. Research me paya gaya hai ki semi-hard negatives par focus karne se sabse achhe embeddings bante hain.

Training ki practical details

Flowers ke example me MobileNet embedding ke upar ek linear layer lagakar model ko triplet loss par train kiya gaya, semi-hard negatives par focus karke. Embedding ko normalize kiya gaya aur dimension 5 rakhi gayi. Loss ki definition ke hisaab se har batch me kam se kam ek positive pair hona zaroori hai — shuffling aur kaafi bada batch size use karne se yeh hota hai. 5 classes aur batch size 32 par positive pair milne ki probability 99.9% hoti hai, lekin 0.1% batches phir bhi fail ho sakte hain, isliye ingest pipeline me aise batches ko discard karna padta hai. Training ke baad embeddings plot karne par dikhta hai ki same label wali images cluster kar gayi hain, aur search results me distances chhoti aur images asal me similar lagti hain.

Yaad rakho: Image search embeddings ka khel hai — generic embeddings se kaam chal sakta hai, lekin triplet loss se trained embeddings same label ko paas aur alag label ko door karke search ko kaafi behtar bana deti hain.

import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_addons as tfa

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_hub as hub
import tensorflow_addons as tfa
import scann
import os

# Load compressed models from tensorflow_hub
os.environ['TFHUB_MODEL_LOAD_FORMAT'] = 'COMPRESSED'

IMG_HEIGHT = 224
IMG_WIDTH = 224
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
BATCH_SIZE = 32
NUM_IMAGES = 100
NUM_NEIGH = 3 # top 3
CLASS_NAMES = ['daisy', 'dandelion', 'roses', 'sunflowers', 'tulips']


def read_and_decode(filename, reshape_dims=[IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH]):
  # Read the file
  img = tf.io.read_file(filename)
  # Convert the compressed string to a 3D uint8 tensor.
  img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(img, channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
  # Use `convert_image_dtype` to convert to floats in the [0,1] range.
  img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)
  # Resize the image to the desired size.
  return tf.image.resize(img, reshape_dims)

def decode_csv(csv_row):
  record_defaults = ["path", "flower"]
  filename, label_string = tf.io.decode_csv(csv_row, record_defaults)
  img = read_and_decode(filename, [IMG_WIDTH, IMG_HEIGHT])
  label = tf.argmax(tf.math.equal(CLASS_NAMES, label_string))
  return filename, img, label, label_string

layers = [
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4",
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Flatten()
]
model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flowers_embedding')
print(model.summary())

def create_embeddings_dataset(embedder, csvfilename, num_images):
  ds = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(csvfilename).
        map(decode_csv).take(num_images).batch(BATCH_SIZE))
  dataset_filenames = []
  dataset_embeddings = []
  for filenames, images, _, _ in ds:
    embeddings = embedder(images)
    dataset_filenames.extend([f.numpy().decode('utf-8') for f in filenames])
    dataset_embeddings.extend(embeddings)
  dataset_embeddings = tf.convert_to_tensor(dataset_embeddings)
  return dataset_filenames, dataset_embeddings

dataset_filenames, dataset_embeddings = create_embeddings_dataset(
    lambda x: model.predict(x),
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv", NUM_IMAGES
)
print(dataset_filenames[:3])
print(dataset_embeddings.shape) # should be (NUM_IMAGES, 1280)

query_filenames, query_embeddings = create_embeddings_dataset(
    lambda x: model.predict(x),
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv", 2
)
print(query_embeddings.shape)

## Create SCaNN searcher
searcher = scann.scann_ops.builder(dataset_embeddings, NUM_NEIGH, "dot_product").score_ah(2).build()

neighbors, distances = searcher.search_batched(query_embeddings)
print(neighbors)
print(distances)

f, ax = plt.subplots(len(query_filenames), NUM_NEIGH + 1,
                     figsize=(5 * (1 + NUM_NEIGH), 5 * len(query_filenames)))
for rowno, query_filename in enumerate(query_filenames):
  ax[rowno][0].imshow(read_and_decode(query_filename).numpy())
  ax[rowno][0].axis('off')
  for colno, neigh in enumerate(neighbors[rowno]):
    ax[rowno][colno+1].imshow(read_and_decode(dataset_filenames[neigh]).numpy())
    ax[rowno][colno+1].set_title('dist={:.1f}'.format(distances[rowno][colno].numpy()))
    ax[rowno][colno+1].axis('off')

layers = [
      hub.KerasLayer(
          "https://tfhub.dev/google/tf2-preview/mobilenet_v2/feature_vector/4",
          input_shape=(IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH, IMG_CHANNELS),
          trainable=False,
          name='mobilenet_embedding'),
      tf.keras.layers.Dense(5, activation=None, name='dense_5'),
      tf.keras.layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.math.l2_normalize(x, axis=1), name='normalize_embeddings')
]
model = tf.keras.Sequential(layers, name='flowers_embedding')
model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(0.001), loss=tfa.losses.TripletSemiHardLoss())
print(model.summary())

# training on just 32*10 images, not full dataset
train_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).take(BATCH_SIZE*10).map(lambda path, img, lint, ls: (img, lint)).batch(BATCH_SIZE)
history = model.fit(train_dataset, epochs=5)

# repeat with new model
dataset_filenames, dataset_embeddings = create_embeddings_dataset(
    lambda x: model.predict(x),
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/train_set.csv", NUM_IMAGES
)
print(dataset_filenames[:3])
print(dataset_embeddings.shape) # should be (NUM_IMAGES, 5)

query_filenames, query_embeddings = create_embeddings_dataset(
    lambda x: model.predict(x),
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv", 2
)
print(query_embeddings.shape)

searcher = scann.scann_ops.builder(dataset_embeddings, NUM_NEIGH, "dot_product").score_ah(2).build()
neighbors, distances = searcher.search_batched(query_embeddings)
print(neighbors)
print(distances)

f, ax = plt.subplots(len(query_filenames), NUM_NEIGH + 1,
                     figsize=(5 * (1 + NUM_NEIGH), 5 * len(query_filenames)))
for rowno, query_filename in enumerate(query_filenames):
  ax[rowno][0].imshow(read_and_decode(query_filename).numpy())
  ax[rowno][0].axis('off')
  for colno, neigh in enumerate(neighbors[rowno]):
    ax[rowno][colno+1].imshow(read_and_decode(dataset_filenames[neigh]).numpy())
    ax[rowno][colno+1].set_title('dist={:.2f}'.format(distances[rowno][colno].numpy()))
    ax[rowno][colno+1].axis('off')

import io
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds

test_dataset = (tf.data.TextLineDataset(
    "gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/flowers_5_jpeg/flower_photos/eval_set.csv").
    map(decode_csv)).map(lambda path, img, lint, ls: (img, lint)).take(NUM_IMAGES).batch(1)
test_results = model.predict(test_dataset)
np.savetxt("vecs.tsv", test_results, delimiter='\t')

out_m = io.open('meta.tsv', 'w', encoding='utf-8')
for img, labels in tfds.as_numpy(test_dataset):
    [out_m.write(CLASS_NAMES[x] + "\n") for x in labels]
out_m.close()
