12Chapter 12 · Image and Text Generation

Image and Text Generation

Ab tak humne images par kaam karne wale tareeke dekhe — classify karna, detect karna, ginna. Ab ulta karte hain — images ko generate karna. Lekin generate karne se pehle model ko samajhna hoga ki image me kya hai, aur iske liye embeddings ko naye tareeke se banana padega.

Embeddings ki problem

Transfer learning me embeddings ek bade labeled dataset par train kiye gaye classification model ki intermediate layer se milti hain. Isme do problems hain. Pehli, inke liye bada labeled dataset chahiye hota hai, aur woh embeddings sirf usi type ki images par achhe kaam karte hain — jaise internet ki photos par train kiye gaye embeddings machine parts ke diagrams ya satellite imagery par utne achhe nahi honge. Doosri, embeddings me sirf wohi information hoti hai jo label decide karne ke liye relevant hai — image ki baaki details prune ho jati hain. Agar hume aisi embedding chahiye jo har type ki image par kaam kare, bina bade labeled dataset ke, aur image ki poori information capture kare, to auxiliary learning task chahiye.

Auxiliary learning tasks

Auxiliary task matlab asli supervised problem se alag ek task, jiske liye bahut saara data aasani se available ho. Text me iska classic example hai agla word predict karna — is task par train kiye gaye model ki intermediate layer se word embeddings milti hain jo text classification jaise alag kaam me use hoti hain. Images ke liye aisa hi auxiliary task hai autoencoder — jahan input image hi apna label ban jati hai.

Autoencoders

Autoencoder me image ko ek network se pass karte hain jo usko pehle ek chhote internal vector me bottleneck karta hai aur phir wapas original size me expand karta hai. Input image hi label hoti hai, isliye yeh self-supervised hota hai — labeling ki zaroorat nahi, aur bahut zyada data par train kar sakte hain. Encoder aur decoder milkar hourglass shape banate hain — encoder har layer me dimensionality shrink karta hai, decoder expand karta hai, aur beech me sabse chhoti jagah hoti hai jise latent vector kehte hain. Yeh latent vector input ka concise representation hota hai, jahan se noise squeeze out hokar signal reh jata hai. Latent dimension ka size ek trade-off hai — bahut chhota hoga to signal kho jayega, bahut bada hoga to noise bhi encode ho jayega. Typical values 128, 256 ya 512 hoti hain.

Architecture aur reverse operations

MNIST handwritten digits par autoencoder ka encoder convolutional layers se 28x28 image ko 2-dimensional latent vector tak squeeze karta hai, aur decoder Conv2DTranspose layers se usko wapas image me expand karta hai. Autoencoder likhte time har layer ka reverse operation jaanna helpful hota hai — Dense ka reverse Dense hota hai, Flatten ka reverse Reshape, aur Conv2D ka reverse Conv2DTranspose hota hai. Upsampling2D bhi ek option hai, lekin usme trainable weights nahi hote — woh sirf pixel values repeat karta hai, jabki Conv2DTranspose kernel se deconvolve karta hai aur behtar upsampled image deta hai.

Training aur latent vectors

Encoder aur decoder ko chain karke train karte hain, loss hota hai input aur output image ke beech ka reconstruction error, jaise mean squared error. Train hone ke baad decoder ko hatakar sirf encoder use kar sakte hain — images ko latent vectors me convert karke classification aur clustering jaise downstream tasks me use kar sakte hain. Agar autoencoder nonlinear activations use karta hai to woh PCA se behtar hota hai, kyunki PCA sirf linear relationships capture karta hai. Similar images ke latent vectors ek saath cluster karte hain — jaise 1s, 2s aur 0s latent space ke alag-alag parts me hote hain.

Autoencoder se generation kyun fail hota hai

Decoder ko user ke diye gaye latent vector se image generate karne ko kaho to woh aksar fail hota hai, aur iske do reasons hain. Pehla, latent space me paas-paas ke do points bilkul alag images generate kar sakte hain — jaise ek triangle aur doosra circle — kyunki space ko organize karne ki koi koshish nahi ki gayi. Doosra, latent space me bade khaali regions hote hain jo kisi valid image se match nahi karte — wahan se random point lene par meaningless image banti hai. Autoencoder ki galti nahi hai — uska kaam sirf reconstruction tha, aur chhote isolated islands se woh kaam ho jata tha. Generation ke liye latent space ko organize aur regularize karna padega — aur yahi variational autoencoder karta hai.

Variational autoencoders (VAEs)

VAE me encoder latent vector ki jagah ek probability distribution ke parameters output karta hai — mean aur variance. Phir us distribution se sample karke decoder ko diya jata hai. Distribution ko standard normal ke paas rakhne ke liye loss me ek regularization term joda jata hai, jise Kullback-Leibler divergence kehte hain — yeh encoder ki distribution ko mean 0 aur standard deviation 1 wali standard normal distribution ke paas rehne par majboor karta hai. Isse latent space smooth aur overlapping bubbles se bhar jata hai — paas ke points similar images dete hain, aur kahin bhi random point lo to plausible image milti hai. Ek point se doosre ki taraf badhne par image smoothly interpolate hoti hai — jaise triangle dheere-dheere gol hokar circle ban jata hai. VAE ka decoder classic autoencoder jaisa hi hota hai, aur loss me reconstruction term ke saath KL divergence term hota hai. VAE discriminative models se alag hote hain — discriminative model sirf classes ke beech decision boundary seekhta hai, jabki generative model har class ki distribution ko explicitly model karta hai.

Yaad rakho: Autoencoder compression seekhta hai, VAE organized latent space seekhta hai — isliye sirf VAE ka decoder random latent vector se bhi samajhdaar image bana sakta hai.

# Import libraries and modules
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
np.set_printoptions(threshold=np.inf)

def plot_latent_space(decoder, n=30, ranges=[-1, 1, -1, 1], figsize=15):
    # display a n*n 2D manifold of digits
    digit_size = 28
    figure = np.zeros((digit_size * n, digit_size * n))
    # linearly spaced coordinates corresponding to the 2D plot
    # of digit classes in the latent space
    grid_x = np.linspace(ranges[0], ranges[1], n)
    grid_y = np.linspace(ranges[2], ranges[3], n)[::-1]

    for i, yi in enumerate(grid_y):
        for j, xi in enumerate(grid_x):
            z_sample = np.array([[xi, yi]])
            x_decoded = decoder.predict(z_sample)
            digit = x_decoded[0].reshape(digit_size, digit_size)
            figure[
                i * digit_size : (i + 1) * digit_size,
                j * digit_size : (j + 1) * digit_size,
            ] = digit

    plt.figure(figsize=(figsize, figsize))
    start_range = digit_size // 2
    end_range = n * digit_size + start_range
    pixel_range = np.arange(start_range, end_range, digit_size)
    sample_range_x = np.round(grid_x, 1)
    sample_range_y = np.round(grid_y, 1)
    plt.xticks(pixel_range, sample_range_x)
    plt.yticks(pixel_range, sample_range_y)
    plt.xlabel("z[0]")
    plt.ylabel("z[1]")
    plt.imshow(figure, cmap="Greys_r")
    plt.show()

def plot_label_clusters(encoder, data, labels, vae=True):
    # display a 2D plot of the digit classes in the latent space
    if vae:
      z_mean, _, _ = encoder.predict(data)
    else:
      z_mean = encoder.predict(data)
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
    plt.scatter(z_mean[:, 0], z_mean[:, 1], c=labels)
    plt.colorbar()
    for label in range(10): # mnist, 10 digits
        cx = np.mean(z_mean[labels == label, 0])
        cy = np.mean(z_mean[labels == label, 1])
        plt.text(cx, cy, str(label), color="white", fontsize=25, fontweight="bold")
    plt.xlabel("z[0]")
    plt.ylabel("z[1]")
    plt.show()

(x_train, _), (x_test, _) = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
mnist_digits = np.concatenate([x_train, x_test], axis=0)
mnist_digits = np.expand_dims(mnist_digits, -1).astype("float32") / 255

latent_dim = 2 # for easy visualization

encoder = tf.keras.Sequential([
    keras.Input(shape=(28, 28, 1), name="image_input"),
    layers.Conv2D(32, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="e_conv1"),
    layers.Conv2D(64, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="e_conv2"),
    layers.Flatten(name="e_flatten"),
    layers.Dense(latent_dim, name="e_dense")
], name="encoder")
encoder.summary()

decoder = tf.keras.Sequential([
    keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,), name="d_input"),
    layers.Dense(7 * 7 * 64, activation="relu", name="d_d1"),
    layers.Reshape((7, 7, 64), name="d_d2"),
    layers.Conv2DTranspose(32, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="d_conv1"),
    layers.Conv2DTranspose(1, 3, activation="sigmoid", strides=2, padding="same", name="d_conv2")
], name="decoder")
decoder.summary()

encoder_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(28, 28, 1), name="image_input")
x = encoder(encoder_inputs)
decoder_output = decoder(x)
autoencoder = keras.Model(encoder_inputs, decoder_output, name="autoencoder")
autoencoder.summary()

autoencoder.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(), loss='mse')
history = autoencoder.fit(mnist_digits, mnist_digits, epochs=30, batch_size=128)

(x_train, y_train), _ = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
x_train = np.expand_dims(x_train, -1).astype("float32") / 255
plot_label_clusters(encoder, x_train, y_train, vae=False)

plot_latent_space(decoder, n=30, ranges=[-2, 3, -3, 3], figsize=15)

12.1Chapter 12 · Image and Text Generation

GANs

VAE images recreate kar sakta hai, lekin bilkul nayi, perceptually real images banane me woh utna successful nahi hota. Iske liye sabse powerful tool hai generative adversarial network — GAN — jisme do networks ek-doosre ke against khelte hain aur ek-doosre ko behtar banate hain.

Generator aur discriminator ka khel

GAN me do neural networks hote hain. Generator random noise se realistic fake images banane ki koshish karta hai, aur discriminator real aur fake images me farq pehchanane ki koshish karta hai. Dono baari-baari train hote hain — jab ek train hota hai to doosre ke weights freeze rehte hain. Shuruaat me generator sirf random noise jaisi images banata hai aur discriminator bhi random guess karta hai. Dheere-dheere discriminator behtar hota hai, generator ko aur realistic banna padta hai, aur phir discriminator ko aur behtar hona padta hai. Yeh tab tak chalta hai jab tak convergence na ho jaye — jab generator itna achha ho jaye ki discriminator sirf random guess kar sake, matlab 50-50 odds. Ise Nash equilibrium kehte hain — agar ek network bahut jaldi dominate karne lage to doosra kabhi recover nahi kar pata.

Training ke steps

Discriminator training me pehle noise se generated images banate hain aur dataset se real images lete hain, dono ko discriminator se pass karte hain aur binary cross-entropy loss calculate karte hain — real images ko label 1 aur fake ko label 0 milta hai. One-sided label smoothing helpful hoti hai — real labels ko 1 ki jagah thoda kam karke discriminator ko overconfident hone se roka jata hai. Generator training me sirf generated images use hoti hain, lekin unko real ka label diya jata hai — generator ko discriminator ko dhokha dena hai, aur discriminator se mile gradients se woh apne weights update karta hai. Generator me LeakyReLU activation achhi kaam karti hai kyunki usme vanishing gradient problem nahi hoti aur negative inputs ki information bhi nahi khoti.

GAN improvements — DCGAN aur mode collapse

Practical me GANs train karna bahut mushkil hota hai — hyperparameters ke prati sensitive, unstable training aur kai failure modes hote hain. Sabse famous problem hai mode collapse — generator ko ek aisa output mil jata hai jo discriminator ko hara deta hai, aur woh baar-baar wahi kuch outputs banane lagta hai, diversity kho deta hai. Vanilla GAN me Dense layers use hoti hain, lekin images par convolutional layers behtar kaam karti hain — isliye deep convolutional GAN, ya DCGAN, me Dense layers ki jagah convolutional layers use hoti hain. Generator Conv2DTranspose se image ko upsample karta hai aur discriminator Conv2D se downsample karta hai, BatchNormalization aur LeakyReLU ke saath. Isse generated images kaafi behtar hoti hain.

Conditional GANs

Normal GAN me generator random digit banata hai lekin control nahi hota ki kaunsa digit bane. Conditional GAN me label ko extra input ke roop me dekar generation ko control kiya ja sakta hai. Generator me label ko embedding layer se dense vector me badalkar random noise vector ke saath concatenate karte hain. Discriminator me label ko image me convert karke input image ke saath concatenate karte hain. Training baaki same rehti hai, bas labels bhi pass karte hain. Inference time par desired label dekar specific digit generate kar sakte hain — jaise pehli row me saare zeros, doosri me saare ones. Conditional DCGAN se results aur bhi clean hote hain.

Image-to-image translation — CycleGAN aur Pix2Pix

Image translation me ek domain ki image ko doosre domain me badla jata hai — jaise ghode wali image ko zebra wali image me. Paired images milna mushkil hota hai, isliye CycleGAN unpaired images se kaam karta hai — isme do generators aur do discriminators hote hain jo cycle me chalte hain. Generator G horses ko zebras me badalta hai aur generator F zebras ko horses me, aur cycle consistency loss check karta hai ki image ko wapas laane par original image mile. Agar paired images hain to Pix2Pix use hota hai — isme U-Net generator hota hai jisme skip connections hote hain, aur PatchGAN discriminator hota hai jo poori image ki jagah chhote patches ko real ya fake classify karta hai. Pix2Pix se map view ko satellite view me badla ja sakta hai, ya hand-drawn sketch ko photographic quality wali image me.

Super-resolution aur inpainting

Super-resolution me low-resolution image ko high-resolution me upscale karte hain. Sabse purana tareeka bicubic interpolation hai, jo smooth aur blurry image deta hai. SRResNet residual blocks se kaafi behtar image banata hai, lekin uska MSE loss sirf average pixel error kam karta hai, perceptual quality nahi. SRGAN me GAN ka use hota hai — generator super-resolution image banata hai aur discriminator check karta hai ki woh high-resolution jaisi lagti hai ya nahi. Generator ki loss me adversarial loss ke saath VGG loss bhi hota hai, jo pretrained network ke feature maps ke beech ki distance hoti hai — isse image perceptually convincing banti hai. Inpainting me photo ka fata ya missing hissa bharna hota hai — context encoder ek area ko hatakar baaki image se woh hissa generate karta hai, reconstruction loss aur adversarial loss ke weighted sum se train hokar. Random blocks ya random regions ko mask karke train karna sirf center region se behtar generalize karta hai.

Yaad rakho: GAN ek khel hai — generator fake banata hai, discriminator pakadta hai, aur dono ek-doosre ko behtar banate hain. Control chahiye to conditional GAN, unpaired translation chahiye to CycleGAN, aur perceptual quality chahiye to adversarial loss ke saath content loss jodo.

# Import libraries and modules
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
print(np.__version__)
np.set_printoptions(threshold=np.inf)

# Create the generator.
latent_dim = 512
vanilla_generator = tf.keras.Sequential(
    [
        tf.keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,)),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=256),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=512),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1024),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=28 * 28 * 1, activation="tanh"),
        tf.keras.layers.Reshape(target_shape=(28, 28, 1))
    ],
    name="vanilla_generator"
)
vanilla_generator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=vanilla_generator,
    to_file="vanilla_generator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Create the discriminator.
vanilla_discriminator = tf.keras.Sequential(
    [
        tf.keras.Input(shape=(28, 28, 1)),
        tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1024),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=512),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=256),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1),
    ],
    name="vanilla_discriminator"
)
vanilla_discriminator.summary()

# Plot discriminator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=vanilla_discriminator,
    to_file="vanilla_discriminator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

class GAN(tf.keras.Model):
    """Custom model for training a GAN.

    Attributes:
        discriminator: Keras `Model`, the discriminator network.
        generator: Keras `Model`, the generator network.
        latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
        one_sided_label_smoothing: float, how much to smooth the real image
            labels by value in [0., 1.].
        discriminator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for
            discriminator network.
        generator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for generator
            network.
        loss_fn: Keras `Loss`, loss function for training both networks.
    """
    def __init__(
        self, discriminator, generator, latent_dim, one_sided_label_smoothing
    ):
        """Instantiates `GAN` model class.

        Args:
            discriminator: Keras `Model`, the discriminator network.
            generator: Keras `Model`, the generator network.
            latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
            one_sided_label_smoothing: float, how much to smooth the real image
                labels by value in [0., 1.].
        """
        super(GAN, self).__init__()
        self.discriminator = discriminator
        self.generator = generator
        self.latent_dim = latent_dim
        self.one_sided_label_smoothing = one_sided_label_smoothing

    def compile(self, discriminator_optimizer, generator_optimizer, loss_fn):
        """Overrides base `Model` class' compile method.

        Args:
            discriminator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for
                discriminator network.
            generator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for generator
                network.
            loss_fn: Keras `Loss`, loss function for training both networks.
        """
        super(GAN, self).compile()
        self.discriminator_optimizer = discriminator_optimizer
        self.generator_optimizer = generator_optimizer
        self.loss_fn = loss_fn

    def discriminator_train_step(self, batch_size, real_images):
        """Trains discriminator for one step.

        Args:
            batch_size: tensor, scalar tensor representing number of elements
                in the mini-batch.
            real_images: tensor, rank 4 tensor of real images with shape
                (batch_size, height, width, depth).

        Returns:
            discriminator_loss: tensor, scalar loss of disriminator step.
        """
        # Sample random points in the latent space.
        random_latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(
            shape=(batch_size, self.latent_dim)
        )

        # Generate images from noise.
        generated_images = self.generator(inputs=random_latent_vectors)

        # Combine generated images with real images.
        combined_images = tf.concat(
            values=[generated_images, real_images], axis=0
        )

        # Create fake and real labels.
        fake_labels = tf.zeros(shape=(batch_size, 1))
        real_labels = tf.ones(shape=(batch_size, 1))

        # Smooth real labels to help with training.
        real_labels *= self.one_sided_label_smoothing

        # Combine labels to be in-line with combined images.
        labels = tf.concat(
            values=[fake_labels, real_labels], axis=0
        )

        # Train ONLY the discriminator.
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            predictions = self.discriminator(inputs=combined_images)
            discriminator_loss = self.loss_fn(
                y_true=labels, y_pred=predictions
            )

        grads = tape.gradient(
            target=discriminator_loss,
            sources=self.discriminator.trainable_weights
        )

        self.discriminator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
            grads_and_vars=zip(grads, self.discriminator.trainable_weights)
        )

        return discriminator_loss

    def generator_train_step(self, batch_size):
        """Trains generator for one step.

        Args:
            batch_size: tensor, scalar tensor representing number of elements
                in the mini-batch.

        Returns:
            generator_loss: tensor, scalar loss of generator step.
        """
        # Sample random points in the latent space.
        random_latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(
            shape=(batch_size, self.latent_dim)
        )

        # Create labels as if they're real images.
        labels = tf.ones(shape=(batch_size, 1))

        # Train ONLY the generator.
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            predictions = self.discriminator(
                inputs=self.generator(inputs=random_latent_vectors)
            )
            generator_loss = self.loss_fn(y_true=labels, y_pred=predictions)

        grads = tape.gradient(
            target=generator_loss, sources=self.generator.trainable_weights
        )

        self.generator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
            grads_and_vars=zip(grads, self.generator.trainable_weights)
        )

        return generator_loss

    def train_step(self, real_images):
        """Trains `GAN` for one step.

        Args:
            real_images: tensor, rank 4 tensor of real images with shape
                (batch_size, height, width, depth).

        Returns:
            losses: dict, dictionary of losses from each sub-training step.
        """
        if isinstance(real_images, tuple):
            real_images = real_images[0]

        # Get dynamic batch size to use for random noise vectors.
        batch_size = tf.shape(input=real_images)[0]

        # First train discriminator.
        discriminator_loss = self.discriminator_train_step(
            batch_size, real_images
        )

        # Then train generator.
        generator_loss = self.generator_train_step(batch_size)

        losses = {
            "discriminator_loss": discriminator_loss,
            "generator_loss": generator_loss
        }

        return losses

def create_train_dataset(batch_size):
    """Creates training dataset.

    Args:
        batch_size: int, number of elements in a mini-batch.

    Returns:
        dataset: `Dataset`, dataset object for training using MNIST.
    """
    # Get and format MNIST data.
    (x_train, _), (x_test, _) = tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()

    # Let's combine both training and test sets.
    combined = np.concatenate([x_train, x_test])
    combined = (combined.astype("float32") - 127.5) / 255.0
    combined = np.reshape(combined, newshape=(-1, 28, 28, 1))

    # Create tf.data.Dataset for training.
    dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(tensors=combined)
    dataset = dataset.shuffle(buffer_size=70000).batch(batch_size=batch_size)

    return dataset

# Instantiate a GAN instance using our vanilla generator and discriminator.
vanilla_gan = GAN(
    discriminator=vanilla_discriminator,
    generator=vanilla_generator,
    latent_dim=latent_dim,
    one_sided_label_smoothing=0.9
)

vanilla_gan.compile(
    discriminator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    generator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    loss_fn=tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
)

# Train vanilla GAN model.
vanilla_gan_history = vanilla_gan.fit(
    create_train_dataset(batch_size=128), epochs=30
)

def plot_loss_history(history):
    """Plots loss history.

    Args:
        history: `keras.callbacks.History`, history object from training job.
    """
    plt.plot(history.history["generator_loss"])
    plt.plot(history.history["discriminator_loss"])
    plt.title("Training losses")
    plt.ylabel("Loss")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.legend(["generator", "discriminator"], loc="upper left")
    plt.show()

def plot_images(images):
    """Plots images.

    Args:
        images: np.array, array of images of
            [num_images, image_size, image_size, num_channels].
    """
    num_images = len(images)

    plt.figure(figsize=(20, 20))
    for i in range(num_images):
        image = images[i]
        plt.subplot(1, num_images, i + 1)
        plt.xticks([])
        plt.yticks([])
        plt.grid(False)
        plt.imshow(
            tf.reshape(image, image.shape[:-1]),
            cmap="gray_r"
        )
    plt.show()

plot_loss_history(history=vanilla_gan_history)

plot_images(
    images=vanilla_gan.generator(
        inputs=tf.random.normal(shape=(12, latent_dim))
    )
)

# Create the generator
def create_generator_block(filters, kernel_size, strides, padding, alpha):
    """Creates generator block of layers.

    Args:
        filters: int, number of output filters/channels.
        kernel_size: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of the kernel.
        strides: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of each stride of
            sliding window.
        padding: str, the type of padding of the output: same or valid.
        alpha: float, the amount of leakiness of LeakyRelu activations.

    Returns:
        List of layers.
    """
    return [
        tf.keras.layers.Conv2DTranspose(
            filters=filters,
            kernel_size=kernel_size,
            strides=strides,
            padding=padding
        ),
        tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=alpha)
    ]

def create_dcgan_generator(latent_dim):
    """Creates deep convolutional GAN generator network.

    Args:
        latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.

    Returns:
        Keras Sequential Model.
    """
    dcgan_generator = [
        tf.keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,)),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=7 * 7 * 256),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2),
        tf.keras.layers.Reshape(target_shape=(7, 7, 256)),
    ] + create_generator_block(
        filters=128, kernel_size=4, strides=2, padding="same", alpha=0.2
    ) + create_generator_block(
        filters=128, kernel_size=4, strides=2, padding="same", alpha=0.2
    ) + [
        tf.keras.layers.Conv2DTranspose(
            filters=1,
            kernel_size=3,
            strides=1,
            padding="same",
            activation="tanh"
        )
    ]

    return tf.keras.Sequential(layers=dcgan_generator, name="dcgan_generator")

dcgan_generator = create_dcgan_generator(latent_dim=512)
dcgan_generator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=dcgan_generator,
    to_file="dcgan_generator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Create the discriminator
def create_discriminator_block(filters, kernel_size, strides, padding, alpha):
    """Creates discriminator block of layers.

    Args:
        filters: int, number of output filters/channels.
        kernel_size: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of the kernel.
        strides: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of each stride of
            sliding window.
        padding: str, the type of padding of the output: same or valid.
        alpha: float, the amount of leakiness of LeakyRelu activations.

    Returns:
        List of layers.
    """
    return [
        tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
            filters=filters,
            kernel_size=kernel_size,
            strides=strides,
            padding=padding
        ),
        tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization(),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=alpha)
    ]

def create_dcgan_discriminator(input_shape):
    """Creates deep convolutional GAN discriminator network.

    Args:
        input_shape: tuple, the shape of the input without batch dimension.

    Returns:
        Keras Sequential Model.
    """
    dcgan_discriminator = [
        tf.keras.Input(shape=input_shape),
        tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
            filters=64, kernel_size=3, strides=1, padding="same"
        ),
        tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)
    ] + create_discriminator_block(
        filters=128, kernel_size=3, strides=2, padding="same", alpha=0.2
    ) + create_discriminator_block(
        filters=128, kernel_size=3, strides=2, padding="same", alpha=0.2
    ) + create_discriminator_block(
        filters=256, kernel_size=3, strides=2, padding="same", alpha=0.2
    ) + [
        tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),
        tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1)
    ]

    return tf.keras.Sequential(layers=dcgan_discriminator, name="dcgan_discriminator")

dcgan_discriminator = create_dcgan_discriminator(input_shape=(28, 28, 1))
dcgan_discriminator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=dcgan_discriminator,
    to_file="dcgan_discriminator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Instantiate a GAN instance using our DCGAN generator and discriminator.
dcgan = GAN(
    discriminator=dcgan_discriminator,
    generator=dcgan_generator,
    latent_dim=latent_dim,
    one_sided_label_smoothing=0.9
)

dcgan.compile(
    discriminator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    generator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    loss_fn=tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
)

# Train DCGAN model.
dcgan_history = dcgan.fit(create_train_dataset(batch_size=128), epochs=50)

plot_loss_history(history=dcgan_history)

plot_images(
    images=dcgan.generator(inputs=tf.random.normal(shape=(12, latent_dim)))
)

import tensorflow as tf
print(tf.version.VERSION)
device_name = tf.test.gpu_device_name()
if device_name != '/device:GPU:0':
    raise SystemError('GPU device not found')

# Import libraries and modules
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
print(np.__version__)
np.set_printoptions(threshold=np.inf)

IMAGE_SHAPE = (28, 28, 1)
NUM_CLASSES = 10
LATENT_DIM = 512

# Create the generator.
def create_label_vectors(
    labels, num_classes, embedding_dim, dense_units
):
    """Creates label vectors from label indices.

    Args:
        labels: tensor, rank 1 tensor of labels with shape (batch_size,).
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.
        embedding_dim: int, the embedding's output dimension.
        dense_units: int, the number of units for `Dense` layer.

    Returns:
        label_vectors: tensor, rank 2 tensor of shape
            (batch_size, dense_units).
    """
    embedded_labels = tf.keras.layers.Embedding(
        input_dim=num_classes, output_dim=embedding_dim
    )(inputs=labels)
    label_vectors = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
        units=dense_units
    )(inputs=embedded_labels)

    return label_vectors

def standard_vanilla_generator(inputs, output_shape):
    """Returns output of standard vanilla generator layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape (batch_size, y, x, channels).
        output_shape: tuple, the shape of the output without batch dimension.

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, depth).
    """
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=64)(inputs=inputs)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=128)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=256)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
        units=output_shape[0] * output_shape[1] * output_shape[2],
        activation="tanh"
    )(inputs=x)

    outputs = tf.keras.layers.Reshape(target_shape=output_shape)(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def create_vanilla_generator(latent_dim, num_classes, output_shape):
    """Creates vanilla conditional GAN generator model.

    Args:
        latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.
        output_shape: tuple, the shape of the output without batch dimension.

    Returns:
        Keras Functional Model.
    """
    latent_vector = tf.keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,))

    labels = tf.keras.Input(shape=())
    label_vectors = create_label_vectors(
        labels, num_classes, embedding_dim=50, dense_units=50
    )

    concatenated_inputs = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate(
        axis=-1
    )(inputs=[latent_vector, label_vectors])
    
    outputs = standard_vanilla_generator(
        inputs=concatenated_inputs, output_shape=output_shape
    )

    return tf.keras.Model(
        inputs=[latent_vector, labels],
        outputs=outputs,
        name="vanilla_generator"
    )

vanilla_generator = create_vanilla_generator(
    latent_dim=LATENT_DIM, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES, output_shape=IMAGE_SHAPE
)
vanilla_generator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=vanilla_generator,
    to_file="conditional_vanilla_generator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Create the discriminator.
def create_label_images(
    labels, num_classes, embedding_dim, image_shape
):
    """Creates label images from label indices.

    Args:
        labels: tensor, rank 1 tensor of labels with shape (batch_size,).
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.
        embedding_dim: int, the embedding's output dimension.
        image_shape: tuple, the shape of the image without batch dimension.

    Returns:
        label_image: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, 1).
    """
    embedded_labels = tf.keras.layers.Embedding(
        input_dim=num_classes, output_dim=embedding_dim
    )(inputs=labels)
    num_pixels = image_shape[0] * image_shape[1]
    dense_labels = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
        units=num_pixels
    )(inputs=embedded_labels)
    label_image = tf.keras.layers.Reshape(
        target_shape=(image_shape[0], image_shape[1], 1)
    )(inputs=dense_labels)

    return label_image

def standard_vanilla_discriminator(inputs):
    """Returns output of standard vanilla discriminator layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape (batch_size, y, x, channels).

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, depth).
    """
    x = tf.keras.layers.Flatten()(inputs=inputs)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=256)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=128)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=64)(inputs=x)
    x = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=0.2)(inputs=x)

    outputs = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1)(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def create_vanilla_discriminator(image_shape, num_classes):
    """Creates vanilla conditional GAN discriminator model.

    Args:
        image_shape: tuple, the shape of the image without batch dimension.
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.

    Returns:
        Keras Functional Model.
    """
    images = tf.keras.Input(shape=image_shape)

    labels = tf.keras.Input(shape=())
    label_image = create_label_images(
        labels, num_classes, embedding_dim=50, image_shape=image_shape
    )

    concatenated_inputs = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate(
        axis=-1
    )(inputs=[images, label_image])

    outputs = standard_vanilla_discriminator(inputs=concatenated_inputs)

    return tf.keras.Model(
        inputs=[images, labels],
        outputs=outputs,
        name="vanilla_discriminator"
    )

vanilla_discriminator = create_vanilla_discriminator(
    image_shape=IMAGE_SHAPE, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES
)
vanilla_discriminator.summary()

# Plot discriminator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=vanilla_discriminator,
    to_file="conditional_vanilla_discriminator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

class GAN(tf.keras.Model):
    """Custom model for training a GAN.

    Attributes:
        discriminator: Keras `Model`, the discriminator network.
        generator: Keras `Model`, the generator network.
        latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
        one_sided_label_smoothing: float, how much to smooth the real image
            labels by value in [0., 1.].
        discriminator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for
            discriminator network.
        generator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for generator
            network.
        loss_fn: Keras `Loss`, loss function for training both networks.
    """
    def __init__(
        self, discriminator, generator, latent_dim, one_sided_label_smoothing
    ):
        """Instantiates `GAN` model class.

        Args:
            discriminator: Keras `Model`, the discriminator network.
            generator: Keras `Model`, the generator network.
            latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
            one_sided_label_smoothing: float, how much to smooth the real image
                labels by value in [0., 1.].
        """
        super(GAN, self).__init__()
        self.discriminator = discriminator
        self.generator = generator
        self.latent_dim = latent_dim
        self.one_sided_label_smoothing = one_sided_label_smoothing

    def compile(self, discriminator_optimizer, generator_optimizer, loss_fn):
        """Overrides base `Model` class' compile method.

        Args:
            discriminator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for
                discriminator network.
            generator_optimizer: Keras `Optimizer`, optimizer for generator
                network.
            loss_fn: Keras `Loss`, loss function for training both networks.
        """
        super(GAN, self).compile()
        self.discriminator_optimizer = discriminator_optimizer
        self.generator_optimizer = generator_optimizer
        self.loss_fn = loss_fn

    def discriminator_train_step(self, batch_size, real_images, input_labels):
        """Trains discriminator for one step.

        Args:
            batch_size: tensor, scalar tensor representing number of elements
                in the mini-batch.
            real_images: tensor, rank 4 tensor of real images with shape
                (batch_size, height, width, depth).
            input_labels: tensor, rank 1 tensor of labels with shape (batch_size,).

        Returns:
            discriminator_loss: tensor, scalar loss of disriminator step.
        """
        # Sample random points in the latent space.
        random_latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(
            shape=(batch_size, self.latent_dim)
        )

        # Generate images from noise.
        generated_images = self.generator(
            inputs=[random_latent_vectors, input_labels]
        )

        # Combine generated images with real images.
        combined_images = tf.concat(
            values=[generated_images, real_images], axis=0
        )

        # Create fake and real labels.
        fake_labels = tf.zeros(shape=(batch_size, 1))
        real_labels = tf.ones(shape=(batch_size, 1))

        # Smooth real labels to help with training.
        real_labels *= self.one_sided_label_smoothing

        # Combine labels to be in-line with combined images.
        labels = tf.concat(
            values=[fake_labels, real_labels], axis=0
        )

        # Train ONLY the discriminator.
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            predictions = self.discriminator(
                inputs=[
                    combined_images,
                    tf.concat(values=[input_labels, input_labels], axis=0)
                ]
            )
            discriminator_loss = self.loss_fn(
                y_true=labels, y_pred=predictions
            )

        grads = tape.gradient(
            target=discriminator_loss,
            sources=self.discriminator.trainable_weights
        )

        self.discriminator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
            grads_and_vars=zip(grads, self.discriminator.trainable_weights)
        )

        return discriminator_loss

    def generator_train_step(self, batch_size, input_labels):
        """Trains generator for one step.

        Args:
            batch_size: tensor, scalar tensor representing number of elements
                in the mini-batch.
            input_labels: tensor, rank 1 tensor of labels with shape (batch_size,).

        Returns:
            generator_loss: tensor, scalar loss of generator step.
        """
        # Sample random points in the latent space.
        random_latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(
            shape=(batch_size, self.latent_dim)
        )

        # Create labels as if they're real images.
        labels = tf.ones(shape=(batch_size, 1))

        # Train ONLY the generator.
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            fake_images = self.generator(
                inputs=[random_latent_vectors, input_labels]
            )
            predictions = self.discriminator(
                inputs=[fake_images, input_labels]
            )
            generator_loss = self.loss_fn(y_true=labels, y_pred=predictions)

        grads = tape.gradient(
            target=generator_loss, sources=self.generator.trainable_weights
        )

        self.generator_optimizer.apply_gradients(
            grads_and_vars=zip(grads, self.generator.trainable_weights)
        )

        return generator_loss

    def train_step(self, features):
        """Trains `GAN` for one step.

        Args:
            features: dict, images key has rank 4 tensor of real images with
                shape (batch_size, height, width, depth) for value and labels
                key has rank 1 tensor of labels with shape (batch_size,).

        Returns:
            losses: dict, dictionary of losses from each sub-training step.
        """
        real_images = features["images"]
        input_labels = features["labels"]

        # Get dynamic batch size to use for random noise vectors.
        batch_size = tf.shape(input=real_images)[0]

        # First train discriminator.
        discriminator_loss = self.discriminator_train_step(
            batch_size, real_images, input_labels
        )

        # Then train generator.
        generator_loss = self.generator_train_step(
            batch_size, input_labels
        )

        losses = {
            "discriminator_loss": discriminator_loss,
            "generator_loss": generator_loss
        }

        return losses

def create_train_dataset(batch_size):
    """Creates training dataset.

    Args:
        batch_size: int, number of elements in a mini-batch.

    Returns:
        dataset: `Dataset`, dataset object for training using MNIST.
    """
    # Get and format MNIST data.
    (x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()

    # Let's combine both training and test sets.
    combined_images = np.concatenate([x_train, x_test])
    combined_images = (combined_images.astype("float32") - 127.5) / 255.0
    combined_images = np.reshape(combined_images, newshape=(-1, 28, 28, 1))

    combined_labels = np.concatenate([y_train, y_test])

    # Create tf.data.Dataset for training.
    dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices(
        tensors={"images": combined_images, "labels": combined_labels}
    )
    dataset = dataset.shuffle(buffer_size=70000).batch(batch_size=batch_size)

    return dataset

# Instantiate a GAN instance using our vanilla generator and discriminator.
vanilla_gan = GAN(
    discriminator=vanilla_discriminator,
    generator=vanilla_generator,
    latent_dim=LATENT_DIM,
    one_sided_label_smoothing=0.9
)

vanilla_gan.compile(
    discriminator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    generator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    loss_fn=tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
)

# Train vanilla GAN model.
vanilla_gan_history = vanilla_gan.fit(
    create_train_dataset(batch_size=128), epochs=30
)

def plot_loss_history(history):
    """Plots loss history.

    Args:
        history: `keras.callbacks.History`, history object from training job.
    """
    plt.plot(history.history["generator_loss"])
    plt.plot(history.history["discriminator_loss"])
    plt.title("Training losses")
    plt.ylabel("Loss")
    plt.xlabel("Epoch")
    plt.legend(["generator", "discriminator"], loc="upper left")
    plt.show()

def plot_images(images):
    """Plots images.

    Args:
        images: np.array, array of images of
            [num_images, image_size, image_size, num_channels].
    """
    num_images = len(images)

    plt.figure(figsize=(20, 20))
    for i in range(num_images):
        image = images[i]
        plt.subplot(1, num_images, i + 1)
        plt.xticks([])
        plt.yticks([])
        plt.grid(False)
        plt.imshow(
            tf.reshape(image, image.shape[:-1]),
            cmap="gray_r"
        )
    plt.show()

plot_loss_history(history=vanilla_gan_history)

num_examples = 12
latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(shape=(num_examples, LATENT_DIM))
for i in range(10):
    labels = tf.ones(shape=num_examples, dtype=tf.int32) * i
    plot_images(
        images=vanilla_gan.generator(
            inputs=[latent_vectors, labels]
        )
    )

# Create the generator
def project_latent_vector(latent_vector, projection_shape):
    """Projects latent vector into an image.

    Args:
        latent_vector: tensor, rank 2 tensor of labels with shape
            (batch_size, latent_dim).
        projection_shape: 3-tuple, the shape to project vector into an image.

    Returns:
        latent_image: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape
            (
                batch_size,
                projection_shape[0],
                projection_shape[1],
                projection_shape[2]
            ).
    """
    projected_latents = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
        units=projection_shape[0] * projection_shape[1] * projection_shape[2]
    )(inputs=latent_vector)
    projected_latents = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(
        alpha=0.2
    )(inputs=projected_latents)
    latent_image = tf.keras.layers.Reshape(
        target_shape=projection_shape
    )(inputs=projected_latents)

    return latent_image

def create_generator_block(
    inputs, filters, kernel_size, strides, padding, alpha
):
    """Creates generator block of layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 image tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, channels).
        filters: int, number of output filters/channels.
        kernel_size: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of the kernel.
        strides: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of each stride of
            sliding window.
        padding: str, the type of padding of the output: same or valid.
        alpha: float, the amount of leakiness of LeakyRelu activations.

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 4 image tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height * 2, width * 2, filters).
    """
    x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        filters=filters,
        kernel_size=kernel_size,
        strides=strides,
        padding=padding
    )(inputs=inputs)
    x = tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization()(inputs=x)
    outputs = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=alpha)(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def standard_DCGAN_generator(inputs):
    """Returns output of standard DCGAN generator layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape (batch_size, y, x, channels).

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, depth).
    """
    x = create_generator_block(
        inputs=inputs,
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        alpha=0.2
    )

    x = create_generator_block(
        inputs=x,
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=4,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        alpha=0.2
    )

    outputs = tf.keras.layers.Conv2DTranspose(
        filters=1, kernel_size=3, strides=1, padding="same", activation="tanh"
    )(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def create_dcgan_generator(latent_dim, num_classes):
    """Creates deep convolutional conditional GAN generator model.

    Args:
        latent_dim: int, the latent vector dimension length.
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.

    Returns:
        Keras Functional Model.
    """
    projection_shape = (7, 7, 256)

    latent_vector = tf.keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,))
    latent_image = project_latent_vector(latent_vector, projection_shape)
    
    labels = tf.keras.Input(shape=())
    label_image = create_label_images(
        labels=labels,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        embedding_dim=50,
        image_shape=projection_shape
    )

    concatenated_inputs = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate(
        axis=-1
    )(inputs=[latent_image, label_image])

    outputs = standard_DCGAN_generator(inputs=concatenated_inputs)

    return tf.keras.Model(
        inputs=[latent_vector, labels],
        outputs=outputs,
        name="dcgan_generator"
    )

dcgan_generator = create_dcgan_generator(
    latent_dim=LATENT_DIM, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES
)
dcgan_generator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=dcgan_generator,
    to_file="conditional_dcgan_generator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Create the discriminator
def create_discriminator_block(
    inputs, filters, kernel_size, strides, padding, alpha
):
    """Creates discriminator block of layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 image tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height, width, channels).
        filters: int, number of output filters/channels.
        kernel_size: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of the kernel.
        strides: int/2-tuple of ints, the height and width of each stride of
            sliding window.
        padding: str, the type of padding of the output: same or valid.
        alpha: float, the amount of leakiness of LeakyRelu activations.

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 4 image tensor of shape
            (batch_size, height // 2, width // 2, filters).
    """
    x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
        filters=filters,
        kernel_size=kernel_size,
        strides=strides,
        padding=padding
    )(inputs=inputs)
    x = tf.keras.layers.BatchNormalization()(inputs=x)
    outputs = tf.keras.layers.LeakyReLU(alpha=alpha)(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def standard_DCGAN_discriminator(inputs):
    """Returns output of standard DCGAN discriminator layers.

    Args:
        inputs: tensor, rank 4 tensor of shape (batch_size, y, x, channels).

    Returns:
        outputs: tensor, rank 2 tensor of shape (batch_size, 1).
    """
    x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
        filters=64, kernel_size=3, strides=1, padding="same"
    )(inputs=inputs)

    x = create_discriminator_block(
        inputs=x,
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=3,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        alpha=0.2
    )

    x = create_discriminator_block(
        inputs=x,
        filters=128,
        kernel_size=3,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        alpha=0.2
    )

    x = create_discriminator_block(
        inputs=x,
        filters=256,
        kernel_size=3,
        strides=2,
        padding="same",
        alpha=0.2
    )

    x = tf.keras.layers.Flatten()(inputs=x)
    outputs = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units=1)(inputs=x)

    return outputs

def create_dcgan_discriminator(image_shape, num_classes):
    """Creates deep convolutional conditional GAN discriminator model.

    Args:
        image_shape: tuple, the shape of the image without batch dimension.
        num_classes: int, the number of image classes.

    Returns:
        Keras Functional Model.
    """
    images = tf.keras.Input(shape=image_shape)

    labels = tf.keras.Input(shape=())
    label_image = create_label_images(
        labels=labels,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        embedding_dim=50,
        image_shape=image_shape
    )

    concatenated_inputs = tf.keras.layers.Concatenate(
        axis=-1
    )(inputs=[images, label_image])

    outputs = standard_DCGAN_discriminator(inputs=concatenated_inputs)

    return tf.keras.Model(
        inputs=[images, labels],
        outputs=outputs,
        name="dcgan_discriminator"
    )

dcgan_discriminator = create_dcgan_discriminator(
    image_shape=IMAGE_SHAPE, num_classes=NUM_CLASSES
)
dcgan_discriminator.summary()

# Plot generator model.
tf.keras.utils.plot_model(
    model=dcgan_discriminator,
    to_file="conditional_dcgan_discriminator_model.png",
    show_shapes=True,
    show_layer_names=True
)

# Instantiate a GAN instance using our DCGAN generator and discriminator.
dcgan = GAN(
    discriminator=dcgan_discriminator,
    generator=dcgan_generator,
    latent_dim=LATENT_DIM,
    one_sided_label_smoothing=0.9
)

dcgan.compile(
    discriminator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    generator_optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(
        learning_rate=0.0002, beta_1=0.5, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8
    ),
    loss_fn=tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True)
)

# Train DCGAN model.
dcgan_history = dcgan.fit(create_train_dataset(batch_size=128), epochs=50)

plot_loss_history(history=dcgan_history)

num_examples = 12
latent_vectors = tf.random.normal(shape=(num_examples, LATENT_DIM))
for i in range(10):
    labels = tf.ones(shape=num_examples, dtype=tf.int32) * i
    plot_images(
        images=dcgan.generator(
            inputs=[latent_vectors, labels]
        )
    )

12.2Chapter 12 · Image and Text Generation

Anomaly Detection & Deepfakes

Normal kya hota hai, yeh seekh lo to abnormal apne aap pakda jayega — aur wahi image jo normal distribution me fit nahi hoti, wohi anomaly hai. Lekin is simple idea ke peeche GANs ka poora khel chhupa hai, aur usi technology ka galat istemal deepfakes me bhi hota hai.

Anomaly detection ka basic idea

Anomaly detection ke use cases bahut hain — nakli currency pehchanana ya medical scans me tumor dhoondhna. Aksar labeled data kam hota hai aur labeling me expert knowledge chahiye hoti hai, isliye supervised approach possible nahi hota — unsupervised approach chahiye. Standard method teen phases me hota hai — pehle sirf normal images se seekho ki normal ko reconstruct kaise karte hain, phir normal images ke reconstruction errors ki distribution seekho, aur aakhir me ek distance threshold set karo jisse upar ki har cheez anomalous flag ho. Sabse important rule hai — model ko sirf normal data par train karo. Agar normal data me anomalies mil gayi to model unhe bhi normal samajh lega aur inference par asli anomalies miss ho jayengi, false negatives badh jayenge.

Autoencoder se anomaly detection

Autoencoder se normal images ko compress karke reconstruct karte hain — reconstruction kabhi perfect nahi hota, hamesha kuch error rehta hai. Normal images ke errors ek distribution banate hain. Agar model ko anomalous image di jaye — jaisi usne training me kabhi dekhi hi nahi — to woh usko sahi se compress aur reconstruct nahi kar payega aur reconstruction error normal distribution se bahut bahar hoga. Bas, image anomalous flag ho gayi. Isse ek kadam aage hai anomaly localization — poori image ki jagah har pixel ko flag karna. Har pixel ka apna error hota hai, aur threshold se upar wale pixels anomalous hote hain — yeh unsupervised segmentation jaisa hai.

GAN kyun zaroori hai

Sirf autoencoder aur reconstruction loss se ek problem hoti hai — model kisi bhi image ko khud me map karna seekh sakta hai, normal manifold seekhne ki jagah. Tab normal aur anomalous dono images ka reconstruction error similar hoga aur detection fail ho jayega. Isliye GAN use hota hai — generator aur discriminator ke saath, kabhi-kabhi extra encoder-decoder networks bhi. Generator autoencoder ya U-Net ho sakta hai, discriminator image ko compress karke logits banata hai. Loss me kai terms hote hain — reconstruction loss, adversarial loss, aur latent loss jo discriminator ki intermediate layer ke feature maps ke beech ki distance hoti hai. Adversarial loss ensure karta hai ki generator ne normal images ka manifold seekha hai. Trained generator normal image ko lagbhag waisa ka waisa reconstruct karta hai, lekin anomalous image me anomalies ko paint out karke woh image bana deta hai jo uske hisaab se bina anomaly ke honi chahiye — isliye error bahut bada hota hai aur anomaly sahi se pakdi jati hai.

Deepfakes kaise bante hain

Deepfakes me existing image ya video me ek insaan ya object ko doosre se replace kar diya jata hai. Iske liye autoencoders ya GANs use hote hain. Ek tareeka hai ek encoder aur do decoders banana — pehle insaan ke chehre ko distort karke encoder se pass karte hain aur pehle decoder se reconstruct karte hain, phir doosre insaan ke chehre ko usi encoder se pass karke doosre decoder se reconstruct karte hain. Baar-baar repeat karne par pehla decoder pehle insaan ke chehre me expert ho jata hai aur doosra doosre ke chehre me. Inference time par pehle insaan ki image ko encoder se pass karke doosre decoder se nikaalo to pehle insaan ka chehra doosre ke chehre me badal jata hai. Adversarial loss ke liye discriminator jodne se image quality aur behtar hoti hai. Aaj to sirf ek hi source image se bhi deepfake banaye ja sakte hain — lekin achhe results ke liye bahut saara data chahiye hota hai.

Deepfakes ka risk

Deepfakes par nazar rakhna zaroori hai kyunki inka galat istemal political ya financial fayde ke liye ho sakta hai — jaise kisi neta ko aisi baat kehte hue dikhana jo usne kabhi kahi hi nahi. Isliye deepfakes ko detect karne par bhi bahut active research chal rahi hai. Technology seekhte time yeh yaad rakhna zaroori hai ki powerful generation tools ka istemal hamesha responsibly karna chahiye.

Yaad rakho: Anomaly detection me model ko sirf normal data par train karo aur reconstruction error ka threshold use karo — aur yaad rakho ki wahi generation technology jo anomalies pakadti hai, deepfakes bhi bana sakti hai.

# Import libraries and modules
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
np.set_printoptions(threshold=np.inf)

def plot_latent_space(decoder, n=30, ranges=[-1, 1, -1, 1], figsize=15):
    # display a n*n 2D manifold of digits
    digit_size = 28
    figure = np.zeros((digit_size * n, digit_size * n))
    # linearly spaced coordinates corresponding to the 2D plot
    # of digit classes in the latent space
    grid_x = np.linspace(ranges[0], ranges[1], n)
    grid_y = np.linspace(ranges[2], ranges[3], n)[::-1]

    for i, yi in enumerate(grid_y):
        for j, xi in enumerate(grid_x):
            z_sample = np.array([[xi, yi]])
            x_decoded = decoder.predict(z_sample)
            digit = x_decoded[0].reshape(digit_size, digit_size)
            figure[
                i * digit_size : (i + 1) * digit_size,
                j * digit_size : (j + 1) * digit_size,
            ] = digit

    plt.figure(figsize=(figsize, figsize))
    start_range = digit_size // 2
    end_range = n * digit_size + start_range
    pixel_range = np.arange(start_range, end_range, digit_size)
    sample_range_x = np.round(grid_x, 1)
    sample_range_y = np.round(grid_y, 1)
    plt.xticks(pixel_range, sample_range_x)
    plt.yticks(pixel_range, sample_range_y)
    plt.xlabel("z[0]")
    plt.ylabel("z[1]")
    plt.imshow(figure, cmap="Greys_r")
    plt.show()

def plot_label_clusters(encoder, data, labels, vae=True):
    # display a 2D plot of the digit classes in the latent space
    if vae:
      z_mean, _, _ = encoder.predict(data)
    else:
      z_mean = encoder.predict(data)
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
    plt.scatter(z_mean[:, 0], z_mean[:, 1], c=labels)
    plt.colorbar()
    for label in range(10): # mnist, 10 digits
        cx = np.mean(z_mean[labels == label, 0])
        cy = np.mean(z_mean[labels == label, 1])
        plt.text(cx, cy, str(label), color="white", fontsize=25, fontweight="bold")
    plt.xlabel("z[0]")
    plt.ylabel("z[1]")
    plt.show()

(x_train, _), (x_test, _) = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
mnist_digits = np.concatenate([x_train, x_test], axis=0)
mnist_digits = np.expand_dims(mnist_digits, -1).astype("float32") / 255

class Sampling(layers.Layer):
    """Uses (z_mean, z_log_var) to sample z, the vector encoding a digit."""

    def call(self, z_mean, z_log_var):
        batch = tf.shape(z_mean)[0]
        dim = tf.shape(z_mean)[1]
        epsilon = tf.random.normal(shape=(batch, dim))
        return z_mean + tf.exp(0.5 * z_log_var) * epsilon

latent_dim = 2 # for easy visualization

encoder_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(28, 28, 1), name="image_input")
x = layers.Conv2D(32, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="e_conv1")(encoder_inputs)
x = layers.Conv2D(64, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="e_conv2")(x)
x = layers.Flatten(name="e_flatten")(x)

z_mean = layers.Dense(latent_dim, name="z_mean")(x) # the autoencoder output
z_log_var = layers.Dense(latent_dim, name="z_log_var")(x)
z = Sampling()(z_mean, z_log_var)

encoder = keras.Model(encoder_inputs, [z_mean, z_log_var, z], name="encoder")
encoder.summary()

latent_inputs = keras.Input(shape=(latent_dim,), name="d_input")
x = layers.Dense(7 * 7 * 64, activation="relu", name="d_d1")(latent_inputs)
x = layers.Reshape((7, 7, 64), name="d_d2")(x)
x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(32, 3, activation="relu", strides=2, padding="same", name="d_conv1")(x)
decoder_outputs = layers.Conv2DTranspose(1, 3, activation="sigmoid", strides=2, padding="same", name="d_conv2")(x)
decoder = keras.Model(latent_inputs, decoder_outputs, name="decoder")
decoder.summary()

def kl_divergence(z_mean, z_log_var):
    kl_loss = -0.5 * (1 + z_log_var - tf.square(z_mean) - tf.exp(z_log_var))
    return tf.reduce_mean(tf.reduce_sum(kl_loss, axis=1))
encoder.add_loss(kl_divergence(z_mean, z_log_var))

z_mean, z_log_var, z = encoder(encoder_inputs) # 3 outputs now
decoder_output = decoder(z)
vae = keras.Model(encoder_inputs, decoder_output, name="vae")
vae.summary()

def reconstruction_loss(real, reconstruction):
  return tf.reduce_mean(
      tf.reduce_sum(
          keras.losses.binary_crossentropy(real, reconstruction), axis=(1, 2)
      )
  )

vae.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(), loss=reconstruction_loss, metrics=["mse"])

history = vae.fit(mnist_digits, mnist_digits, epochs=30, batch_size=128)

(x_train, y_train), _ = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()
x_train = np.expand_dims(x_train, -1).astype("float32") / 255
plot_label_clusters(encoder, x_train, y_train, vae=True)

plot_latent_space(decoder, n=30, ranges=[-2, 3, -3, 3], figsize=15)

12.3Chapter 12 · Image and Text Generation

Image Captioning

Image se text generate karna — jaise photo dekhkar ek line me batana ki usme kya ho raha hai — yeh image captioning hai. Yeh visually impaired logon ke liye image descriptions, social media ki accessibility aur museum audio guides jaise kaamo me use hoti hai.

Architecture — encoder aur decoder

Image captioning ek asymmetric transformation problem hai — encoder images par kaam karta hai aur decoder text generate karta hai. Typical approach me image encoder ke liye Inception jaisa convolutional model use hota hai jo image ko embeddings me badalta hai, aur caption decoder ke liye ek language model use hota hai jo sequence generate karta hai. Do concepts samajhna zaroori hai — attention aur GRU. Attention se model seekhta hai ki caption ke har word ke liye image ke kis hisse par focus karna hai — jaise frisbee word predict karte time model frisbee wale hisse par dhyaan deta hai. GRU cell sequence model ka basic building block hai — language model ko yaad rakhna padta hai ki usne pehle kaunse words predict kiye, isliye state ek step se doosre step tak pass hoti hai aur ek step ka output agle step ka input banta hai.

Dataset — COCO captions

Captioning model train karne ke liye images aur unke captions wala dataset chahiye hota hai — COCO captions dataset aisa hi ek bada corpus hai, jisme har image ke multiple captions hote hain. Images alag-alag sizes ki hoti hain, isliye unko ek fixed size me resize karte hain — jaise Inception model ke liye 299x299 — aur model ki preprocessing apply karte hain.

Captions ko tokenize karna

Caption ko model ke liye numbers me badalna padta hai. Pehle punctuation hatate hain, lowercase karte hain, words me todte hain, unusual words hatate hain, aur shuruaat aur ant me special tokens jodte hain — jaise start aur end. Phir saare captions ko ek hi length tak pad karte hain taaki batching ho sake. Tokenizer se word-to-index lookup table banti hai, jisse dono directions me convert kiya ja sakta hai — word se id aur id se word.

Batching ki mushkil

Har image ke paanch tak captions ho sakte hain, isliye ek image se paanch tak feature-label pairs ban sakte hain. Isliye seedha dataset ko batch nahi kar sakte — pehle generator se image-caption pairs banane padte hain, har caption ke liye image repeat karke, aur phir un pairs ko batch karte hain. Yeh step miss ho jaye to batch sizes inconsistent ho jayenge.

Captioning model — encoder, attention, decoder

Image encoder pretrained Inception model ke baad ek Dense layer lagata hai — Inception ka output flatten karke Dense se pass karte hain aur ReLU lagate hain. Attention mechanism me do dense layers hoti hain — ek spatial component ke liye, matlab image me kahan focus karna hai, aur ek temporal component ke liye, matlab sequence me kis word par focus karna hai. In dono ko tanh se jodkar score nikalte hain, softmax se attention weights banate hain, aur features ko in weights se multiply karke context vector banate hain. Decoder har word ko embedding me badalta hai, usko context vector ke saath concatenate karta hai aur GRU cell me daalta hai. GRU ka output dense layers se hokar decoder output deta hai — jo logits hote hain, kyunki agla word vocabulary ke hazaron words me se ek hona hai. Loss function me padded words ko mask karna padta hai taaki woh loss me count na hon.

Training loop aur teacher forcing

Encoder aur decoder do alag models hain, isliye simple model.fit se kaam nahi chalta — caption ke words decoder ko ek-ek karke dene padte hain. Har training step me decoder ki state reset karte hain, input start token se shuru karte hain, phir har position par decoder ko chalakar loss calculate karte hain aur agla word input me daalte hain. Important baat yeh hai ki input me asli target word daala jata hai, model ka predicted word nahi — ise teacher forcing kehte hain. Saara kaam GradientTape me wrap karke gradients nikalte hain aur encoder aur decoder dono ke weights update karte hain. Yeh loop desired epochs tak chalate hain aur epoch-end loss ko plot karne ke liye store karte hain.

Prediction — greedy, beam search ya probabilistic

Prediction me image aur start token se shuru karte hain, decoder se logits lete hain aur agla word chunte hain — yeh tab tak repeat hota hai jab tak end token na mile ya maximum length poori na ho. Word chunne ke teen tareeke hain. Greedy approach me sabse zyada likelihood wala word chunte hain — fast hai lekin a aur the jaise uninformative words par zyada zor deta hai. Beam search me top teen ya paanch candidates rakhkar poori sequence ki probability optimize karte hain — best results deta hai lekin computationally mehenga hota hai aur latency badhata hai. Probabilistic tareeke me word ko uski likelihood ke proportion me randomly chunte hain — novelty aur speed ka achha trade-off hai, lekin reproducible nahi hota. Generated captions aksar sahi hoti hain — jaise baseball khelte logon ki photo par model ne sahi pehchana ki field par log baseball khel rahe hain — lekin kabhi-kabhi galti bhi karta hai, jaise white line ko sadak ka divider samajh lena. Stopwords ko training data se hataya gaya tha, isliye model proper sentences nahi banata — bada dataset hota to stopwords rakhkar proper sentences bhi generate ki ja sakti thi.

Yaad rakho: Captioning me image encoder, attention aur GRU decoder milkar kaam karte hain — training me teacher forcing use hoti hai, aur prediction me greedy fast hai, beam search best hai, aur probabilistic tareeka dono ke beech ka balance hai.

# Change these to control the accuracy/speed
VOCAB_SIZE = 1000 # use fewer words to speed up convergence
ATTN_UNITS = 32 # size of dense layer in Attention; larger more fine-grained
EPOCHS = 20 # train longer for greater accuracy
BATCH_SIZE = 64 # larger batch sizes lead to smoother convergence, but need more memory
EARLY_STOP_THRESH = 0.0001 # stop once loss improvement is less than this value
EMBED_DIM = 16 # embedding dimension for both images and words

# This is what Inception was trained with, so don't change unless you
# use a different pre-trained model. Inception takes (299, 299, 3) as
# input and provides (64, 2048) as output
IMG_HEIGHT = 299
IMG_WIDTH = 299
IMG_CHANNELS = 3
FEATURES_SHAPE = 2048
ATTN_FEATURES_SHAPE = 64

import matplotlib.pylab as plt
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds

GCS_DIR="gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/"

def filter_for_crowds(example):
    return (tf.math.count_nonzero(example['objects']['is_crowd']) > 0)

def get_image_label(example):
  captions = example['captions']['text'] # all the captions
  img_id = example['image/id']
  img = example['image']
  img = tf.image.resize(img, (IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)) # inception size
  img = tf.keras.applications.inception_v3.preprocess_input(img)
  return {
        'image_tensor': img,
        'image_id': img_id,
        'captions': captions
  }

trainds = tfds.load('coco_captions',
                    split='train',
                    shuffle_files=False,
                    data_dir=GCS_DIR)

# reduce number of images in one of these ways
trainds = trainds.filter(filter_for_crowds)
#trainds = trainds.take(10000)

trainds = trainds.map(get_image_label)

# get all the captions to feed into the Tokenizer
STOPWORDS = {'ourselves', 'hers', 'between', 'yourself', 'but', 'again', 'there', 'about', 'once', 'during', 'out', 'very', 'having', 'with', 'they', 'own', 'an', 'be', 'some', 'for', 'do', 'its', 'yours', 'such', 'into', 'of', 'most', 'itself', 'other', 'off', 'is', 's', 'am', 'or', 'who', 'as', 'from', 'him', 'each', 'the', 'themselves', 'until', 'below', 'are', 'we', 'these', 'your', 'his', 'through', 'don', 'nor', 'me', 'were', 'her', 'more', 'himself', 'this', 'down', 'should', 'our', 'their', 'while', 'above', 'both', 'up', 'to', 'ours', 'had', 'she', 'all', 'no', 'when', 'at', 'any', 'before', 'them', 'same', 'and', 'been', 'have', 'in', 'will', 'on', 'does', 'yourselves', 'then', 'that', 'because', 'what', 'over', 'why', 'so', 'can', 'did', 'not', 'now', 'under', 'he', 'you', 'herself', 'has', 'just', 'where', 'too', 'only', 'myself', 'which', 'those', 'i', 'after', 'few', 'whom', 't', 'being', 'if', 'theirs', 'my', 'against', 'a', 'by', 'doing', 'it', 'how', 'further', 'was', 'here', 'than'}
MAX_CAPTION_LEN = 1
def preprocess_caption(c):
    global MAX_CAPTION_LEN
    caption = "starttoken {} endtoken".format(c.decode('utf-8'))
    words = [word for word in caption.lower().split()
            if word not in STOPWORDS]
    MAX_CAPTION_LEN = max(MAX_CAPTION_LEN, len(words))
    return (' '.join(words))


train_captions = []
for data in trainds:
  str_captions = [preprocess_caption(c) for c in data['captions'].numpy()]
  train_captions.extend(str_captions)

# Choose the most frequent words from the vocabulary & remove punctuation etc.

    max_tokens=VOCAB_SIZE, output_sequence_length=MAX_CAPTION_LEN)
tokenizer.adapt(train_captions)
