def create_batched_ds(trainds, batchsize):
  # generator that does tokenization, padding on the caption strings
  # and yields img, caption
  def generate_image_captions():
    for data in trainds:
      captions = data['captions']
      img_tensor = data['image_tensor']
      str_captions = [preprocess_caption(c) for c in data['captions'].numpy()]
      padded = tokenizer(str_captions)
      for caption in padded:
        yield img_tensor, caption # repeat image
  
  return tf.data.Dataset.from_generator(
      generate_image_captions,
      (tf.float32, tf.int32)).batch(batchsize)

for img, caption in create_batched_ds(trainds, 193).take(2):
    print(img.shape, caption.shape)
    print(caption[0])

class ImageEncoder(tf.keras.Model):
   def __init__(self, embedding_dim):
     super(ImageEncoder, self).__init__()
     inception = tf.keras.applications.InceptionV3(
         include_top=False,
         weights='imagenet'
     )
     self.model = tf.keras.Model(inception.input,
                                 inception.layers[-1].output)
     self.fc = tf.keras.layers.Dense(embedding_dim)

   def call(self, x):
     x = self.model(x)
     x = tf.reshape(x, (x.shape[0], -1, x.shape[3]))
     x = self.fc(x)
     x = tf.nn.relu(x)
     return x

class BahdanauAttention(tf.keras.Model):
  def __init__(self, units):
    super(BahdanauAttention, self).__init__()
    self.W1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units)
    self.W2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(units)
    self.V = tf.keras.layers.Dense(1)

  def call(self, features, hidden):
    # features(CNN_encoder output) shape == (batch_size, 64, embedding_dim)
    # hidden shape == (batch_size, hidden_size)
    # hidden_with_time_axis shape == (batch_size, 1, hidden_size)
    hidden_with_time_axis = tf.expand_dims(hidden, 1)

    # attention_hidden_layer shape == (batch_size, 64, units)
    attention_hidden_layer = (tf.nn.tanh(self.W1(features) +
                                         self.W2(hidden_with_time_axis)))

    # score shape == (batch_size, 64, 1)
    # This gives you an unnormalized score for each image feature.
    score = self.V(attention_hidden_layer)

    # attention_weights shape == (batch_size, 64, 1)
    attention_weights = tf.nn.softmax(score, axis=1)

    # context_vector shape after sum == (batch_size, hidden_size)
    context_vector = attention_weights * features
    context_vector = tf.reduce_sum(context_vector, axis=1)

    return context_vector, attention_weights

class CaptionDecoder(tf.keras.Model):
  def __init__(self, embedding_dim, units, vocab_size):
    super(CaptionDecoder, self).__init__()
    self.units = units

    self.embedding = tf.keras.layers.Embedding(vocab_size, embedding_dim, input_length=MAX_CAPTION_LEN)
    
    self.gru = tf.keras.layers.GRU(self.units,
                                   return_sequences=True,
                                   return_state=True,
                                   recurrent_initializer='glorot_uniform')
    self.fc1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(self.units)
    self.fc2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(vocab_size)

    self.attention = BahdanauAttention(self.units)

  def call(self, x, features, hidden):
    # defining attention as a separate model
    context_vector, attention_weights = self.attention(features, hidden)

    # x shape after passing through embedding == (batch_size, 1, embedding_dim)
    x = self.embedding(x)

    # x shape after concatenation == (batch_size, 1, embedding_dim + hidden_size)
    x = tf.concat([tf.expand_dims(context_vector, 1), x], axis=-1)

    # passing the concatenated vector to the GRU
    output, state = self.gru(x)

    # shape == (batch_size, max_length, hidden_size)
    x = self.fc1(output)

    # x shape == (batch_size * max_length, hidden_size)
    x = tf.reshape(x, (-1, x.shape[2]))

    # output shape == (batch_size * max_length, vocab)
    x = self.fc2(x)

    return x, state, attention_weights

  def reset_state(self, batch_size):
    return tf.zeros((batch_size, self.units))

encoder = ImageEncoder(EMBED_DIM)
decoder = CaptionDecoder(EMBED_DIM, ATTN_UNITS, VOCAB_SIZE)

optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam()
loss_object = tf.keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy(
    from_logits=True, reduction='none')

def loss_function(real, pred):
  mask = tf.math.logical_not(tf.math.equal(real, 0))
  loss_ = loss_object(real, pred)

  mask = tf.cast(mask, dtype=loss_.dtype)
  loss_ *= mask

  return tf.reduce_mean(loss_)

loss_plot = []
@tf.function
def train_step(img_tensor, target):
  loss = 0

  # initializing the hidden state for each batch
  # because the captions are not related from image to image
  hidden = decoder.reset_state(batch_size=target.shape[0])

  # initialize the batch of predictions with [[3],[3], ...] i.e. with start tokens
  dec_input = tf.expand_dims([tokenizer(['starttoken'])[0][0]] * target.shape[0], 1)

  with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
      features = encoder(img_tensor)

      for i in range(1, target.shape[1]):
          # passing the features through the decoder
          predictions, hidden, _ = decoder(dec_input, features, hidden)

          loss += loss_function(target[:, i], predictions)

          # using teacher forcing
          dec_input = tf.expand_dims(target[:, i], 1)

  total_loss = (loss / int(target.shape[1]))

  trainable_variables = encoder.trainable_variables + decoder.trainable_variables

  gradients = tape.gradient(loss, trainable_variables)

  optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(gradients, trainable_variables))

  return loss, total_loss

checkpoint_path = "./checkpoints/train"
ckpt = tf.train.Checkpoint(encoder=encoder,
                           decoder=decoder,
                           optimizer = optimizer)
ckpt_manager = tf.train.CheckpointManager(ckpt, checkpoint_path, max_to_keep=5)

import time

batched_ds = create_batched_ds(trainds, BATCH_SIZE)

prev_loss = 999
for epoch in range(EPOCHS):
    start = time.time()
    total_loss = 0
    num_steps = 0

    for batch, (img_tensor, target) in enumerate(batched_ds):
      batch_loss, t_loss = train_step(img_tensor, target)
      total_loss += t_loss
      num_steps += 1

      if batch % 100 == 0:
        print ('Epoch {} Batch {} Loss {:.4f}'.format(
            epoch + 1, batch, batch_loss.numpy() / int(target.shape[1])))
    
    current_loss = total_loss / num_steps
    
    # storing the epoch end loss value to plot later
    loss_plot.append(current_loss)

    ckpt_manager.save()

    print ('Epoch {} Loss {:.6f} Time taken {:.1f} sec'.format(
        epoch + 1,
        current_loss,
        time.time() - start))
    
    # stop once it has converged
    improvement = prev_loss - current_loss
    if improvement < EARLY_STOP_THRESH:
        print("Stopping because improvement={} < {}".format(improvement, EARLY_STOP_THRESH))
        break
    prev_loss = current_loss

plt.plot(loss_plot);

for id in range(10):
    print(id, tokenizer.get_vocabulary()[id])

## Probabilistic prediction using the trained model
def plot_attention(image, result, attention_plot):
  fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))

  len_result = len(result)
  num_panels = len_result//2
  if num_panels*2 < len_result:
    num_panels += 1
  for l in range(len_result):
    temp_att = np.resize(attention_plot[l], (8, 8))
    ax = fig.add_subplot(len_result//2, num_panels, l+1)
    ax.set_title(result[l])
    img = ax.imshow(image)
    ax.imshow(temp_att, cmap='gray', alpha=0.6, extent=img.get_extent())
    ax.axis('off')

  plt.tight_layout()
  plt.show()

def predict_caption(filename):
  attention_plot = np.zeros((MAX_CAPTION_LEN, ATTN_FEATURES_SHAPE))
  hidden = decoder.reset_state(batch_size=1)
  img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(tf.io.read_file(filename), channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
  img = tf.image.resize(img, (IMG_HEIGHT, IMG_WIDTH)) # inception size
  img_tensor_val = tf.keras.applications.inception_v3.preprocess_input(img)

  features = encoder(tf.expand_dims(img_tensor_val, axis=0))
  dec_input = tf.expand_dims([tokenizer(['starttoken'])[0][0]], 1)
  result = []
  previous_word_ids = []
  for i in range(MAX_CAPTION_LEN):
    predictions, hidden, attention_weights = decoder(dec_input, features, hidden)
    attention_plot[i] = tf.reshape(attention_weights, (-1, )).numpy()

    if i < 10:
        # mask out <pad> <unk> <start> <end>, since we don't want <end>
        masked_predictions = predictions[0]
        mask = [0.0, 0, 0, 0] + [1.0] * (masked_predictions.shape[0] - 4)
        # end is okay after 5th word
        if i > 5:
            mask[3] = 1
        # avoid repeating words
        for p in previous_word_ids:
          mask[p] = 0
        mask = tf.convert_to_tensor(mask)
        masked_predictions *= mask
        # keep only the top 3 words, and draw out of log distribution
        top_probs, top_idxs = tf.math.top_k(input=masked_predictions, k=3, sorted=False)
        chosen_id = tf.random.categorical([top_probs], 1)[0].numpy()
        predicted_id = top_idxs.numpy()[chosen_id][0]
    else:
        # draws from log distribution given by predictions
        predicted_id = tf.random.categorical(predictions, 1)[0][0].numpy()
    result.append(tokenizer.get_vocabulary()[predicted_id])
    previous_word_ids.append(predicted_id)
    
    if tokenizer.get_vocabulary()[predicted_id] == 'endtoken':
      return img, result, attention_plot

    dec_input = tf.expand_dims([predicted_id], 0)
  
  attention_plot = attention_plot[:len(result), :]
  return img, result, attention_plot

filename="gs://practical-ml-vision-book-data/images/redhawks_game.jpg"
for i in range(5):
    image, caption, attention_plot = predict_caption(filename)
    print(' '.join(caption[:-1]))
img = tf.image.decode_jpeg(tf.io.read_file(filename), channels=IMG_CHANNELS)
plt.imshow(img);
plt.axis('off');

print(encoder.summary())

print(decoder.summary())

F1End Matter · Interview FAQs
Interview FAQs
Computer vision interviews (current era) ke liye — CNNs se lekar GANs tak, 36 sawaal-jawaab. Har jawaab isi book ke concepts par aadharit hai.
Q01 Machine learning aur expert system me kya farak hai?
Expert system me insaan ke logic ko haath se rules me likha jata hai, jaise phool ki pankhudiyan safed hon to ye guldaudi hai. Machine learning me computer ko bahut saare labelled examples dikhaye jate hain aur woh khud patterns seekh leta hai. Tasveeron jaise complex data ke liye machine learning behtar hai, kyunki wahan ke patterns ko rules me likhna lagbhag namumkin hai.
Q02 Supervised aur unsupervised learning me kya antar hai?
Supervised learning me har example ke saath sahi label diya jata hai, jaise tasveer ke saath phool ka naam, aur model nayi tasveer ki category predict karna seekhta hai. Unsupervised learning me labels nahi hote — model khud data me patterns ya groups dhoondhta hai. Is book ke zyada tar kaam, jaise classification aur detection, supervised learning hain.
Q03 CNN fully connected network se tasveeron par behtar kyun hai?
Fully connected layer har pixel ko independent treat karta hai aur har node ke liye lakhon weights chahiye hote hain. CNN me ek chhota filter poori tasveer par slide karta hai aur wahi weights har jagah use hote hain, is liye parameters bahut kam hote hain. Saath hi CNN pixels ki spatial hierarchy seekhta hai — pehle kinare, phir shapes, phir poori cheez — jo tasveeron ki asli structure hai.
Q04 Transfer learning kya hai aur ye kab use karni chahiye?
Transfer learning me pehle se bade dataset par trained model ke weights ko freeze kar ke sirf naye classifier layers train kiye jate hain. Ye tab use karni chahiye jab tumhara dataset chhota ho — har label ke liye paanch hazaar se kam images hon. Isse 5-Flowers dataset par accuracy 0.48 se badh kar 0.90 ho gayi thi, kyunki model ko lakhon parameters ke bajay sirf 20 hazaar train karne pade.
Q05 Transfer learning aur fine-tuning me kya farak hai?
Transfer learning me pretrained layers ko freeze kar diya jata hai aur sirf naye layers train hote hain. Fine-tuning me pretrained layers ko bhi thoda-thoda train karne diya jata hai, taaki woh naye dataset ke hisaab se adjust ho jayein. Fine-tuning me learning rate bahut kam rakhna padta hai, warna purana knowledge khatam ho jata hai — is liye warm-up schedule aur differential learning rate use hote hain.
Q06 Overfitting kya hai aur use kaise roka jata hai?
Overfitting tab hota hai jab model training data ko ratne lagta hai aur naye data par kharab perform karta hai — training accuracy badhti rehti hai lekin validation accuracy girne lagti hai. Ise rokne ke liye regularization (L1 ya L2 penalty), dropout, early stopping, aur zyada data ya data augmentation use hote hain. Batch normalization bhi training ko stable bana kar overfitting kam karne me madad karta hai.
Q07 ReLU activation function itni popular kyun hai?
ReLU simple hai — negative value ko zero kar deti hai aur positive ko waisa hi rehne deti hai. Iska gradient active hisse me constant rehta hai, is liye sigmoid ke muqable training bahut fast hoti hai. Sigmoid extremes par saturate ho jata hai aur gradient lagbhag zero ho jata hai, jisse training slow ho jati hai. ReLU ki ek kami dead ReLU hai, jise Leaky ReLU ya ELU se door kiya jata hai.
Q08 ResNet me skip connection kya problem solve karti hai?
Bahut gehre networks me gradient patla pad jata hai aur training ruk jati hai — ise vanishing gradient problem kehte hain. Skip connection input ko layer ke output me seedha jod deti hai, to gradient bina kam hue behta hai aur network ko sirf residual seekhna hota hai. Isi se 50 ya 100 layers wale networks train ho pate hain, aur ResNet aaj ke models ka benchmark ban gaya hai.
Q09 Global average pooling kya hai aur ye kab use nahi karna chahiye?
Global average pooling me aakhri feature map ke har channel ka average le kar seedha softmax lagaya jata hai — isme koi learnable weight nahi hota aur heavy fully connected head ki zaroorat khatam ho jati hai. Ye classification ke liye bahut achha hai, kyunki wahan location ki jaankari kaam ki nahi hoti. Lekin object detection jaise kaamon me jahan location important hai, wahan global average pooling use nahi karna chahiye.
Q10 Object detection aur image segmentation me kya farak hai?
Object detection me har object ke liye ek bounding box aur class milti hai — matlab object kahan hai, ye pata chalta hai. Instance segmentation me har object ki exact pixel-level shape milti hai, to do same type ke objects bhi alag dikhte hain. Semantic segmentation me tasveer ke har pixel ko ek category milti hai, lekin alag objects ko alag nahi kiya jata — saare log ek hi category hote hain.
Q11 YOLO aur RetinaNet me kya farak hai?
YOLO tasveer ko grid me tod kar aakhri feature map se seedha box predict karta hai — ye simple aur bahut fast hai, lekin location ki accuracy kam hoti hai aur ek cell me ek hi class predict ho pati hai. RetinaNet feature pyramid network, anchor boxes aur focal loss use karta hai — ye har scale par detection karta hai aur background imbalance ko handle karta hai, is liye zyada accurate hai lekin thoda slow hai.
Q12 Focal loss kya hai aur ye detection me kyun zaroori hai?
Ek tasveer me ek lakh se zyada anchor boxes hote hain lekin asal objects sirf kuch hote hain, to normal loss me background boxes ki chhoti losses mil kar asal detections ki loss ko daba deti hain. Focal loss easy background examples ki loss ko bahut kam kar deta hai, taaki model mushkil aur rare examples par dhyaan de sake. Yehi wajah hai ki RetinaNet jaise single-shot detectors train ho pate hain.
Q13 Manual labeling me folder structure aur metadata table me se kaunsa behtar hai aur kyun?
Metadata table behtar hai kyunki ek image ke kai labels ho sakte hain aur folder approach me duplication ho jaata hai. Folder approach tez hai, isliye best combination ye hai ki images ko folders me organize karo aur phir script se crawl karke metadata table bana lo.
Q14 Object detection aur segmentation ke liye labeling me kya extra chahiye hota hai?
Object detection me metadata me bounding box ke vertices chahiye hote hain, aur segmentation me bounding box ki jagah polygon chahiye hota hai. Doughnut jaise shape ke liye do polygons lagte hain, aur kabhi-kabhi boundary ko pixels ke set ke roop me bhi represent karte hain.
Q15 Voting system labeling me kaise madad karta hai?
Voting se human error aur ambiguous cases handle hote hain — ek image do raters ko dikhao, agree karein to label assign karo, disagree karein to image discard karo, neutral class me daalo, ya teesre labeler se majority vote lo. Multilabel me har category ko alag binary problem maan kar majority se decide karte hain.
Q16 Noisy Student approach kya hai aur ye kaise kaam karta hai?
Pehle thodi si images manually label karke ek chhota teacher model train karo, phir usse lakhon unlabeled images ke pseudo-labels predict karwao. Phir labeled aur pseudo-labeled data par dropout aur augmentation ke saath ek bada student model train karo, aur student ko naya teacher bana kar process repeat karo.
Q17 Selection bias, measurement bias aur confirmation bias me kya farak hai?
Selection bias tab hota hai jab training data production ke scenarios ka skewed subset ho, measurement bias tab hota hai jab training aur production me image collect karne ka tareeka alag ho, aur confirmation bias tab hota hai jab real world ki existing bias dataset me copy hokar amplify ho jaaye.
Q18 Dataset ko train, validation aur test me kaise split karna chahiye aur kyun?
Aam split 80:10:10 hota hai — training par weights tune hote hain, validation par hyperparameters optimize hote hain, aur test par final evaluation hoti hai. Split ek baar karo aur save karo, har run me dobara split mat karo, warna har experiment ka test set alag hoga.
Q19 TFRecords kya hain aur CSV se behtar kyun hain?
TFRecords ek efficient binary format hai jisme image, label, shape aur metadata ek hi record me store hote hain. Ye batch reading me tez hain, file pattern se padhe ja sakte hain, aur decode aur scaling pehle se karke training ko tez bana dete hain, jabki CSV alag-alag JPEG files par depend karta hai.
Q20 Training-serving skew kya hai aur isse kaise roka ja sakta hai?
Training-serving skew tab hota hai jab training aur inference me preprocessing alag ho jaaye, jisse model ke results galat ho jaate hain. Isse rokne ke liye preprocessing functions ko dono pipelines me reuse karo, preprocessing ko model ke andar daalo, ya tf.transform se transform artifact save karke serving me apply karo.
Q21 Data augmentation ki teen categories kya hain aur inka fayda kya hai?
Teen categories hain — spatial transformation jaise flip aur crop, color distortion jaise brightness aur contrast badalna, aur information dropping jaise Cutout aur Mixup. Inse dataset ka effective size badhta hai, overfitting kam hota hai aur model production ki variety ko behtar handle karta hai.
Q22 IoU aur mAP kya hain aur object detection me kaise use hote hain?
IoU predicted aur actual bounding box ke overlap ka area hai, unke union ke area se divide kiya hua — 1 matlab perfect overlap aur 0 matlab koi overlap nahi. IoU par threshold lagakar true aur false positives decide karte hain, precision-recall curve se average precision milti hai, aur saari classes ka mean lekar mAP milta hai.
Q23 TensorBoard se training ke dauraan kya-kya monitor kar sakte hain?
TensorBoard se loss aur accuracy curves, weight histograms, model graph aur device placement, training images aur confusion matrix monitor kar sakte hain. Weight distribution Gaussian jaisi honi chahiye — zero ki taraf skew dead layers aur bahut bade values overfitting ka sign hote hain.
Q24 Continuous evaluation kya hai aur iske main steps kya hain?
Continuous evaluation me deployed model ko bheje gaye data ka random sample save karke label karte hain, us par sliced metrics calculate karte hain, moving average plot karte hain, aur metric girne par alert bhej kar retrain karte hain. Isse prediction drift aur fairness issues jaldi pakde jaate hain.
Q25 TensorFlow Serving kya hai aur online prediction ke liye isko kyun use karte hain?
TensorFlow Serving ek web microservice hai jo trained SavedModel ko HTTP REST API ke roop me expose karta hai. Client JSON request bhejta hai aur JSON me prediction pa leta hai, bina TensorFlow install kiye ya tensor ke baare me jaane. Isse abstraction aur performance dono problems solve hoti hain, kyunki model powerful servers par accelerators ke saath chalta hai aur traffic ke hisaab se autoscale hota hai.
Q26 Serving signature kya hoti hai aur usko retrain kiye bina kaise badal sakte hain?
Serving signature woh function hoti hai jo model export karte time serving ke liye define ki jati hai — yeh batati hai ki input kya hoga aur output kya milega. Exported model ko load karke ek nayi function likhi ja sakti hai jo purani signature ko andar se call kare aur result me filename ya sequence number jaisi pass-through values jod de, phir model ko nayi signature ke saath dobara export kar dete hain. Ek model me multiple signatures bhi rakhi ja sakti hain, jinme se ek default hoti hai.
Q27 Batch aur stream prediction ke liye Apache Beam kyun use karte hain?
Batch prediction embarrassingly parallel hoti hai, lekin ek machine par bahut saare threads chalane se memory problem aati hai kyunki har thread ko model ki copy chahiye. Apache Beam kaam ko bahut saari machines par distribute karta hai, har worker par model ek baar shared handle se load hota hai, aur filenames ko batch karke TensorFlow operations fast ho jate hain. Wahi Beam code batch aur streaming dono ke liye kaam karta hai aur Dataflow par autoscale hota hai.
Q28 TensorFlow Lite kya hai aur edge devices par model ko efficient kaise banate hain?
TensorFlow Lite ek framework hai jo trained TensorFlow model ko edge devices par inference ke liye convert karta hai — isse train nahi kar sakte. Efficiency ke liye MobileNet jaisa edge-optimized model use karte hain aur weights ko float32 se int8 me quantize karte hain, jisse memory ek-chauthai ho jati hai aur integer arithmetic bahut fast hoti hai, accuracy me sirf 0.2 se 0.5% ka nuksan hota hai. Device par TensorFlow Lite interpreter chalakar prediction li jati hai.
Q29 Federated learning kya hai aur yeh privacy me kaise madad karta hai?
Federated learning me har device apna training data apne paas rakhkar sirf gradient update share karta hai, original image ya data nahi. Bahut saare devices ke gradients ko average karke shared model update hota hai, aur har device usko apne interactions se fine-tune bhi kar sakta hai. Isse privacy-sensitive use cases me bhi model improve hota hai bina data ke device se bahar gaye. Differential privacy jodne se protection aur strong ho jati hai.
Q30 Kubeflow Pipelines kya hai aur ML pipeline ki zaroorat kyun padti hai?
Kubeflow Pipelines ek framework hai jo dataset banana, training aur deployment jaise steps ko ek automated pipeline me jodta hai aur Kubernetes par chalata hai. Iski zaroorat isliye padti hai kyunki naya data aata rehta hai, data drift se performance girti hai aur naye experiments hote rehte hain — yeh sab manual karna possible nahi hota. Har step ek containerized component hota hai, ek step ka output doosre ka input banta hai, aur run schedule ya nayi files aane par trigger ho sakta hai.
Q31 Explainability kya hai aur LIME, Integrated Gradients aur xRAI me kya farq hai?
Explainability batati hai ki model ne kis basis par prediction di — yeh trust, debugging aur bias pakadne ke liye zaroori hai. LIME image ke patches ko hatakar dekhta hai ki kaunse patches prediction ke liye sabse important hain. Integrated Gradients baseline se actual image tak har pixel ka gradient integrate karke pixel-wise attribution deta hai, jo X-ray jaisi low-contrast images par behtar hai. xRAI dono ko combine karke region-based attribution deta hai, jo natural images par zyada precise hota hai.
Q32 No-code computer vision tools ko project ke pehle step ke roop me kyun use karna chahiye?
No-code tools bina code likhe viability check, data quality check aur benchmark teeno dete hain. Agar achievable accuracy acceptable se bahut door hai to futile project par time waste nahi hota, confusion matrix se pata chalta hai ki kaisa aur data chahiye, aur mili hui accuracy apne models ko compare karne ka baseline ban jati hai. Flowers dataset par no-code tool ne lagbhag 3 dollar me 96.4% accuracy di, jo bahut tuning ke baad bane models ke barabar thi.
Q33 Object counting me density estimation detection se behtar kyun hoti hai?
Overlapping aur chhote objects ko detect karke ginne par boxes miss ya combine ho jate hain, aur segmentation scale-invariant nahi hoti. Density estimation me image ko patches me todkar har patch me object centers ki ginti estimate karna sikhate hain, phir saari densities ko sum karke total count milta hai. Yeh location ki information bhi bachata hai aur bheed, cells ya berries jaise crowded scenes me behtar kaam karta hai. Simulated images se bhi isko train kiya ja sakta hai.
Q34 Pose estimation me PoseNet joints ke saath offsets aur voting kyun use karta hai?
Sirf joints detect karne se kaam nahi chalta kyunki model kuch joints miss kar sakta hai ya galat joints detect kar sakta hai. Har detected joint ke saath paas ke joints ki offset location bhi predict hoti hai, jaise wrist se elbow ki location, to ek joint ke liye multiple candidate locations mil jati hain. Phir Hough transform jaisi weighted voting se final location decide hoti hai, jisse pose robust banti hai. Multiple logon ke liye segmentation mask se pixels ko alag-alag persons ko assign kiya jata hai.
Q35 GAN kya hai aur mode collapse kya hota hai?
GAN me do networks hote hain — generator fake images banata hai aur discriminator real aur fake me farq pehchanata hai. Dono baari-baari train hokar ek-doosre ko behtar banate hain, jab tak discriminator sirf random guess na karne lage. Mode collapse ek failure mode hai jisme generator ko ek aisa output mil jata hai jo discriminator ko hara deta hai aur woh baar-baar wahi kuch outputs banane lagta hai, diversity kho deta hai. DCGAN me convolutional layers use karke aur label smoothing jaise tricks se isko kam kiya jata hai.
Q36 VAE aur normal autoencoder me kya farq hai, aur image captioning me attention ka kya role hai?
Normal autoencoder latent vector output karta hai aur sirf reconstruction seekhta hai, isliye uska latent space unorganized hota hai aur random point se meaningless image ban sakti hai. VAE encoder se distribution ke parameters — mean aur variance — output karwata hai aur KL divergence loss se usko standard normal ke paas rakhta hai, jisse latent space smooth ho jata hai aur generation possible hoti hai. Image captioning me attention mechanism decoder ko batata hai ki har word predict karte time image ke kis hisse par focus karna hai, jaise frisbee word ke liye frisbee wale region par.
